en: Oṃ, homage! Homage to the glorious Guru!
[Then follows the worship of the maṇḍala according to the sequence of Śrī Siddhilakṣmī.]
He cleanses it for the sake of the dwelling; he spreads out the sacrificial grass on the ground for the purpose of providing a seat and a place of rest.
The ritual sipping of water (ācamana) is performed with the threefold truth (tritatva).
KH PHREṂ HRĀṂ SVĀHĀ to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). KH PHRAṂ HRĪṂ SVĀHĀ to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva).
KHPHREṂ HRŪṂ SVĀHĀ to the principle of Śiva.
A prostration to the Guru on the bare ground.
Salutation to that venerable Guru who has revealed that state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is indeed the entire universe—salutations to that illustrious Guru.
Aiṁ, salutations to the supreme gurus. Aiṁ, salutations to the pre-eminent gurus.
Aiṃ! Homage to the supreme teachers and gurus.
Having spread out a layer of grass on the ground, he sat down.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving have been pervaded.
Aiṁ! The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, and the Guru is the god Maheśvara;
the Guru is the god who is the entire universe—to that Śrī Guru, obeisance.
Aiṃ, salutations to the supreme gurus. Aiṃ, salutations to the pre-eminent gurus.
Aiṃ! Salutation to the supreme teachers, the gurus.
Salutation to the lotus-seat at Balisa. Salutation to the tortoise-seat at Thavaka.
On the side, the scattering of unbroken grains.
KH PHREṂ! O crusher of all enemies, abode of infinite power! To the weapon (astra), PHAṬ! [I offer] the sandals.
The face is veiled with the vajra-mudrā.
KHPHREṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ VAJRAPAÑJARE SVĀHĀ ||
Touching at the ten openings.
KHPHREṂ CALAMAKULE KULAMACALE HRĪṂ HRŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ ||
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
KHPHREṂ! O crusher of all enemies, abode of infinite power, to the weapon (astra), PHAṬ!
The purification of the hands.
KH PHREṂ | To Paramahaṃsinī, the abode of the power of omniscience, salutation to both thumbs.
KH PHREṂ! Homage to the one who bestows the path to nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of satisfaction, with the two index fingers.
Khphreṁ! Salutation to the one who pacifies adverse calamities, the abode of the power of primordial awakening, through the two middle fingers.
KH PHREṂ! To the one who shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions, the abode of independent power—to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*.

Khphreṃ, salutation to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhā) for the one who is the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities, the abode of unimpaired power; Khphreṃ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands (karatalapṛṣṭha) for the weapon (astra), the subduer of all enemies, the abode of infinite power.
The ritual placement on the limbs (karanyāsa).
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Yoginīs of Accomplishment! The sandal of the Lord of the Eastern Face! Pādukāṃ!
Khphreṁ! Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment; the sandals of the Lord of the Southern Face.
Khphreṃ! Homage to Nityoditānandananditā, the Mistress of the Northern Face; [I worship] the sandals!
KH PHREṂ! To the Mistress of the entire wheel of families, the Lord of the western face, [I offer] the sandals.
Khphreṃ! To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī and to the Lord of the upward-facing [face], the sandals!
The ritual placement on the face.
Khphreṃ! Homage to the heart, O Supreme Swan-like Goddess, the abode of the power of omniscience.
Khphreṃ! To the giver of the path to nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of satisfaction, svāhā to the head!
KH PHREṂ! O pacifier of adverse calamities, to the crest-lock (śikhā) which is the abode of the power of primordial awakening, VAUṢAṬ!
KHPHREṂ! To the armor, the abode of the independent power that shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions—HŪṂ!
KH PHREṂ! To the three eyes, which are the boat for crossing over all calamities and whose abode is unimpaired power, VAUṢAṬ!
KHPHREṂ! O crusher of all enemies, abode of infinite power, PHAṬ to the weapon-mantra!
Thus ends the ritual assignment of the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The worship of the water vessel.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals for the water vessel (jalapātra). Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, the sandals for the venerable lord of the water vessel (jalapātrabhaṭṭāraka).
The six-limbed [practice].
Khphreṃ, homage to the heart. Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head. Khphreṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Khphreṃ, for the armor, hūṃ! Khphreṃ, for the three eyes, vauṣaṭ! Khphreṃ, for the weapon, phaṭ!
Performing the invocation and other rites, one should display the *dhenumudrā*.
The Gāyatrī.
Khphreṃ! We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon her who is ninety [years] plus one; may that Lakṣmī inspire us.
The consecration.
The worship of the argha vessel.
Aiṃ Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals for the seat of the argha vessel.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava!
KHPHREṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ ŚVĀṂ SAḤ SAḤ SAḤ PARĀDEVI AMṚTAṂ VAMA SVĀHĀ ||
The purification of substances.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
The six-limbed [practice].
Khphreṃ, homage to the heart! Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head! Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock!
Khphreṃ, for the armor, hūṃ. Khphreṃ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Khphreṃ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers: obeisance!
One should display the yonimudrā.
The purification of the elements is performed by means of the tortoise mudrā.
aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hsauḥ hsauḥ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
Self-worship.
Khphreṃ, for myself, sandalwood and the *pādukā*. Khphreṃ, unbroken rice and the *pādukā*.
Khphreṃ, the sandals of Vīrabhasma! Khphreṃ, the sandals that enchant all people!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, salutations to the Self; [I offer] flowers and sandals.
KHPHREṂ! O you who crush all enemies, PHAṬ to the weapon!
With this mantra, one should sprinkle [water] upon one's own head.
From the heart: for the invocation.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! May that Goddess Parāparā, who resides in space and whose nature is space, who has gone to the world of the gods and is gentle, come here to this maṇḍala.
I shall summon this; I summon.
Threefold añjali gesture. Navātman.
Aiṁ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ! To the Lord of Viras, Bhairavānanda, who is the Power of Bliss (Ānandaśakti), ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ! To the venerable Navātman, the Lord of the Guru-maṇḍala, [I offer] the sandals.
Karma.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the sovereign hero Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, śkṣmlvryīṃ, to the venerable mistress of the twenty-eight rites, [I offer] the sandals.
The Root Abode.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, [I offer] the sandals to the venerable Paścima Mūlasthāna Bhaṭṭārikā, the sovereign of the heroes, the blissful Bhairava-Ānanda, [invoked by] Śkṣmlvryīṃ.
Tumbuleśvarī.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hdrkṣmlvryūṃ Sdrkṣmlvryīṃ, the sandals of the Goddess Śrī Jayatuṃbureśvarī.
The topknot.
Aiṃ Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ, the sandals to the venerable Śikhā-Svacchanda-Mahābhairava.
O Great Form!
Aiṃ Hūṃ! To Mahākāla Mahābhairava, the subduer of all enemies, [I offer] the sandals.
Ugracaṇḍā.
Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hsphreṃ ugracaṇḍaripumardanī hūṃ phreṃ, always protect you and me, juṃ saḥ, O Mṛtyuharā, the sandal!
O Ugracaṇḍī!
Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hskhphreṃ ugracaṇḍi ripumardanī hūṃ phreṃ! Always protect you and me, juṃ saḥ! O remover of death, [grant] the sandals!
The Goddess of Accomplishment (Siddhilakṣmī).
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
Kāli!
Oṃ phreṃ siddhikalāli hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ.
Tripura.

Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ Klvrhrhmkhlhrklhrīṃ. In the Brahma-cakra, at the great seat (pīṭha) of Oḍiyāna, O Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, whose nature is the Lord of the Carya-seat and the power of the Supreme Brahman, [I worship] Your sandals with this mantra.
Thus is the worship.
Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers: salutation!
One should display the yonimudrā.
For the sake of the worship of the abode of craving.
Oṃ, homage to Gaṅgā. Oṃ, homage to Yamunā. Oṃ, homage to Narmadā.
Oṃ, salutation to Kāverī. Oṃ, salutation to Kauśikī. Oṃ, salutation to Gaṇḍakī.
Oṃ, salutation to Sarasvatī. Oṃ, salutation to the full water-pot.

Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To the Great Army of the Kula-tree, O Enchanter, to all the holy fords, to the deity of the mantra, to the Kalās and the Tattvas, to the Lord of the Tattvas, to the essence of Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra, to the Tattva of Ātman-Vidyā-Śiva, Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ! [I offer] the sandals to the form of the complete water-pot.
Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers: homage!
One should display the dhenumudrā.
Bathing with the water of the sacred tradition, the Vedic utterances, and the physical body; [the offering of] water.
The syllable *ū* is the seed-syllable of Vāyu; above that is Varuṇa, and above that is Vajrapāṇi.
Above that is Kāla, joined with the final letter of the alphabet; above that is the supreme seed-syllable of Fire (*raṃ*), together with *haṃsa*.
It is marked by the lunar drop at its end, possesses the strength of a white lotus, and flows with streams of milk.
But seeing a false witness, one constantly burns their entire family; for such sin is indeed equal to Mount Meru.
Duduya.
By the command of Śiva, I constantly bathe you— the source of milk among milks, the most pure upon the earth, and the eternal wish-fulfilling cow— with milk.
They were maintained.
I bathe the Lord Umāpati, the beloved of the gods, with curd;
may the deities always be well-pleased.
The enclosure.
Śiva, the progenitor of the three worlds, who wields the Pināka bow purified by clarified butter and whose Liṅga is purified by the Pināka, exists in the form of fire and serpents.
The yellow robe.
O beloved of the gods, that which is produced by the power of Gomukhī is dear to you;
by means of this bath, situated upon the wish-fulfilling tree, one's desires are attained.
With the *sāsarī* [mudrā].
This sugar-candy is exceedingly delicious and likewise cooling to the mind;
the Goddess, who bestows unbroken boons, has been bathed with sugar-candy moon-shaped sweets.
Likewise, with the five products of the cow and so forth, the five Brahmans and so forth as the perfuming agents,
and combined with the five substances, I bathe [the deity] with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
Some carry a staff with a skull at its top.
Aiṃ! Within the circle of the venerable Saṃvarta-maṇḍala, the power of bliss is established in the stages of the Krama.
Subhīmā has emitted the fourfold group of principles (nyāya), which resides in both the Akula and Kula; then another fivefold group and a sixfold group.
Furthermore, there are four, another five, and again four; this is the reality of the maṇḍala.
Bow down to that excellent Bhairava, Śrī Kujeśa, by whom [all things] were emitted.
For the purpose of shaving the hair on the ground at a sacred site.
The syllable *ū* is the seed-syllable of Vāyu; above that is Varuṇa with the thunderbolt in his hand;

above that is Kāla joined with the final letter of the alphabet; above that is the supreme seed-syllable of Fire, together with *haṃsa*, the lunar drop, and the end of dissolution—a supreme white lotus from which streams of milk flow.
But seeing a fraudulent act, one always burns away family impurity; for such sin is indeed equal to Mount Meru.
Bathing the eyebrows || ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ || Consciousness ||
May this divine sandalwood from Śrīkhaṇḍa, rich in fragrance and most enchanting,
adorned upon the forehead, be accepted.
Anointed with sandalwood paste, it is meritorious, pure, and a destroyer of sins; it constantly wards off calamities and bestows fortune, sovereignty, and happiness.
Sindūra (vermilion)
Vīreśvarī is the great heroine, adorned with ashes;
she is the goddess who attracts the three worlds, most excellent and crimson with vermilion.
Or else.
O Mother of the World, accept this cotton garment, the supreme purifier that bestows happiness and prosperity; salutations to you.
View.
May this vision-granting [teaching], which reveals the fourteen worlds— Heaven, Mortal Realm, and the single Pātāla— be accepted for the sake of attaining the fruit of the divine eye.
The Ear-flag.
O Supreme Goddess, accept this beautiful four-cornered banner known as Karṇa, which possesses the luster of pure vermilion.
The five banners.
O Goddess, accept this pair of earrings, this five-colored banner,
and this supreme flag for the sake of attaining the fruit of the five siddhis.
Unbroken.
Grant me my desired boon— unbroken and inexhaustible, fulfilling desires for dharma,
pleasure, and wealth— and bestow upon me the supreme goal in the world beyond.
The performers of sacrifice.
The sacred thread is the supreme purifier, which Prajāpati produced together with the body;
may this life-prolonging, foremost, auspicious, and brilliant sacred thread be a source of strength and splendor for you.
In Caṃphumāḍha.
O Goddess of gods, this divine wish-fulfilling jewel parasol shines like the full moon; by its being offered, grant me the fruit of my heart's desire.
Svāna.
O auspicious lady, this supreme ritual of offering flowers is rich with the fragrance of various blossoms, including the blooming of jasmine, and bestows the attainment of good fortune.
With a golden-colored sacrificial ground.
To him who possesses for the sake of victory a lineage that holds the reflection of the Self— a mirror bright as the full moon that destroys the pride of enemies.
First, the bath for the patron (*yajamāna*) for the purpose of beautification; [and] the splendor of the reciter (*vācaka*).
[Thus ends the procedure for bathing in the shadow.]
Now follows the worship of the sacrificial ground (thaṇḍila).
One should sip water with the *tritatva* mantra.
Khphreṃ Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Khphreṃ Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva).
KHPHREṂ HRŪṂ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva! KHPHREṂ HRĀṂ HRĪṂ HRŪṂ, svāhā to the principle of all things!
The offering to the Sun (sūryārgha). The formula beginning with "Today and so forth" (adyādi). The statement (vākya).
Having extracted the seed-syllable ending with the letter *va*, one should place *Śiva* (the letter *ha*) upon it;
at the beginning, middle, and end, it is adorned with the three fires (*ra*).
Having illuminated it with the Varman mantra, one should extract this [mantra] with the Sāvitrī;
this is the most excellent and supreme peak-mantra, Mahāmārtaṇḍabhairava.
Argha, obeisance! Flower, obeisance!
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ hrīṃ saḥ, salutation to the illustrious Kulamārtaṇḍa Mahābhairava, accompanied by the Power of Radiance (prakāśa-śakti).
Rhrkṣrū-īṃ, salutation to the illustrious Mahāmārtaṇḍabhairava.
Homage to the Guru.
Salutation to that venerable Guru who has revealed that state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the god Maheśvara;
the Guru is indeed the entire universe—to that venerable Guru, I offer salutations.
Aiṃ. Salutations to the supreme gurus.
Aiṃ, salutations to the supreme preceptors. Aiṃ, salutations to the supreme teachers.
To the lotus-seat at the back, the sandals; to the tortoise-seat at the front, the sandals;
on the sides, the scattering of unbroken rice grains.

KH PHREṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ VAJRAPAÑJALE SVĀHĀ ||

The ritual placement (nyāsa).
KH PHREṂ! O crusher of all enemies, to the abode of infinite power, to the weapon-mantra, PHAṬ!
The purification of the flask.
Khphreṃ! To Paramahaṃsinī, the abode of the power of omniscience, homage to both thumbs!
KH PHREṂ! Salutation to the two index fingers, the abode of the power of satisfaction, who bestows the path to nirvāṇa.
KH PHREṂ! To the pacifier of calamities and misfortunes, the abode of the power of primordial awakening, salutation to the two middle fingers.
KH PHREṂ! To the one who shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions, the abode of independent power—to the two ring fingers, homage!
KH PHREṂ! To the one who is the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities, the abode of unimpaired power—to you, salutation with the two little fingers.
KH PHREṂ SAKALAŚATRUPRAMATHANI ANANTAŚAKTIDHĀMNE ASTRĀYA KARATALAPṚṢṬHĀBHYĀṂ NAMAḤ. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa).
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Yoginīs of Accomplishment! The sandal of the Lord of the Eastern Face! Pādukāṃ!
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment; the sandals of the Lord of the Southern Face.
Khphreṃ! Homage to Nityoditānandananditā, the Mistress of the Northern Face; [I worship] your sandals.
KH PHREṂ! To the Mistress of the entire family wheel, the Lord of the western face, [I offer] the sandals.
Khphreṁ! To the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī and to the Lord of the Upward-Facing Mouth, [I offer] the sandals.
Thus ends the placement on the mouth (*vaktranyāsa*).
Khphreṁ! To the abode of the power of omniscience, O Supreme Swan-like Goddess, salutation to the heart.
KH PHREṂ! To the one who bestows the path to nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of contentment, svāhā to the head!
KH PHREṂ! To the crest-lock (śikhā), the pacifier of calamities and misfortunes, the abode of the power of primordial awakening—Vauṣaṭ!
KHPHREṂ! To the one who shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions, the abode of independent power; for the armor, HŪṂ!
KHPHREṂ! To the three eyes, which are the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities and the abode of unimpeded power, VAṢAṬ!
KH PHREṂ! O you who crush all enemies, to the abode of the power of water, to the weapon, PHAṬ!
Thus ends the ritual assignment of the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
Taṃ at the center of the eyebrows; Dyaṃ at the heart; Thāṃ at the navel; Oṃ at the mouth.
Hrīṃ at the left nostril; Hūṃ at the right nostril.
HĀṂ at the left eye; PHREṂ at the right eye; KṢOṂ at the left ear; KROṂ at the right ear.
Na on the *liṅga*; Maḥ on the anus. Thus is the Nyāsa of the nine gates.
The worship of the water vessel.
Khphreṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, the sandals for the seat of the water vessel.

The six-limbed [practice].
Khphreṃ, homage to the heart. Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head. Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.

Perform the invocation and other rites; then, display the dhenumudrā.
The Gāyatrī.
Khphreṃ! We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon her ninety-one [forms]; may that Lakṣmī inspire us.
The consecration.
The worship of the argha vessel.
Aiṃ Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals for the vessel of the offering water (arghapātra).
KH PHREṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, VAUṢAṬ to Ānandabhairava.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Śvāṁ Saḥ Saḥ Saḥ, O Supreme Goddess, vomit forth nectar, Svāhā!
The purification of the substances: three handfuls.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.

[Perform] invocation, installation, [and offer] sandalwood, unbroken rice, and flowers; [utter] "Namaḥ. One should display the Yoni-mudrā.
