aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hsauṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
Self-worship.
Khphreṃ, for myself, sandalwood, pādukā. Khphreṃ, unbroken rice, pādukā.
Khphreṃ, the sandals of Vīrabhasma! Khphreṃ, the sandals that enchant all people!
Khphreṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Namaḥ. To the Self, flowers and sandals.
*Khphreṃ sakalaśatrupramathani astrāya phaṭ*. With this mantra, one should sprinkle [water] upon the crown of one's own head.
One should recite the Mālinī [mantra].
Oṃ, salutations to Caṇḍikā! The illustrious Bhairava said:
Aiṃ! Be victorious, O Goddess Mālinī, stainless one, destroyer of impurity!
You are the Goddess who is the source of the power of knowledge; you are the intellect that increases splendor.
The mother of all beings is established in this saṃsāra;
O Goddess Vīrāvalī, O affectionate one, show compassion!
Victorious is You, the supreme power of primordial wisdom (*parājñānaśakti*), born from the manifestation of the ultimate reality of Nirvāṇa, consisting of light, and having emerged in manifest form;

You are auspicious through Your powers of will (*icchā*) and action (*kriyā*). You are the straight line, the beautiful stroke, and again, in the form of a coil like a sleeping serpent king; You are praised as the Lord, the power of resonance (*nādaśakti*).

You are the light-form of the Asuras, the essential nature, named the Eldest of Śiva, as well as Vāmā, Raudrī, and Ambikā who is called Manonmanī; you are the form of the Bindu, the form of Vadhūtī, and the shape of the half-moon; you are the triangle, the letter *a*, the letter *u*, and the letter *m* joined into a single unity at the beginning, and you are that very essence.
Abiding in the form of the *bhaga*, originating from the reality of primordial patience (*kṣānti*), having the form of the womb (*yoni*),
the awakener of Śrīkaṇṭha, the mother of Rudra, likewise possessing infinite power, extremely subtle, the consort of the three forms, and the one who receives the offering (*argha*).
O Bhārabhūti, you who are of the nature of Tithīśa, you who are like a pillar (Sthāṇubhūtā), and Harākṣā;
O Jhaṇṭhīśa, Bhautīśa, and Sadyojātātmikā, you are worshipped for the sake of grace; O Krūra, Sāṅga, Mahāsena, and Saṃbhoginī!

She who reaches the end of the sixteen vowels, who gathers the drops of nectar, who is immersed in the body of vibration; she who bestows the bliss of supreme liberation and the complete joy of the Residue; the Bhairavī whose power is play in the garden of Bhairava;
the supreme slayer, the power of Rudra, the mistress of yoga and the mother of accomplishments; the all-pervasive one, the mass of sounds, the ocean of the source-syllables.

Pure in speech, auspicious, the Mistress of Accomplished Speech, Mātṛkā, Siddhi, Icchā, Kriyā, Maṅgalā, Siddhilakṣmī, Vibhūti, Saṃbhūti, Gati, she who is called Śāśvatī, Nārāyaṇī, Raktacaṇḍā, Karālā, Kṣaṇā, Bhīmarūpā, Mahocchuṣmā— O Yoginī, you are my beloved.
Victorious, unconquered, and the deluder of Rudra, you are seated upon the lap of the god known as Navātman; O Goddess,
you are worshipped by practitioners of the path of mantra who follow the way of spells, who are devoted to the drinking of heroes (vīrapāna), and who are deeply faithful—
with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and festivals of divine drink— O wearer of skulls, skeletons, and the *kapāla* vessel.

O beloved fond of wine and meat, you perform penance with those auspicious yet trivial Śaiva mantras and vidyās produced through one birth, two births, three births, or four, five, six, or seven births.
There were those who shone with their vows—shaven-headed ascetics, skeletons, and *kāpālikas* who had ascended to divine conduct;
they uttered these mantra-syllables: *namaḥ*, *oṃ*, *svāhā*, *svadhā*, *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭ*, *hūṃ*, and *phaṭ*, holding [skulls] in their left hands.

O Yoginī, you who bestow the perfection of yoga, you are worshipped by practitioners who chant the rosaries of protective mantras, by their spiritual sons, by the Mothers, by those initiated into the maṇḍalas, by yogis, and by assemblies of yoginīs; you, who delight in the play of Rudra, look upon us with eyes like lotus petals, filled with affection.

For him, there exists unimpeded accomplishment (siddhi) that abides in the divine realm, the atmosphere, and the seven netherworlds, as well as among those who move through the sky. A pure person, with water [offered] out of devotion, should recite this Daṇḍaka once, twice, thrice, four, five, six, seven, or eight times at one, two, or three sessions of the day.

O Goddess, O beloved of Mahālakṣmī, whatever man constantly remembers [you], he is protected even from thieves, fire, weapons, the ocean, or the mountain peak— due to your affection for your son— even if he be a thief of gold,
an adulterer, or a slayer of a Brahmin.
O Goddess, those defiled by the great sin of killing a cow are liberated upon remembering your face,
which resembles the full moon and has cheeks adorned with shimmering divine rubies and excellent earrings;
even those whose arms, thighs, feet, and toes are bound with firm bonds or serpent-nooses are set free.

O Goddess Mahākālī, whose splendor is like the fire of cosmic destruction, by the chanting of Your name they are released from terrible and great diseases; O You who possess the radiance of the filaments of the lotus— the lotus being the bees that are the crowns of Skanda, Brahmā, Indra, Candra, and Ārka, and the flower-weaponed Kāmadeva— by meditating upon Your two lotus feet.
O Mother of all heroes, O Bhairavī; O Bhairava, I have come for refuge to you. Forgive my offense, forgive my offense, O Śivā!
Thus praised by the high-souled Bhairava, the Great Goddess,
the Supreme Sovereign, then emerged after bursting through the *liṅga*.
[Thus ends the Mālinīdaṇḍaka Stotra.]
Then, having given the fivefold offering.
The pair [of deities] in the forest of the *thaṇḍila* [sacrificial ground], possessing the power of the offering of the well-recited [mantras].
Aiṃ, the sandals for the peacock’s blood.
Meditative absorption.
Resembling the flower of the hibiscus, adorned with red garments,
seated upon a peacock throne, and wearing a sacred thread made of darbha grass.
The three-eyed one with tawny hair standing upright, as well as Vāsipheta,
Vainaka, Kālahasta, and likewise the trident and the khaṭvāṅga staff.
I worship the Lord who holds the vessel of the bindu, the youth clad in a kṣatriya’s garland.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Aiṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals of Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha; [this is] the offering.
Aiṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ! O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, with your mass of tawny matted hair, three eyes, and flaming mouth, descend!
Come, come, O Blessed One, into the center of the maṇḍala! Accept the offering as it has been presented;
grant me my desired goal! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Oṃ! May Vaṭuka, who grants all accomplishments, be satisfied by this offering of bali;
may he, who is served by spirits and children, always grant me peace and prosperity.
This belongs to all the Vaṭukas.
Aiṃ, the sandals for Narāsana.
meditative absorption (dhyāna)
Mounted upon a great preta, endowed with a pale-red (pāṭala) complexion,
holding a sword and a shield in his hands, as well as a bowl and a khaṭvāṅga staff.

Salutations to you, the protector of the field (kṣetrapālaka), the Great God of terrible form, who wears a garland of severed heads, who blazes with formidable fangs, whose hair stands erect, and whose eyebrows and eyes are tawny.
Homage to the Flower of Dhyāna.
Aiṃ Thhmrauṃ. To the goddess Dambhakī of Prastaradvīpa and the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa, [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṃ! O Lord of this very place, by whatever name you are known, descend into the center of the maṇḍala!
Descend, O four-armed, three-eyed one, and so forth, who holds a khaṭvāṅga, a pheṭaka, and a trident in your hands;
you who are adorned with a garland of great skulls and possess a radiance equal to ten million flashes of lightning! Come, come, O Blessed One!
In the form of Bhairava, accept the offering as it has been presented; ward off my obstacles! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣuṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ! O Guardian of the Site and Field (Sthānakṣetrapāla), accept this bali offering together with incense and lamps; svāhā!
In this [place], may the Kṣetrapāla who dwells among the Kṣatriyas,
being pleased by this offering of bali, grant me protection from all [harm].
Of all these fields.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the lion-throne.
meditative absorption (dhyāna)

She possessed the luster of molten gold, could assume any form at will, was in the prime of youth, had the appearance of one intoxicated with passion, yet was skeletal, adorned with every kind of ornament.
Adorned with a linga-noose, a skull, a goad, and a water-pot,
and seated upon a corpse, she grants the fulfillment of all desires and aims.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Aiṃ Yāṃ, the sandal-paste for the Yoginīs; the offering.

Whosoever among the Yoginīs are born of the *pīṭhas*, born of the *kṣetras*, innate (*sahaja*), born of yoga (*yogaja*), born of the womb (*garbhaja*), or born of the *kula*; whosoever among the Yoginīs are the sky-farers (*khecarī*), earth-farers (*bhūcarī*), cow-path-farers (*gocarī*), or those consisting of one syllable, two syllables, three syllables, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine syllables, who traverse the three worlds; [all these belong to me].
Accept the offering of those who have arrived as they are; grant me success! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ! Whether from the upper reaches of the cosmic egg, or in heaven, in the expanse of the sky, on the partless ground, or in the netherworld, in fire, or in water and air—wherever you may be situated;
whether you have set foot in the sacred fields (kṣetra), seats (pīṭha), and secondary seats (upapīṭha) throughout the directions, [I worship you] with incense, lamps, and other offerings.
May the goddesses, who are always pleased with us and are worthy of worship by the lords of heroes, protect us through this auspicious rite of bali-offering.
To the Yoginīs, svāhā! To the Yoginī of all castes, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ! Whatever yoginī there may be—whether fierce, gentle, most terrible, or supreme;
whether moving through the sky, moving on the earth, or moving through space—may she always be pleased with me.
[This is] for all these yoginīs.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the seat of the pretas.
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).
She is of terrible form, most fierce, and of wrathful appearance; she is Caṇḍikā, whose face is made formidable by fangs, and she stands upon a corpse.
Fleshless and adorned with a garland of skulls by Kālarātri,
the Goddess holds a sword and a *pheṭa*, and bears a *ḍamaru* drum and a *khaṭvāṅga* staff.
With a *kartī* and a skull-bowl in her hands, and likewise holding a vessel of nectar (*bindu*),
she has curly, upward-pointing, tawny hair, tawny eyebrows, and tawny eyes.
With her limbs adorned with all ornaments, her hair standing erect, and possessing a formidable form, she is Cāmuṇḍā, the Supreme Goddess.
Aiṁ Hskhphreṁ, the sandals of Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī. Oblation.

Aiṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! In the sacred seat of Oḍiyāna, the Mistress of the Seat, Vikaṭā, of fierce form; in the sacred seat of Jālandhara, the Mistress of the Seat, Śrī Jvālāmukhī, Śrī Jvālāmālinī; in the sacred seat of Pūrṇagiri, the Mistress of the Seat, Pūrṇāvaraṇākhyā; in the sacred seat of Kāmarūpa...
The mistress of the seats (pīṭhanāyakī) is Śrī Kāminī, Śrī Bahurūpasvāminī, and Śṛṣṭikāriṇī;
Ha, Kva, Ḍa, Kkī; Karṇāṭī, Koṅkaṇā, and Lāḍadeśī; Rodraśakti;
Oḍiyāna, Jālandhara, Pūrṇagiri, and Kāmarūpa—these are the seats (pīṭha), fields (kṣetra), secondary fields (upakṣetra), and the four paths (catuḥpatha).

O Ekavṛkṣanadīsaṃghaṭṭe! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ! O you who pacify all obstacles and bestow all accomplishments! Accept this offering of raw flesh and this oblation of blood! Consume it! Eṃ!
O Ambā Śrīsiddhicāmuṇḍā, [worship] your sandals!
Hskhphreṁ! O glorious Siddhicāmuṇḍā, accept this bali offering, svāhā!

Oṃ! Those beings of various forms who dwell in the heavens, on earth, or in the intermediate space, and those situated in the depths of the netherworld, who are manifested through animal births—[to them, I offer this].
May the hundreds of cruel beings, such as heretics and others, who are stationed here, be satisfied with a pleased mind; may these spirits accept this offering.
Oṃ! Being satisfied by this offering of food, may you, the deities of the bali, forgive us;
may you dwell as you please, even including the elder piśācas.
All these belong to Cāmuṇḍā.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the Lord of Mice.
Meditative concentration.
[I bow to] Gaṇeśvara, who resembles a conch, a kunda flower, or the moon; who has the face of an elephant;
who is mounted upon a rat-throne; and who is the three-eyed Supreme Lord.
Salutations to the one who has become the king of elephants, holding a rosary for recitation, an axe, a drop, and likewise a leaf, as well as a spear and a sacred thread.
Homage to the flower of meditative concentration.
Aiṃ Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ! To the venerable Lord of the Kula-gaṇas, the sandals! [Offering of] bali.
Aiṃ Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaiṃ Gauṃ Gaḥ, to Gaṇeśvara, Glāṃ Glīṃ Glūṃ Glauṃ Glaḥ, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Glauṃ, to Mahāgaṇapati, Herambanātha, the elephant-faced one of golden hue,
possessing ten arms and three eyes, seated upon a great lion-throne.

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to Cañcalā Devī together with Her Śakti; to Glūṃkāra, who is accompanied by the group of five syllables consisting of the consonants from Gha to Na, the vowels, and the semi-vowels; to the Fruit-God (Phaladeva) of the four corners—white, black, yellow, and green—in the center.

To the Lord of the Gaṇas, the Master of the Gaṇas, together with his limbs, his attendants, and his retinue, the bestower of all accomplishments—to him [I offer] saffron and red [flowers]. Conquer all wicked ones! Crush and destroy all great obstacles! Paralyze and shatter the applications of hostile yantras and tantras! O Great King Kūṣmāṇḍa and the rest!
Destroy the diseases of leprosy!

O you who bestow happiness, good fortune, health, strength, and sovereignty; O cause of universal enchantment, grant all gold, wealth, grain, and all livestock, and increase the ten directions, the slaves, and the maidservants.

Destroy all misfortunes; grant all peace! Accept this offering of wine, meat, flowers, incense, lamps, and cooked rice, presented according to tradition; accept this bali! Turu muru glāṁ glīṁ glaṁ glaiṁ glauṁ glaḥ glāṁ śrīṁ geṁ glauṁ glaḥ glūṁ mahāgaṇapataye svāhā!
Forgive me, O Giver of Boons; svāhā!
Aiṁ gāṁ gīṁ gūṁ glaiṁ gauṁ gaḥ glauṁ! O Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara, accept this oblation; svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ, to Gaṇapati, the bestower of boons, bring all people under my control; accept this offering, svāhā!
Oṃ! May Vighnarāja, together with his Śakti, constantly bestow peace upon me, accomplishing all my tasks at all times without obstacle.
Of all these groups.
[One should perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the mudrās of the staff, the threatening gesture, the womb, the drop, and the elephant.
Recitation.
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Svāhā. Thrauṃ Svāhā.
Yāṃ svāhā || Hkhphreṃ svāhā || Glūṃ svāhā ||
Accept this recitation, svāhā!
Hymn of Praise.
O son of Gaurī, Kumāra, the sky-like expanse, the field, the Yoginīs,
Cāmuṇḍā of fierce form, Gaṇeśa the Lord of Obstacles who removes the fear of misfortune.

Adorned with flowers and other offerings, incense, lamps, meat, and oblations, her limbs decorated, she who grants the desired fruits of those who worship her bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
O Deceiver, may all this in the ritual procedure for the worship with offerings be completely fulfilled.
Homage to Śrīnātha! Homage to Śrīsiddhinātha! Homage again and again to Śrīkujeśanātha! Thus is the fivefold offering (pañcabali).
Having performed the purification with betel leaves and other items, [perform] the libation (tarpaṇa).

May Aṃ, seated upon the throne of the gratified spirits (pretāsana), be present during the ritual movement; may Bhairava, whose form is the mantra, and Caṇḍī, seated upon the fierce throne (caṇḍāsana), protect us; may the guardians of the world (lokapālas) with their serpent hoods, the lords of serpents, the yakṣas, the rākṣasas, the daityas, together with the hosts of ancestors (pitṛgaṇa), the mothers (mātaraḥ), and the guardians of the field (kṣetrapālas) [be present].
May the yoginīs, joined in yoga, whether moving in water or moving in the sky, drink this breath.
May all the deities, the Rudras, the Vināyakas, the Yoginīs, and the Kṣetrapālas drink [of this] while I remain established as a goddess.
The sentence.
Homage to the illustrious Lord! Homage to the illustrious Master of Accomplishment!
Homage to the illustrious Kujeśanātha; salutations again and again!
The ritual of bowing with the command. Having sipped water, [offer] three drops on the face.
The invocation.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! May that Goddess who is both supreme and non-supreme, who dwells in the sky and whose nature is space, who has gone to the world of the gods and is gentle, come here to this mandala.
I shall summon this; I summon.
The three gods.
Khphreṃ, sandals for the human throne; Khphreṃ, sandals for the peacock throne.
KH PHREṂ! To the one who sits upon the mouse, the sandals!
KH PHREṂ THHMRAUṂ: To the goddess Dambhakī of Prastaradvīpa, the great darkness, and to the Kṣetrapāla, [I offer] the sandals and the sacrificial offering (bali).
Khphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. The oblation.
Khphreṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ! To the venerable Kulagaṇeśvara, the sandals! The offering!
The Thaṇḍirīyas [should] perform the Hṅavana, Dathu-pāṭa, and Valisaṃ.
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the tarjanī, staff, and elephant mudrās.
Now follows the worship of the seasons.
Aiṁ, the pādukā for Ādhāraśakti. Aiṁ, the pādukā for Anantāsana.
Pādukā to the one whose seat is the bulbous root (kanda). Aiṃ! Pādukā to the one whose seat is man (nara).
Aiṁ, the pādukā for the petal-seat. Aiṁ, the pādukā for the filament-seat.
Aiṁ, the sandals for the seat of the pericarp; Aiṁ, the sandals for the lotus-seat.
Meditative absorption.
Three-eyed, six-armed, and peaceful, adorned with matted locks and a crescent moon,
wearing a garland of skulls, white in color, and seated in the yogic posture.
Rudra is clothed in a tiger skin, adorned with serpent-king ornaments,
and holds a trident and a rosary in his right hands.
One should depict the god Mṛtyuñjaya, the destroyer of death and disease, holding a skull-cup and a water-pot in his left hands, while both hands form the yoga-mudrā.
Thus ends the flower of meditative concentration; homage!
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, homage to Mṛtyuñjaya, the embodiment of the full water-pot.
The Bali offering: Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā. Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu. Oṃ, salutation to Rudra.
Oṃ, homage to Sadāśiva. Oṃ, homage to Īśvara.
Salutation to the Ganges and the other rivers, and to the seven oceans.
Aiṃ, salutation to the fortnight. Salutation to the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa.
Aiṃ, obeisance to the Season. Aiṃ, obeisance to the Year.
Aiṁ, salutation to the seven oceans beginning with the salt ocean.
Aiṃ, salutation to the lunar days beginning with Nandā. Aiṃ, salutation to the constellations beginning with Aśvinī.
Aiṁ, salutation to the yogas beginning with Viṣkambha. Aiṁ, salutation to the muhūrtas.
Aiṃ, salutation to the nine planets beginning with Āditya.
Aiṃ, salutation to the twelve zodiac signs beginning with Aries.
Aiṃ, salutations to the seven sages, beginning with Vasiṣṭha.
Aiṁ, salutation to the eight long-lived ones, beginning with Aśvatthāman.
Aiṃ, salutation to the ten world-protectors, beginning with Indra.
Aiṃ, salutation to the eight Kula serpents beginning with Ananta.
Rudracaṇḍā and the others.
The sandals of the goddess Śrī Rudracaṇḍā; the sandals of the goddess Śrī Pracaṇḍā.
The sandal of the goddess Śrīcaṇḍogrā; the sandal of the goddess Śrīcaṇḍanāyikā.
The venerable goddess Caṇḍā, the sandal; the venerable goddess Cavati, the sandal.
The sandal of the goddess Śrīcaṇḍarūpā; the sandal of the goddess Śrīaticāṇḍikā.
Aiṁ Hskṣmlvryūṁ, [I offer] the sandals to the form of the Full Vase (Saṃpūrṇakalaśamūrti). The offering (bali).
The triple añjali gesture.

Aiṁ Hskṣmlvryūṁ! O Kulavṛkṣa Mahāsena, O Enchanter, to the Lord of the Kalās, Tattvas, and Mantra-deities of all sacred fords; to the essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, and to the Tattva of Śiva-Vidyā; Hskṣmlvryūṁ Śkṣmlvryīṁ!
Salutation to the venerable form of the complete water-pot (kalaśa).
The six-limbed [practice].
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, homage to the heart of Mṛtyuñjaya.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, svāhā to the head of Mṛtyuñjaya.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, vaṣaṭ to Mṛtyuñjaya for the crest-lock (śikhā).
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, hūṃ! To Mṛtyuñjaya, for the armor.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, to Mṛtyuñjaya, for the three eyes, vauṣaṭ!
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, to Mṛtyuñjaya, for the weapon, phaṭ! [Bali offering.]
Hnasakana || Homage to Śrī.
Sidhramūṅa. Homage to Lakṣmī. [Perform] the invocation and other rites. One should display the Dhenu-mudrā.
Recitation: Oṃ juṃ saḥ svāhā.
Hymn of Praise.

I bow down to that very Bhairava, the primordial deity known as Mṛtyuñjaya, who is worshipped by the guardians of the celestial worlds, headed by Brahmā, and upon whom they have prostrated themselves; to him I go for refuge.
May all this ritual procedure for worship—consisting of perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps—be completely fulfilled here.
Thus concludes the worship of the vase.
Now follows the worship of the water-pot (kumbhapūjā).
Aiṃ, the sandals for the lotus seat.
Meditative absorption.
Resembling the white snow-mountain and the moon, she has five faces and three eyes;
she is endowed with ten powerful arms, with various weapons raised in her hands.
Or one should meditate upon the Goddess, reddish-rose in hue, the bestower of all happiness,
holding an elephant-goad, a sword, a trident, a severed head, and likewise a vessel of blood.
Holding a noose, a skull-topped staff, and a vessel, as well as a water-pot and the gesture that grants fearlessness,
she is Kumbhadevī, the Mother of the World and Queen of the Gods.
Having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess, who bestows the fruits of all desires.
Homage to the Flower of Dhyāna.
The triple añjali gesture.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
Gaṃ glūṃ, the sandals to Gaṇapatīnātha, together with his beloved consort Svaśaktivallabhāmbā.
Vaṃ plūṃ, the sandals for Śrī Vaṭukanātha, together with his beloved Śakti.
KṢĀṂ KṢŪṂ, O Kṣetrapāla of your own station, together with your Śakti and beloved consort, [I offer] the pādukā.
KH PHREṂ MAHĀKALĀCAṆḌINĪ RAUDRAMUKHE HRĀṂ HRĪṂ HRAUṂ KĀṂ ŚRĪKĀKAMUKHĪ PĀDUKĀM ||
Khphreṃ Cīṃ, the sandals of Śrīcaṇḍamukhī!
Khphreṃ Duṃ Śrīṭāṅkāli, [I worship] your sandals!
Khphreṃ Tṛṃ, the sandals of Śrīrāpiṇī.
KH PHREṂ PTHAṂ PĀVAKĪ PĀDUKĀṂ ||
Khphreṃ Yaiṃ Śrīyamaghaṇṭhī, the sandals!
Khphreṁ Sauṁ, [I worship] the sandals of Śivādūtī.
Khphreṃ Kṣaḥ, the sandals of the Mother Śrīkṣayaṃkarī.
From the east to the northeast; in the center.
KHPHREṂ ĀṂ KROṂ PHREṂ MAHĀSIDDHI SAMAYA KHPHREṂ BHAIRAVĪ GHORALAKṢMĪ VARAPRADE SVĀHĀ ||
Three handfuls of water offered with joined palms.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. Bali. Six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga).
Khphreṃ, homage to the heart. Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head. Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
KHPHREṂ KAVACĀYA HŪṂ || KHPHREṂ NETRATRAYĀYA VAṢAṬ || KHPHREṂ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ ||
Bali.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! Those who reside in the divine atmosphere, the earth, and the depths of the netherworld—Kākinī, Cākinī, Ṭāṅkālī, and likewise Tāpinī.
Yamaghaṇṭā, Śivādūtī, Kṣayāntā, and Parameśvarī.
Having taken the bali offering, I, through devotion, offer it with the word "svāhā."
Performing the invocation and other rites, one should display the yonimudrā.
Recitation.
KHPHREṂ SVĀHĀ ||
Hymn of Praise.
Mounted upon a lotus and a corpse, resembling a crystal gem, five-faced and three-eyed, she deludes the three worlds; her body is draped in divine garments and she possesses ten arms,
holding in her left hands a skull-cup, a trident, a jar, the gesture of granting boons, a great noose, and a severed head.
I bow to Siddhilakṣmī, who holds a bell, a skull-topped staff, a sword, and a goad together with the gesture of fearlessness.
May all this—the ritual procedure for worship consisting of the offering of perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps—be completely fulfilled here.
Thus concludes the worship of the jar (kumbhapūjā).
Now follows the worship of the field and the vase.
In the southeast: the seat.
Aiṃ, the sandals for Narāsana.
Meditative concentration.
[He meditates on] the Lord of the Field (Kṣetrapāla), who has the luster of a cloud, who holds a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga) and a sword beginning with the letter *ka*,
and who bears a skull-bowl (*pheṭaka*) and a superior trident (*varakādi*), the Supreme Lord.
He has six arms and three eyes, stands upon a man, wears a garland of severed heads,
is clothed in human skin, possesses matted hair, and has the moon as his crest-jewel.
One should meditate on the bestower of all accomplishments for the pacification of all obstacles.
Homage to the flower of meditative concentration.
Threefold salutation with joined palms.
Aiṁ Kṣāṁ Kṣīṁ Kṣūṁ Kṣmlvryūṁ, the sandals for Kṣetrapāla.
The six-limbed [practice].
KṢĀṂ, obeisance to the heart; KṢĪṂ, svāhā to the head; KṢŪṂ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
KṢAIṂ, HŪṂ, for the armor; KṢAUṂ, VAṢAṬ, for the three eyes; KṢAḤ, PHAṬ, for the weapon.
Bali.
Aiṃ! Descend, O Lord of this very place, by whatever name you are known, descend into the center of the maṇḍala!
You who possess four arms and three eyes, holding a khaṭvāṅga, a sword, a pheṭaka, and a trident;
adorned with a garland of great skulls; possessing a radiance equal to ten million flashes of lightning!
Come, come, O Bhairava, in your terrifying form! Accept this offering from those who have arrived as they are;
dispel my obstacles! Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! Thus ends the field-offering (kṣetrabali).
Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers—obeisance!
One should display the tarjanī-mudrā.
Japa: KṢĀṂ SVĀHĀ.
Hymn of Praise.
Seated upon a human corpse, abiding in the south wind,
dwelling in every house— to you, O Kṣetrapāla, obeisance!
May all this—the ritual procedure for worship consisting of offerings of perfume, flowers, incense, and lamps—be completely fulfilled here.
Thus concludes the worship of the field and the vessel.
Now follows the worship of the Vaṭuka-kalaśa.
In the northeast: Aiṃ, the pādukā for the peacock-throne.
Meditative concentration.
One should meditate upon the three-eyed God of gods, Vaṭuka, who holds a staff, is fierce, has a tawny form, and is seated upon a peacock.
Homage to the flower of meditative concentration.
The triple añjali gesture.
Aiṁ vāṁ vīṁ vūṁ vmlvryūṁ, the sandals for Vaṭukanātha.
The six-limbed [practice].
Vāṃ, salutation to the heart. Vīṃ, svāhā to the head. Vūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the tuft of hair.
Vaiṃ for the armor, hūṃ; Vauṃ for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ; Vaḥ for the weapon, phaṭ.
Bali.

Aiṃ! O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, radiant with a mass of tawny matted hair, three-eyed one with flaming mouths, descend! Come, come, O Blessed One, into the center of the maṇḍala! Accept the offering as it has been presented; grant me my desired object! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! Thus ends the offering to Vaṭuka.
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the staff mudrā.
Japa: VĀṂ SVĀHĀ.
Hymn of Praise.

Vlāṃ vlīṃ vlūṃ! O you who hold a lute in hand, va vi va vu! O Vaṭuka! Klīṃ oṃ! Hara! O you who possess the staff-gesture (daṇḍamudrā)! Hrīṃ dhrīṃ drāṃ! Taṃ! O you who exist in the triple resonance, O unstruck sound, O you who are struck down, O bestower of enjoyment, O bestower of liberation!
Haṃ he haṃsa! O you who abide in the method of the swan, O you who have gone to the state beyond *la*, *ra*, and *pa*, O bestower of perfection on the path of the self!
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ aiṃ! O Kulogha, Kakaka, Kivipula, Vīrabhadra, salutations to you!
May all this—the ritual procedure for worship consisting of the offering of perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps—be complete here.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the worship of the Vaṭuka-kalaśa.
Now follows the worship of the astrologer and the water-pot.
Nairṛtya.
Aiṁ, the sandals for the seat of the crucible.
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon the four-armed deity, red in color and three-eyed,
holding a noose and a goad, and adorned with a rosary of beads.
The mantra-practitioner should visualize the Bestower of Boons, his body embraced by Śakti,
seated upon a lotus posture and dancing atop a mouse.
Wearing a mass of matted hair, peaceful, and adorned with a crescent moon as his crest-ornament.
Homage to the flower of meditative concentration.
The triple añjali gesture.
Aiṃ Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gmlvryūṃ Glauṃ, the sandals of Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara.
The six-limbed [practice].
*gāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *gīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *gūṃ* to the crest-lock, *vauṣaṭ*;
*gaiṃ* to the armor, *hūṃ*; *gauṃ* to the three eyes, *vaṣaṭ*; *gaḥ* to the weapon, *phaṭ*.
Bali.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ, to Gaṇapati, the bestower of boons, bring all people under my control; accept this offering, svāhā!
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the elephant mudrā.
Recitation.
glūṃ svāhā ||
Hymn of Praise.
Salutations to you, the elephant-faced one, the great hero, who holds the root-modaka in his hand, the dispeller of all obstacles, and the son of Gaṅgā.
May all this—the ritual procedure for worship consisting of the offering of perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps—be completely fulfilled here.
Thus concludes the worship of Gaṇaka and Lasa.
Now follows the worship of the Yoginī-vase.
Vāyavya | Āsana |
Aiṃ, the sandals for the corpse-seat. Aiṃ Jāṃ, the sandals for the Yoginīs.
Meditative absorption.
The goddess holds a trident and a bowl, her body is red, and she is mounted upon a lion;
she is endowed with all auspicious marks, possesses three eyes, and has the crescent moon as her crest-ornament.
Thus is meditation.
The triple añjali gesture.
Aiṃ Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ Smlvryūṃ, the sandals of all the Yoginīs.
The six-limbed [practice].
Sāṃ, salutation to the heart. Sīṃ, svāhā to the head. Sūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Saiṃ for the armor, hūṃ; sau for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ; saḥ for the weapon, phaṭ.
Bali.
Aiṃ! Whosoever among the Yoginīs are born of the *pīṭhas*, born of the *kṣetras*, born together (*sahajā*), born of enjoyment (*jogajā*), born of the womb (*garbhajā*), or born of the *kula*;

whosoever among the Yoginīs are the sky-farers (*khecarī*), earth-walkers (*bhūcarī*), cow-path wanderers (*gocarī*), or those consisting of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, or ten syllables; those who traverse the three worlds—[to them, salutation].
Accept the offering of those who have appeared as they are; grant me accomplishment! HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
Perform the invocation and other rites; then display the yoni-mudrā.
Japa: Sāṃ svāhā.
Hymn of Praise.
I bow to you, O Yoginī, the Goddess who pervades the three worlds, who wields the sword and the skull-cup, and who crushes all obstacles.
May all this—the ritual procedure for worship consisting of the offering of perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps—be completely fulfilled here.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the worship of the Yoginī-vessel.
Now, for the western direction.
The worship of the sacrificial ground; the ritual vessel marked with the signs of the flaying knife and skull-cup; the offering of the sacrificial ground, the fire, and the parched grain.
Homage to the Guru.
Salutations to that venerable Guru who has revealed that state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and unmoving world is pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutations to that illustrious Guru.
Aiṃ, salutations to the supreme gurus. Aiṃ, salutations to the gurus who abide in the highest station.
Aiṃ, salutations to the supreme teachers and gurus.
The sandals for the one in the lotus posture on the head; the sandals for the one in the tortoise posture on the crest-lock.
On the side, the scattering of unhusked grains.
Kiṇi vircce koṅkarṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ.
One should perform a complete circumambulation with the Vajramuñja mudrā.
Aiṁ Aiṁ Hūṁ Phaṭ! To the Vajra-enclosure, Svāhā! [This is] the touching of the ten gates.
Aiṃ cala makule kulamacale hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Kiṇi vircce koṅkaṇṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ pādukāṃ.
The purification of the hands.
Aiṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā; Hrāṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals for the two thumbs.
Aiṁ Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the Lamp of the Kula; Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, [I offer] the sandals to the two index fingers.
Aiṁ Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ, O you with the curly locks! Hrūṁ, [I worship] the sandals at the two middle fingers.
Aiṃ Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhi Bahurūpāyai Hreṃ Śrīṃ; [I offer] the sandals to the two ring fingers.
Aiṁ Chāṁ Chīṁ, to Mahantārikā, Hrauṁ; [I offer] the sandals to the two little fingers (Kaniṣṭhā).
Aiṁ Kiṇi Vicce Koṅkaṇṇāyai Hraḥ; salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.
The ritual placement of the letters.
Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed Lady, the Lotus of the Heart, the Auspicious One with the Upward-Facing Face; [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula, to the one whose face is preceded by Śrī—to her, the sandals!
Aiṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ, O you with the tawny mane, [I offer] the sandals to the venerable southern face.
Aiṃ! To the one who is Ghorā, Aghorā, and Aghorāmukhī, to the multiformed Śrī-Uttaravaktrā, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ Chāṃ Chīṃ, [I offer] the sandals to the Mantrārīkā, the venerable Western Face.
Kiṇi Vicce, [I offer] the sandal for Koṅkarṇā, the venerable Parāparavaktrā.
The placement [of the mantras] is on the face.
Aiṁ! Salutation to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā; Hrāṁ! To the Heart, the sandals.
Aiṃ Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula, Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head!
Aiṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ, Vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock of Varvara.
Aiṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ, O you with the curly locks, Hrūṃ! [This is] for the tuft of hair (śikhā).
Aiṃ, O Ghorā, Aghorā, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpā; Hraiṃ, for the armor, Hūṃ!
Aiṃ Chāṃ Chīṃ, vaṣaṭ to Mahantārikā and her three eyes! Hrauṃ! Vaṣaṭ!
Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ.
Thus is the placement of the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The worship of the water vessel.
Aiṃ, the pādukā for the seat of the water vessel.

Aiṁ Hskṣmlvryūṁ. To the venerable Lord of the Water Vessel (Śrījalapātrabhaṭṭāraka), the power of bliss (Ānandaśakti) and sovereign hero of Bhairava-bliss (Bhairavānandavīrādhipati), Śkṣmlvryīṁ—[I offer] my sandals.
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṃ, hūṃ, for the armor; Hrauṃ, vaṣaṭ, for the three eyes; Hraḥ, phaṭ, for the weapon.
Salutations to the invocation, the installation, the moon, the unhusked grain, and the flower.
One should display the Dhenu-mudrā.
The Gāyatrī; the consecration.
Aiṃ! We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon her who is the lamp of the Kula; may that Kubjī inspire us.
The worship of the argha vessel.
Aiṁ, the pādukā for the sanctification of the argha vessel.

Aiṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraḥ! Quiver! O you of most terrible form, crackle, move swiftly, roar, vomit, subdue, strike down, shatter the obstacles! Hūṃ phaṭ krauṃ! O Śrī Mahākaumārikā, Vicce! [I worship] the sandals.

Aiṃ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ! To the venerable Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Sovereign Queen of the Great Vidyās (Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī), HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ! Sandals for the venerable Mistress of the Arghapātra (the vessel of offering).
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṃ, for the armor, hūṃ. Hrauṃ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ.
Hraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon!
Salutations to the invocation, the installation, the fierce one, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers.
One should display the yonimudrā.
Purification of the Elements (Bhūtaśuddhi): Having formed the Tortoise Mudrā (Kacchapa-mudrā).
aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hsauṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
Self-worship.
Aiṁ, sandalwood, the sandals. Hrīṁ, unbroken rice grains, the sandals.
The sandals of Śrī Vīrabhasma; the sandals of Hsphreṃ, the enchantress of all people.
Hsauṃ: various parasols, ornaments, flowers, and sandals.
Aiṁ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ Ānandaśakti Bhairavānandavīrādhipataye ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ; [I offer] flowers and sandals to my own self. Aiṁ KUSAUṂ; [I offer] sandals. Thus is the self-worship (ātmapūjā).
The invocation.
Within the mandala of Śrī Saṃvarta, the power (śakti) that bestows bliss through the sequential steps is most formidable;
it has emanated the fourfold logic, the fivefold group residing in both Akula and Kula, another sixfold group, four others,
and again another fivefold group of four— this is the mandala.
Let one bow to that excellent guru, Śrī Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom [all things] are interpenetrated.
I shall summon this; I summon.
Aiṃ Alūṃ, the sandals of the venerable Ādideva of the infinite maṇḍala.
The three gods.
Aiṃ, the sandals for Narāsanā; Aiṃ, the sandals for Mayūrāsanā.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the seat of the crucible. Aiṃ Thrauṃ, the sandals for the goddess Dambhakī, the great crow Kṣetrapāla of Prastaradvīpa. Oblation.
Aiṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals of Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha; [this is] the offering.
Aiṃ Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ! To the venerable Lord of the Kula-gaṇas, the sandals! [Offering of] bali.
Salutations for the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers.
One should display the *daṇḍagaja* mudrā with the index finger.
The sandals for the lotus posture; the sandals of one's own guru, Tuṣṇīśānandanātha Deva.
The sandals of the supreme guru, the divine Śrī Caryānandanātha.
The sandals of the supreme teacher, the venerable Śrī Mitrānandadeva.
Aiṁ Hskṣmlvryūṁ, to the venerable Lord of the Three Purifications (Śrītriśuddhibhaṭṭāraka), the sovereign hero Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, Śkṣmlvryīṁ, [I offer] the sandals.
Bali: the invocation and so forth; one should display the Dhenu and Yoni mudrās.
Aṃ astrāya phaṭ. Purification of the hands. The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the hands and limbs.
Hsaṃ, salutation to the heart; Kṣmaṃ, svāhā to the head; Lvaṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Nyaṃ for the armor, hūṃ; ūṃ for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ; aḥ for the weapon, phaṭ.
Thus concludes the ritual assignment of the hands and limbs (karāṅganyāsa).
Haṃ, the sandal at the place of the crest-lock; Saṃ, the sandal at the place of the head.
KṢAṂ on the forehead, salutation to the sandals; MAṂ on the circle of the face, salutation to the sandals.
Laṃ, sandals for the heart; Vaṃ, sandals for the navel; Raṃ, sandals for the secret place.
Yaṃ jānau pādukāṃ || Ūṃ pādadvayoḥ pādukāṃ || Aṃ saṃ sarvāṅge pādukāṃ ||
Thus concludes the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the ninefold self.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, the sandals for the venerable Navātman-nyāsa. The offering:
Aiṃ, the sandals for the lotus-seat; the sandals for the corpse-seat.
Now, meditation.
Aiṁ: Seated upon a corpse in the lotus posture, ten-faced and three-eyed, with a sky-colored complexion, greatly radiant, and endowed with all auspicious marks.
The eastern face is the color of gold, the southern is adorned with black,
the northern is yellow, and the one above that is reddened.
To the right of the red [color] is smoky gray, and to the north is white;
above that is yellow, and to the right of the yellow is black.
They say the upper [face] is red, and above that, the supreme face is white;
the god has eighteen arms and is adorned with a garland of severed heads.
The god holds a sword and a *pheṭa*, as well as a trident and a goad;
he likewise holds a sacred thread, an excellent water-pot, a hand-drum, and a skull-topped staff.
He holds a well-joined arrow and bow, adorned with a bell on his arm;
he has a discus and a mace in his hands, and his other hand is extended in the gesture of granting boons.
The deity should bear the bindu upon the letter *ka* and be adorned with various ornaments;
his color should be that of a corpse, and he should be comfortably seated upon his seat.
Whoever, with a disciplined mind, meditates upon this ninefold mandala of form— the mandala of the Guru— those men shall swiftly attain accomplishment.
Thus ends the flower of meditative concentration; homage!
Aiṁ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ! To the worship of the hero Ānandaśaktibhairava-Ānanda, ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ!
The sandals of the venerable Navātma-guṇamaṇḍala-bhaṭṭārikā.
Aiṃ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ. Salutation to the sandals of the venerable Navātma-guru-maṇḍala-bhaṭṭāraka.
The communal worship of the Gaṇas.
nlūṃ om, the great worship: the sandals for the venerable Kubjikā of the Guru-maṇḍala.
Mlūṃ E, this great offering for the Śakti of the Guru-maṇḍala; Pā, the sandals.
Plūṃ u, the sandals of the venerable Goddess of the maṇḍala of the supreme preceptor.
Slūṃ, the sandals of Śrījñānā, the maṇḍala of the supreme guru.
Glūṃ, the sandals for the command of the glorious maṇḍala of the gurus.
Salutation to the sandals of the supreme lineage of gurus of the Śiva-tattva.
Salutation to the sandals of the supreme and non-supreme lineage of gurus of the Śrīvidyā-tattva.
The sandals of Śrī-Ājñākusumā; the sandals of Śrī-Jayā.
The sandals for Śrī Vijayā; the sandals for Śrī Ajitā; the sandals for Śrī Aparājitā;
the sandals for Śrī Haṃ Śāntyatītā; the sandals for Śrī Yaṃ Śānti.
Śrī Raṃ, the sandal of Vidyā; Śrī Vaṃ, the sandal of Pratiṣṭhā.
Śrī Laṃ, the sandal for Nivṛtti; Śrī Kulabhairava, the sandal.
The sandals to Śrī Kulanātha Bhairava; the sandals to Śrī Kulatumburu Bhairava.
Pādukā to Śrī Kulapāṭaka Bhairava; pādukā to Śrī Kulājñā Bhairava.

The sandals to the Goddess of the Śrīkula Command (Ājñā). KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢU KṢAḤ, the sandals to the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla). GĀṂ GĪṂ GŪṂ GAḤ GLAUṂ, the sandals to the Lord of the Śrīkula Gaṇas (Śrīkulagaṇeśvara).
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha.
Kroṃ Śrīṃ Mahākaumārikā Vicce, [I worship] the sandalwood slipper.
Aiṁ Hskṣmlvryūṁ, to the venerable Navātman, the lord of the circle of gurus, the consort Śkṣmlvryīṁ, and the sovereign Ānandaśaktibhairava-Ānandavīra, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṁ śkṣmlvryīṁ, Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, Hskṣmlvryūṁ Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī; [I offer] the sandals to the venerable Navātma-gurumaṇḍala-bhaṭṭarikā.
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṁ, for the armor, hūṃ. Hrauṁ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Hnaḥ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
This is their offering.
Aiṃ Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarvasarve Hreṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ, O you who possess the form of Rudra, Hraḥ! [I offer] the sandals. [The offering: Bali.
Aiṃ Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ Trailokyākarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmāṅgadrāvaṇī Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇī Aiṃ So Saḥ, [I worship] the Śrīpādukā.
Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ! To Kubjikā, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Not-Terrible One, O She Whose Face is Not-Terrible! Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi Vicce! [Salutation to] the Sandals.

The sandals of the divine siddhis and the wheel of commitment (samayacakra) within the entire seat of mantras, the lion-throne seat, the secondary seats, the fields, the subsidiary fields, and the gathering places.
Aiṁ. Whatever has been spoken or remains unsaid—all that, Aiṁ, is the sandal for the venerable Heart.
Thus is the offering for each individual.
[Offer] the invocation, the seat, the water for the feet, unbroken rice, and flowers with "Namaḥ. One should display the Yoni-mudrā.
The Three Bindus. Homage to the illustrious Nātha. Homage to the illustrious Siddhinātha.
Homage to the venerable Kujeśanātha; salutations again and again. Thus ends the worship of the maṇḍala of the gurus.
The sandals for the lotus posture.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ. To the venerable lineage of Gurus, the sandals [are offered]. The oblation.
The sandals for the lotus posture.
Aiṁ śkṣmlvryīṁ. To the venerable Oṣadhikarmabhaṭṭārikā, [this is] the sandal and the offering. Balih.
The sandals for the bull-throne; the sandals for the lion-throne.
Aiṁ Hskṣmlvryūṁ. To the one honored by Bhairava and Ānandaśakti, Śkṣmlvryūṁ;
to the venerable Śrīkaṇṭhanātha together with his Śakti, [I offer] the sandals. The sacrificial offering (bali).
The Brahmāṇī and others.
The sandals for the one seated upon a swan; the sandals for the one seated upon a bull.
The sandals for the peacock-throne; the sandals for the eagle-throne.
The sandal for the one seated upon a buffalo; the sandal for the one seated upon an elephant.
The sandals for the seat of the pretas; the sandals for the seat of humans.
Aiṃ! O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Giver of Boons, O Pure One, O Brahmāyaṇī, O Vicce—[I offer] the sandals. [I offer] the sacrificial oblation (bali).
Aiṃ! O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Giver of Boons, O Stainless One, O Māheśvarī, O Vicce—[I offer] the sandals. [The offering].
Aiṃ! O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Giver of Boons, O Immaculate One, O Kaumāri, O Vicce! [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṃ! O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Giver of Boons, O Immaculate One, O Vaiṣṇavī, O Vicce! [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṃ! O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Giver of Boons, O Immaculate One, O Vārāhī, O Vicce—[I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṃ! O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Giver of Boons, O Immaculate One, O Indrāṇī, O Vicce! [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṃ! O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Giver of Boons, O Immaculate One, O Cāmuṇḍā, O Vicce—[I offer] the sandals. [This is] the oblation.
Aiṃ! O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Bestower of Boons, O Pure One, O Mahālakṣmī, O Vicce! [I offer] the sandals. Oblation.
This is the offering (bali) for them.
Pādukā to the Power of the Support (Ādhāra-śakti). Pādukā to the Seat of Bliss (Ānanda-āsana).
The sandal for the one whose seat is the bulbous root; the sandal for the one whose seat is the Nārā flower; the sandal for the one whose seat is the leaf.
Pādukā to Keśarāsana; pādukā to Karṇikāsana; pādukā to Padmāsana;
pādukā to Siṃhāsana; pādukā to Mahiṣāsana.
The sandals for the seat of Śumbha; the sandals for the seat of Niśumbha.
Salutation to Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Caṇḍacogrā; salutation to the sandals of Śrīṁ Hrīṁ.
The sandals of Śrī Rudracaṇḍā; the sandals of Śrī Pracaṇḍā.
The sandals of Śrī Caṇḍogrā; the sandals of Śrī Caṇḍanāyikā.
The sandals of Śrī Caṇḍā; the sandals of Śrī Caṇḍavatī.
The sandals of Śrī Caṇḍarūpā; the sandals of Śrī Aticaṇḍikā.
Aiṁ Hsphreṁ, the sandals of the illustrious Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī.
Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hsphreṃ ugracaṇḍe ripumardaṇi hūṃ phreṃ, always protect you and me, juṃ saḥ! O Mṛtyuharā, [this is for] the sandals. The offering (bali).
Aiṃ, the sandals for the lotus seat.
Aiṁ! To Rīṅgaṇḍi Piṅgaṭī Kuḍu Kaṇḍāyī, Svāhā! To Vāgeśvarī, the Great Mahantārikā, Vicce’s sandals! Oblation! (Baliḥ)
Aiṃ, the pādukā for Ādhāraśakti. Aiṃ, the pādukā for Anantāsana.
Sandals for the one whose seat is a bulbous root; sandals for the one whose seat is a reed; sandals for the one whose seat is a leaf.
The sandal for Keśarāsana; the sandal for Karṇikāsana.
Pādukā to the one seated on a lotus throne; pādukā to the one seated on the five pretas.
Hsauṃ Svāhā! Sandal for the fire-throne of the preta; sandal for the bull-throne.
The sandals for the lion-throne.
Aiṃ Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarvasarve Hreṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ, O you whose form is Rudra, Hraḥ! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ Trailokyākarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmāṅgadrāvaṇī Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇī Aiṃ So Saḥ, [I worship] the Śrīpādukā.

Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ! To Kubjikā, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Not-Terrible One, O She Whose Face is Not-Terrible! Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi Vicce! [Salutation to] the Sandalwood Slippers.
Aiṁ! Salutations to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā! Śrāṁ Śrīṁ Śrūṁ! Ṅa Ña Ṇa Na!
O you whose face is not terrible (Aghorāmukhī)! Chāṁ Chīṁ Kiṇi Vicce! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṁ Bhagavati Siddhe Hsphreṁ Hsphrīṁ Hsphrūṁ Kubjike Śrāṁ Śrīṁ Śrūṁ Khage Aiṁ Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhī Kiṇi Vicce Pādukāṁ. Thus, the offering (bali) is made for each [name].
Aiṃ! Whosoever among the Yoginīs are born of the *pīṭhas*, born of the fields (*kṣetra*), born together (*sahaja*), born of yoga, born from the womb, or born of the *kula*;

whosoever among the Yogins are the *khecarīs*, *bhūcarīs*, *gocarīs*, the single-syllabled, two-syllabled, three-syllabled, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine-syllabled ones who traverse the three worlds; [to them all, salutation].
Accept the offering of those who have appeared as they are; grant me accomplishment! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Three handfuls of water.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśakti, the sovereign hero (vīra) Bhairavānanda, and to Śkṣmlvryīṃ, the venerable lord of the twenty-eight rites (karmabhaṭṭāraka), [this] sandal (pādukā).

Aiṃ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ. For the worship of the hero Ānandaśaktibhairava-ānanda, [I offer] the sandals to the venerable Mahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, the auspicious Mistress of the Twenty-eight Karmas. Bali offering. Six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga).
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṃ, hūṃ, for the armor.
Hrauṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes. Hraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon.

Aiṃ! The sandals of the entire assembly of the seats (pīṭha), lion-thrones (siṃhāsana), primary seats (pīṭhī), secondary seats (upapīṭha), fields (kṣetra), subsidiary fields (upakṣetra), gathering places (saṃdoha), subsidiary gathering places (upasandoha), divine perfections (divyasiddhi), and the wheel of the covenant (samayacakra).
Aiṁ, whatever has been stated or unstated—all that, Aiṁ, is the sandal for the venerable Heart.
The offering (bali) is performed with the root mantra.
Salutations for the invocation, the installation, and the sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers.
One should display the Dhenu-yoni-mudrā. Thus ends the ritual worship (karmapūjā).
To the one seated upon a lotus, [I offer] sandals.
Aiṁ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ. To the venerable Trikhaṇḍā Bhāṭṭārikā, who consists of the Rudrakhaṇḍa, the Mātṛkhaṇḍa, and the Mantrakhaṇḍa, [I offer] the sandals. The offering (bali). The invocation and so forth.
One should display the trikhaṇḍā mudrā.
Aiṁ, the sandals to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti). Aiṁ, the sandals to the Seat of Ananta (Anantāsana).
Aiṃ, the sandals for the one whose seat is the bulb; the sandals for the one whose seat is the lotus.
Pādukā for the seat of petals; pādukā for the seat of filaments.
The sandals for the one seated upon the pericarp; the sandals for the one seated upon the lotus.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the seat of the five pretas. Aiṃ, the sandals for the seat of the Brahma-preta, the lord of the moon-maṇḍala.
Aiṁ, to the sovereign of the solar orb, seated upon the corpse of Viṣṇu, the sandals!
Aiṁ, the sandals for the sovereign of the fire-maṇḍala, whose throne is a Rudra-ghost.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the Lord of the Brahma-maṇḍala, seated upon the throne of the corpse (īra-preta).
Aiṃ, the pādukā for Sadāśiva, the lord of the Śakti-maṇḍala, who is seated upon a corpse-throne.
Aiṁ, the sandals for the Bull-throne. Aiṁ, the sandals for the Lion-throne.
Meditative absorption.
Aiṃ: I bow to the God established upon the bull, resplendent with the form of the color of the sky, having one face, three eyes, and bearing eighteen arms.
In her right hands, she holds a hand-drum, an axe, an arrow, a sword, a goad, a vajra, a conch, and the playing of a lute, as well as the gestures of granting boons and warding off fear.
In the left [hands], he holds a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), a trident, a bow, a shield, and a noose;
as well as a bell, a skull-cup, a hero’s [emblem], and the gestures of granting fearlessness and destroying fear.
A goddess situated upon the left thigh, her knee bound with a silken cloth;
she has one face and three eyes, and is described as being of a reddish (aruṇa) complexion.
Two-armed, granting boons with the right hand and dispelling fear with the left, she stands upon a lion;
she is richly adorned with various ornaments and possesses all auspicious marks.
This [deity], whose nature is the bliss of Bhairava, is proclaimed as the eldest of the eldest;
by meditating thus upon Mahādeva, human beings quickly attain perfection.
Homage to the Flower of Dhyāna.
Aiṃ Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarvasarve Hreṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ, O you whose form is Rudra, Hraḥ! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṁ Aiṁ Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṁ, who attracts the three worlds; Hrīṁ, who melts the limbs of desire; Klīṁ Strīṁ, the great agitator; Aiṁ Sā Saḥ, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
The sandals of the goddess Śrī Jayā; the sandals of the goddess Śrī Vijayā; the sandals of the goddess Śrī Ajitā; the sandals of the goddess Śrī Apājitā; the sandals of the goddess Śrī Jambhanī.
The sandals of the goddess Śrīstambhanī; the sandals of the goddess Śrīmohanī.
The sandals of the goddess Śrī Ākarṣaṇī. This is the offering for them.
Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṃ chīṃ kiṇi vicce! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ! Salutations to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā! Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ! To the one with the face of Aghorā, Ṅa Ña Ṇa! Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi Vicce! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ Bhagavati Siddhe Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ Kubjike Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ Khage Aiṃ Ghore Aghore Aghorākṣi Kiṇi Vicce Pādukāṃ. Baliḥ.
Three times with joined palms.
The sandals for the bull-throne; the sandals for the lion-throne.

Aiṁ hskṣmlvryūṁ, [I offer] the sandals to Śkṣmlvryīṁ, the venerable Lord of the Root Abode of the Western Tradition (Śrīpaścimamūlasthānabhaṭṭāraka), who is the sovereign of Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Viras, and the Power of Bliss (Ānandaśakti).
Aiṁ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ! To Ānandaśakti, the sovereign lord Bhairavānandavira;
to the venerable Mahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ; the sandals of the venerable Bhaṭṭārikā of the Western Root Abode.
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṁ, for the armor, hūṃ. Hrauṁ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Hraḥ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
The offering (bali) is made with the root mantra.

The sandals of the entire seat of mantras, the lion-throne, the pedestal, the secondary seats, the fields, the secondary fields, the meeting-places, the secondary meeting-places, and the wheel of the divine siddhis and the samaya.
Aiṁ. Whatever has been stated or unstated, all that—Aiṁ—is the sandal-paste for the venerable Heart.
This is the *bali* offering for them. Perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth. One should display the *yonimudrā*.
The Three Bindus. Homage to the illustrious Nātha. Homage to the illustrious Siddhinātha.
Homage to the illustrious Kujeśanātha; salutations again and again. [Thus ends the section on the Western Goddess.]
Then, [the ritual] for the temple of Jayatuṃbeśvarī.
The worship at the sacrificial ground; the threatening gesture and the marked jar; the offering of the sacrificial ground, the oblation, and the recitation of the *pāṭa*.
Having sipped water with the threefold truth (tritatva).
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva).
Hrūṃ, svāhā to the reality of consciousness.
Homage to the Guru.
Salutations to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutations to that illustrious Guru.
Aiṃ, salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the gurus who are the Parameṣṭhin.
Salutations to the supreme teachers and gurus. [I offer] the sandals to Balisa Padmāsana.
Place the sandals upon the tortoise-seat with the *thavaka* mantra; [protect] with the weapon-mantra *phaṭ*.
Aiṁ Hrūṁ Phaṭ! Within the vajra-penetrating cage, svāsvā!
O you who are unmoving in the family of the moving, hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Hraḥ! Phaṭ to the weapon!
The purification of the vase.
Hrāṃ, salutation to the little finger; Hrīṃ, svāhā to the ring finger; Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the middle finger.
Hraiṁ, to the index finger, hūṃ! Hrauṁ, to the thumb, vaṣaṭ! Hraḥ, to the weapon-mantra, phaṭ!
The placement of the hand.
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṁ, for the armor, hūṁ. Hrauṁ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Hraḥ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
The ritual placement of the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The worship of the water vessel.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the seat of the water-vessel.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, the sandals of the venerable Jalapātra-bhaṭṭārikā.
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṃ, hūṃ, for the armor; Hrauṃ, vaṣaṭ, for the three eyes; Hraḥ, phaṭ, for the weapon.
[Perform] the invocation (āvāhana), the stabilization (sthāpana), and offer sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers with "Namaḥ. One should display the cow-mudrā (dhenumudrā).
The Gāyatrī.
Hrīṃ! Let us know Ugraṇḍā; may we meditate upon Goddess Durgā; may Caṇḍā inspire us.
The worship of the argha vessel.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the seat of the argha vessel.
Aiṃ Aghore Hrīṃ Paramaghore Hrīṃ Ghorarūpe Haḥ! O you of terrible countenance, fearsome and terrifying one, vomit, drink, roar, roar! Phaṭ Hsauṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ!
Aiṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, the sandals for the venerable Mistress of the Argha-vessel (arghapātrabhaṭṭārikā).
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṁ, for the armor, hūṃ. Hrauṁ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Hraḥ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
[Perform] the invocation, the installation, and [offer] sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers; [say] "Namaḥ. One should display the *yonimudrā*.
Purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi): having formed the tortoise mudrā (kacchapamudrā).
aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hsauṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
Self-worship.
Aiṁ, sandalwood, the sandals. Hrīṁ, unbroken rice grains, the sandals.
Śrīṃ, the sandal of Vīrasma; Hsphreṃ, the sandal that fascinates all people.
Hsauṃ, the flower and sandals adorned with various parasols. Aiṃ, kusau, the sandals.
Thus ends the self-worship.
The invocation.

Within the mandala of Śrī Saṃvarta, the power of bliss is established through the successive stages; there is the most formidable fourfold emission according to the rule, another fivefold group pertaining to both Akula and Kula, and a sixfold group.
Then there are four, another fivefold group, and again four; this is that mandala.
Obeisance to that excellent Śrīkujeśa, who is the supreme Bhairava and by whom all is permeated.
I shall summon this; I summon.
Aiṃ Alūṃ, the sandals of the venerable Ādideva of the infinite maṇḍala.
The Three Deities.
Aiṃ, the sandals for Narāsanā; Aiṃ, the sandals for Mayūrāsanā.
Aiṃ, the sandal for the seat of the crucible.
Aiṁ Thrauṁ! To the goddess Dambhakī of Prastaradvīpa and the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa, [I offer] the sandals. The oblation.
Aiṁ Śrīṁ Hrīṁ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. The offering.
Aiṃ Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ, the sandals to Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara. Bali.
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the gesture of the staff-elephant with the index fingers.
Brahmāṇyā and others, Aśitāṅga and others.
Aiṃ, the sandals for the one seated upon a swan; the sandals for the one seated upon a bull.
The sandals for the peacock-throne; the sandals for the garuḍa-throne.
The sandals for the one seated upon the elephant; the sandals for the one seated upon the elephant.
The sandals for the seat of the pretas; the sandals for the seat of humans.
Hrāṃ Aṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Brahmāṇī and Aśitāṅgabhairava.
Hrāṃ Kaṃ, the sandal for Māheśvarī and Rurubhairava.
Hrāṃ Caṃ, to the Youthful One (Kumārī) and Caṇḍabhairava, the sandals!
Hrāṃ ṭaṃ, the sandals for Vaiṣṇavī Krodhabhairava.
Hrāṃ Taṃ! O Vārāhī, [offer] the sandals to Unmattabhairava.
Hrāṃ Paṃ, the pādukā for Indrāyaṇī Kapālīśa Bhairava.
Hrāṃ Yaṃ, [I offer] sandals to Cāmuṇḍā Bhīṣaṇabhairava.
Hrāṃ Śaṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Mahālakṣmī Saṃhārabhairava.
These are the offerings (bali).
The sandals of the goddess Śrī Rudracaṇḍā; the sandals of the goddess Śrī Pañcaṇḍā.
The sandals of the goddess Śrīcaṇḍogrā; the sandals of the goddess Śrīcaṇḍanāyikā.
The sandals of the goddess Śrīcaṇḍā; the sandals of the goddess Śrīcaṇḍavatī.
The sandal of the goddess Śrī Caṇḍarūpā; the sandal of the goddess Śrī Aticaṇḍikā.
The sacrificial offering.
Aṃ, the sandals of the goddess Brahmāṇī; Kaṃ, the sandals of the goddess Maheśvarī.
Caṃ, the sandals of the goddess Kaumāri; ṭaṃ, the sandals of the goddess Vaiṣṇavī.
To that Vārāhī Devī, the sandal; Paṃ, to Indrāṇī Devī, the sandal.
And the *pādukā* of the goddess Amuṇḍā; the auspicious *pādukā* of the goddess Mahālakṣmī.
This is the bali offering for them.
Aiṃ, salutation to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti). Salutation to the Seat of Ananta (Anantāsana).
Homage to the one whose seat is a bulbous root. Homage to the one whose seat is a seed. Homage to the one whose seat is a leaf.
Salutation to the one whose seat is the filaments. Salutation to the one whose seat is the pericarp. Salutation to the one whose seat is the lotus.
Salutation to the lion throne.
Now, meditation.
Aiṃ! [I bow to] the Goddess with eighteen arms, whose breasts and nipples are full, holding a skull-cup, a shield, a bell, a mirror, a threatening gesture, and a bow.
She holds a banner, a hand-drum, and a noose in her left hands,
as well as a sword, a spear, an arrow, a goad, and a terrifying thunderbolt.
Holding a mace, a spear, and a discus in her right hands,
she resembles ten million suns and is adorned with various ornaments.
Mounted upon a lion, the fierce vehicle of death, she bestows the fruits of all actions;
she is radiant with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, and a crown and diadem.
Having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess, who is adorned with all ornaments, saluted by all the gods, and who bestows the fruit of one's desired aims.
Thus ends the flower of meditative concentration; homage!
The triple añjali.
Aiṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hṛkṣmlvryūṃ Sṛkṣmlvryīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ. The sandals of the Goddess Jayatumbureśvarī. [Offer] the *bali* and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*).
Hrāṃ, obeisance to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṁ, for the armor, hūṃ. Hrauṁ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Hraḥ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
[Offer] invocation, water for the feet, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers; [say] "Namaḥ. One should display the yoni-mudrā.
Homage to the illustrious Nātha! Homage, repeated homage, to the illustrious Siddhinātha!
[Thus ends the Jayatumbeśvarī temple.]
Now, [the ritual] for Śikhāmahākāla Deguliya.

The worship of the sacrificial ground (thaṇḍila), the skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga) as the emblem, the ritual vase (kalaśa), the sacrificial ground, the boundary-line (khavālī), the heap of grain (lithupāṭa), and the bali offering.
Having sipped water with the threefold truth (tritatva).
Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the Self (ātmatattva). Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva). Hrūṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva).
Homage to the Guru.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the undivided, circle-like form which pervades all that is moving and unmoving.
Aiṃ! The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutation to that illustrious Guru.
Aiṃ. Salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the gurus who abide in the highest station.
Salutations to the supreme teachers and gurus. O Balisa, [I offer] the sandals to the lotus seat.
I place the sandals upon the tortoise-seat. Hraḥ! To the weapon, Phaṭ!
Aiṃ hūṃ phaṭ! To the diamond cage, svāhā!
Aiṃ, O Moving One, in the Unborn; O Unmoving One, in the Born! Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Hraḥ! Phaṭ to the weapon!
The purification of the hands.

Ṭhriṃ hrauṃ ṭhriṃ svāhā.
Hymn of Praise.
With devotion, I salute the heroic Divākara, the wielder of great power, who devours the darkness of the disease of conceptualizing worldly desires.
Here [are] the fragrance and so forth. Thus ends the water offering for the Sun.
Homage to the Guru. Meditation.
Seated upon a thousand-petaled lotus, white in color,
he holds the Guru’s Jñānamudrā and a book;
with his hands displaying the Varada and Abhaya gestures, he maintains the [appropriate] mudrās.
I worship the two-eyed one, who is delightful with white ornaments.
His body is surely embraced by one hand of his beloved, who is throbbing with redness on his left side,
as she holds a beautiful blue lotus and smiles upon her face.
And others always [meditate upon] the all-pervading one in the form of Bharga with another [mantra].
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Salutation to that venerable Guru who has revealed that state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—to that Śrī Guru, I offer salutations.
Aiṃ, salutations to the supreme gurus. Aiṃ, salutations to the pre-eminent gurus.
Aiṃ! Homage to the supreme teachers and gurus.
The sandals for Padmāsana. The bali offering.
The sandals for Kūrmāsana; the seat for Thavaka; the scattering of unbroken rice grains (akṣata) at the side.
Khphreṃ! O crusher of all enemies, to the abode of infinite power, for the weapon-mantra, Phaṭ! [I worship] the sandals.
Binding the face with the vajra-mudrā: KHPHREṂ HRŪṂ PHAṬ VAJRAPAÑJARE SVĀHĀ.
Touching the ten gates: KHPHREṂ CALAMAKULE KULAMACALE HRĪṂ HRŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
One should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma) with the root mantra.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the ṛṣi and other [constituent parts].

Oṃ. Of this Śrī Siddhilakṣmī Mālā-mantra, Īśvara is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the metre (chandaḥ), Śrī Siddhilakṣmī is the deity (devatā), HSKHPHREṂ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Svāhā is the power (śakti); its application (viniyoga) is for the sake of accomplishing all undertakings.
On the head: Salutation to the Seer Īśvara. On the mouth: Salutation to the Anuṣṭubh metre.
In the heart: Homage to the deity Śrī Siddhilakṣmī. At the mūlādhāra: Homage to the seed-syllable HSKHPHREṂ.
To the feet, svāhā; obeisance to Śakti. This is the application for the accomplishment of all purposes and goals.
Now follows the ritual placement on the hands (kara-nyāsa).
Khphreṃ! O you who crush all enemies, to the abode of infinite power, to the weapon-mantra, Phaṭ!
The purification of the hands.
Khphreṃ! To the abode of the power of omniscience, O Supreme Swan-like Goddess, salutations to both thumbs.
Khphreṃ! To the giver of the path to nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of satisfaction, salutation with the two index fingers.
Khphreṃ! Homage to the two middle [fingers], the abode of primordial awakening power that pacifies adverse calamities.
KH PHREṂ! To the abode of the independent power that crushes all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions, homage with the two ring fingers.
KH PHREṂ. To the one who is the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities, the abode of unimpeded power—to you, salutation with the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhā).
*Khphreṃ sakalaśatrupramathani anantaśaktidhāmne astrāya kalatalapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ.* Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the hands.
KHPHREṂ. Homage to all the Yoginīs of Accomplishment! The sandals of the Lord of the eastern face! PĀDUKĀM.
KH PHREṂ. Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment! The sandals of the Lord of the Southern Face! PĀDUKĀṂ.
Khphreṃ! Homage to the one who delights in eternally arisen bliss; the sandal of the Lord of the Northern Face.
KH PHREṂ! To the Mistress of the entire wheel of families, the Lord of the western face, [I offer] the sandals.
KH PHREṂ! To the Blessed Lady Candakāpālinī and the Lord of the upward-facing [face], the sandals!
Thus ends the placement upon the mouth.
The ritual placement on the limbs (aṅganyāsa), the heart, and meditation (dhyāna).
One should place the supreme goddess of the heart, whose entire body is white, who holds a noose and a goad, and who bestows the skull-bowl, the trident, fearlessness, and the boon.
Khphreṃ! O Supreme Swan-like Goddess, to the abode of the power of omniscience, homage to the heart!
Meditation by means of the channel.
One should place on the head the goddess Śirodevī, who is yellow in color, adorned with the previously mentioned weapons, endowed with all ornaments, and the bestower of success.
KH PHREṂ! To the giver of the path to nirvāṇa, the abode of the power of satisfaction, svāhā to the head!
Meditation on the crest-lock.
And upon the crest, one should install the goddess Śikhā, who is red, surrounded by her primary weapons,
the eternal Mīnākṣī, the bestower of tranquility, who is worshipped by the lords of heroes.
KH PHREṂ! To the crest-lock (śikhā), the pacifier of calamities and misfortunes, the abode of the power of primordial awakening—VAṢAT!
The meditation on armor.
One should place the slender Varmadevī, who is tawny-colored, adorned with weapons as before, wearing red garments, and uniquely honored by hosts of heroes.
KHPHREṂ! To the armor, the abode of the independent power that shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions—HŪṂ!
Meditation with the eyes.
One should place the eternal Netradevī, who is black in color, endowed with weapons,
and beautiful in all her limbs, upon the eyes.
KH PHREṂ! To the three eyes, which are the vessel of unimpeded power for crossing the ocean of all calamities, VAUṢAṬ!
Meditation through the weapon-mantra.

One should always perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon one's limbs of the mantra-deity, who has the luster of crystal and is surrounded by her weapons as before, for she bestows all desired objects.
KHPHREṂ! O crusher of all enemies, to the abode of infinite power, to the weapon-mantra PHAṬ!
Thus is the ritual placement upon the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the nine gates.
Then, meditation.
The goddess is accompanied by Hāṭakamañjuvarṇā; her central face is red, while the pair of faces on the left and right are yellow and white, beautiful to behold.
Her upper face is said to be black, most charming at its sides.
This pair of beautiful, red lotus-like faces, worthy of worship, was proclaimed by the illustrious Bhairava.
Above that, his face is described as most enchanting, variegated, and auspicious;
by its side, two other faces are known to be smoky-colored and extremely terrifying.
He likewise holds a serpent, a bell, a trident, another sword, and a skull-cup.
She beautifully bears upon her mountain-like form a skull-topped staff and a pair of hands displaying the gestures of granting boons and dispelling fear.
She is eternally captivating, holding in her lotus-like hands a variegated and beautiful bow, arrows, a great tree,
a mace, a tomara-weapon, a thick ploughshare, a pestle, a deer-horn, and a chowrie,
while her clusters of lotus-eyes are ever enchanting.
The slender woman, dwelling in the realm of the departed, was clothed like an elephant-skin and born from the mouth of a corpse.
Thus, salutation to Dhyānapuṣpa.
*Bhrūṃ* in the center; *Dyaṃ* in the heart; *Thāṃ* at the navel; *Uṃ* in the mouth; *Hrīṃ* in the left nostril.
HŪṂ in the right nostril; HĀṂ in the left eye; PHREṂ in the right eye; KṢOṂ in the left ear.
Kroṃ at the right ear.
Not on the penis; maḥ on the testicles.
Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the nine gates.
Now, the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma).
With the mantra "haṃ saḥ hsauṃ," one should offer the living person through the iḍā channel into the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra).
Then, having visualized the entire kaluṣa on the surface of the left armpit as black in color, one should contemplate it as being burnt away.
Again: *khphreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ* on the right arm.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Vaṭuka; [place this] on the left arm.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Durgā; [on] the right thigh.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣāṃ, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla; [place this] on the left thigh.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Paṃ, salutation to the Supreme Self (Paramātman); [at] the heart.
Having performed the purification of the hands with *ślīṃ paśuṃ hūṃ phaṭ*,
having made three sounds with the *tāla* gesture for the purpose of dispelling obstacles, and having performed the binding of the directions (*digbandha*) with *hūṃ phaṭ*,
[one should proceed] with the twelve long *praṇavas* from the *mūlādhāra* up to the *brahmarandhra*.
Having purified the channels,
the living consciousness residing in the heart is drawn up by means of this path.
Having uttered "Haṃ Saṃ," and having joined [the breath] at the dvādaśānta within the supreme radiance by means of the saṃghaṭamudrā, one should perform its protection with the Astra-mantra.
One should repeat the earth-syllable (*pṛthvībīja*) sixty times, visualizing it as situated in the earth from the feet up to the knees.

Having contemplated the water as dissolved [in the body] from the knees up to the crown of the head, one should repeat the syllable *hrīṃ* forty-eight times while focusing on the element of water (*ab-tattva*).
Having visualized [the deity] dissolved into the fire, one should visualize that the fire-element, the seed-syllable *hūṃ*, from the base up to the heart,
has dissolved by reciting it thirty-six times.
Having repeated the seed-syllable of air, *jyo*, from the heart up to the throat, one should contemplate it as dissolved into space.
Having repeated the seed-syllable "Hauṃ" twelve times from the throat up to the end of the sixteen [fingers], one should contemplate that one's own causal consciousness has dissolved.
Having dried the impurities within one's own body with the seed-syllable *yaṃ* (wind), burned them with the fire-seed-syllable *raṃ*,
and flooded them with the nectar-seed-syllable *vaṃ*, one should then increase the elements beginning with space (*ākāśa*)— each joined with its respective seed-syllable—
from twelve up to sixty-two in number, in reverse order, while reciting *haṃ*.

Having meditated upon the elements as having arisen from their respective causes— recalling the earth through the seed-syllable *laṃ*, the curvature through the seed-syllable *vaṃ*, and space through the seed-syllable *haṃ*— and having visualized one's own body as being purified of all sins from mind and body and recreated anew by merit, one should contemplate it as being of the nature of Śiva.

Reciting "I am the living consciousness" (jīvacaitanya so'ham) and with the mantra "I am the living swan" (jīvahaṃsa), one should lead [the soul] to its own place, the heart-lotus, and perform the installation of the vital breaths (praṇapratiṣṭhā).
Mantra: Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ haṃ saḥ. O Speech, Mind, Eyes, Ears, Tongue, Nose, Prāṇa, and Apāna of Paraśiva, having come here, remain happily for a long time, svāhā!
Perform the consecration of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhā) while reciting [the mantra] with the heart-mudrā.
Then follows the Mātṛkā-nyāsa. Of this, the venerable Mātṛkā-nyāsa:

Of this mantra for the placement (*nyāsa*) of the venerable Mātṛkā: Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the deity (*devatā*), the consonants are the seed-syllables (*bīja*), the collection of vowels is the power (*śakti*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purification of the body.
Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā. Oṃ, salutation to Gāyatrī. [To be placed] upon the tongue.
Oṃ, salutation to Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī. [At] the heart.
Oṃ aṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ, homage to the heart; [on] the two thumbs.
Oṃ iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ, svāhā to the head. [To be placed] on the two index fingers.
Oṃ uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). [This is for] the two middle fingers.
Oṃ eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ kavacāya hūṃ. [Recite] over the two ring fingers.
Oṃ oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; [this is for] the two little fingers.
Oṃ aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ astrāya phaṭ. [Recite] over the palms and backs of the hands.
Oṃ aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ, obeisance to the heart.
Oṃ i caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ, svāhā to the head.
Oṃ uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā).
Oṃ eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ, hūṃ for the armor.
Oṃ oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ vauṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Oṃ aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ astrāya phaṭ.
Having thus performed the placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa).
The meditation on the eight Mātṛkās.
In the foundation (ādhāra), the generative organ (liṅga), the navel, the heart-lotus, the root of the palate, and the forehead;
in the eight-petaled, sixteen-spoked, twenty-two-petaled, ten-petaled, twelve-petaled, and four-petaled [lotuses];
at the end of the abode (vāsānta), in the middle of the hair (bāla), and in the region of the throat accompanied by the letters ḍa, pha, ka, and ṭha, [one should place] the vowels.
I bow to the form of the letters situated on all the petals, which resound with meaningful sound. Having meditated thus:
Then follows the meditation on the external Mātṛkā.
Her body, consisting of face, hands, feet, belly, and chest, is composed of the fifty distinct letters;
she possesses a radiant matted lock adorned with a digit of the moon, and is as white as the moon or jasmine.

I bow to that Bhāratī, who holds a rosary and a water-pot, whose three eyes are adorned with decorative streaks, who rests upon a lotus, who possesses a rosary, and who is weighed down by the burden of her full breasts. Having meditated thus:
Aṃ on the forehead; Āṃ on the mouth; Iṃ and Īṃ on the eyes; Uṃ and Ūṃ on the two ears; Ṛṃ and Ṝṃ on the nostrils.
Ḷaṃ ḹṃ on the two cheeks; eṃ aiṃ on the two lips; oṃ auṃ on the upper and lower rows of teeth.
Aṃ on the head; aḥ on the face; kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ on the right arm.
Caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ña on the left arm; ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ on the right thigh.
Taṃ, thaṃ, daṃ, dhaṃ, naṃ on the left arm; paṃ, phaṃ on the sides; vaṃ on the back.
*Bhaṃ* at the navel; *maṃ* on the left side; *yaṃ* at the heart; *raṃ* on the right side; *laṃ* at the crown of the head.
Vaṃ on the left shoulder; Śaṃ from the heart to the right arm; Ṣaṃ from the heart to the right arm.
*Saṃ* at the heart and so forth, and *kṣa* at the left foot; *haṃ* at the heart and so forth, and *laṃ* in the stomach; *kṣaṃ* in the mouth. Thus is the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
O Goddess of the gods, whatever mantra one constantly recites without the ritual placement (nyāsa) is entirely fruitless for him; it would be as if one were making a deaf person hear.
Then one should begin the ritual placement (nyāsa).
The first placement of the six goddesses.
Meditation on the messenger from the heart.
Blue in color and extremely fierce, she stands in the dancing posture with one leg half-bent;
her hair is matted, she has three eyes, and she rests upon the heart of a corpse.
In her left hands she holds a skull-cup, a khaṭvāṅga staff, and a human head;
in her right hands she holds a plough; she has two arms and wears a tiger-skin garment.
