Aiṃ Hskhphreṃ! O Kālikāli, Mahākālī! Hrīṃ! O Goddess who feeds on flesh and blood! Hūṃ! O Goddess with red and black faces! Hrauṃ! Let my enemies see me! O Śrīhṛdayadūtī, the Goddess Kālikā, [worship] the venerable sandals!
The meditation on Śirodūtī.
Resembling the rising sun, she is short-statured, pot-bellied, and three-faced;
her limbs are adorned with jewels, serpents, and bones, and she is radiant with terrifying fangs.
She wears a garland of heads dripping with blood and is clothed in a tiger skin;
her faces are black, white, and red, and she possesses two eyes.
In the left hands, he holds a bow and a khaṭvāṅga, and with two [other] hands, he displays the mudrā born of yoga.

Aiṁ Aiṁ! Homage to the Blessed One, the Wicked Caṇḍālinī, who devours the blood and flesh of enemies, who carries a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff; slay, burn, vomit, cook! Hūṁ! Kill so-and-so! Seize!
Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā! O Śrī Duṣṭacaṇḍālinī, [reside] in the place of the head!
The venerable sandals.
The meditation on Śikhādūtī.
The best of practitioners should place the black form, born from the sword, with three eyes, upon a corpse-lotus; and Śikhādūtī, he should place in the crest-lock (śikhā).
Aiṃ Aghore Hrauṃ Aghore Hsphreṃ Ghoraṃ Tare Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Sarvataḥ Sarvasarve Hskhphreṃ!
Salutations to you, O you whose form is Rudra! Hsauṃ! To the venerable Śikhāsvanda at the station of the crest, [I offer] the venerable pādukā.
The meditation on Kavacadūtī.
Yellow in color, with five faces, fierce, dwarfish, and long-bellied, she stands upon a corpse; holding a sword, an arrow, a goad, a chisel, and the gesture of granting boons in her right hands,
and a fruit, a bow, a noose, and so forth, as well as the gesture of fear, in her left hands, O Sun.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ, O Uttoḷiyāsimadiyā, Hrīṃ, O Savapūhaviyavaṭiyā, Hrīṃ, O Diliyāsiulekhiyā, Hrīṃ,
O Sarvadulikhiyā Śrībherakhikā, [I worship] the venerable sandals at the station of the armor (kavaca).
The meditation on Netradūtī.
I shall describe Netradūtī, who is red in color and possesses a graceful form;
she holds a bow, an arrow, a trident, and a bell in her left and right hands respectively.
Aiṃ hūṃ Guhyakubjikā hūṃ phaṭ hrīṃ Rakte Mahāraktacāmuṇḍeśvarī aiṃ haṃ svāhā; [I worship] the Śrīpādukā of Raktacāmuṇḍā located in the place of the eyes.
The meditation on Astradūtī.
Deep red in color, she brandishes a vajra-khaṭvāṅga with her left hand and waves a vajra with her right; her hair is disheveled.
The Jina, clad in sky-clad nakedness, treads upon [the ground] while her feet are covered by a cloth;
her limbs are adorned with bone ornaments, and she is radiant with terrifying fangs.
She is always considered to be the three-eyed Guhyapratyaṅgirā.

Aiṁ hskhphreṁ śkhphreṁ hrāṁ hrīṁ hrūṁ! Strike down all those who have performed, caused to be performed, or will perform any affliction, such as the application of yantras, mantras, or powders— O Draṣṭrākarālī hrāṁ hrīṁ hrūṁ hlauṁ hlaiṁ ślīṁ Guhyakubjikā, O Astradūtī Guhyakubjikā, [I worship] the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā)!
Thus ends the Ugraṣaṅka.
Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six Ḍākinīs.
The meditation on the ḍākinīs.
In the throat-cavity, within the Viśuddhi cakra which is a lotus of eight petals, one should meditate on her who is red in color, three-eyed, and holding a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga),
a skull-cup, a trident, and a great hide;
she is endowed with a single face, strikes fear into the ignorant, and is not attached to skin or bone.
I pay homage to Ḍākinī, who is worthy of worship by means of seed-syllables, her body surrounded by Mṛtā and the other goddesses.
Aiṃ ḍāṃ ḍīṃ ḍūṃ ḍmlvryūṃ! O Ḍākinī, protect me; protect my skin-element;
O you who bring all beings under control, [protect] the Śrī-pādukā. [This is for] the venerable Vāyavyā.
The meditation on Rākiṇī.

In the heart-lotus with twelve petals, one should meditate on Kālarātri, who is dark-complexioned, has three eyes, and possesses two faces adorned with fangs; she holds a rosary, a trident, a skull-cup, and a hand-drum in her arms, stands upon blood, and is surrounded by [her attendants] such as Praśaktā, whom she favors through pure devotion.
Meditate upon that Dākini, who is worshipped by the illustrious Vīrendras and who bestows desired fruits.
Aiṃ Rāṃ Rīṃ Rūṃ Rmlvryūṃ! O Rākinī, protect me; protect my blood-element!
O you who cause all beings to come together, [protect] the Śrī-pādukā! [Place it] in the heart.
The meditation on Lākinī.

At the navel, upon a lotus of the directions and intermediate points, one should meditate on the Great Fierce Śakti, black in color, possessing three eyes and three faces, holding in her hands the trident, the skull-bowl, the goad, and the gesture of fearlessness;
she is surrounded by Ḍāmari and the others, bestows fear upon the ignorant folk, and is the sole Mistress of the elements of purification.
At the end of the Gauda region, one should meditate upon that Lākinī, whose mind is attached [to the center] and who bestows all happiness.
Aiṃ lāṃ līṃ lūṃ lmlvryūṃ! O Lākinī, protect me; protect my marrow;
O you who bring all beings under control, [protect] the venerable sandals at the navel.
The meditation on Kākinī.
In the lotus called Svādhiṣṭhāna, which shines with six petals, she has four faces and three eyes;

she is yellow in luster, holds a trident, a rosary, and the letter *Ka* in her hands, as well as the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness; she is established in the fat-element (*medas*), delighted by the pride of her enemies, and is the primordial source (*bandhinī*) existing from before.
One should meditate upon that Kākinī, who is yellow, adorned with a garland of lotuses, and bestows desired fruits.
Aiṃ Kāṃ Kīṃ Kūṃ Kmlvryūṃ! O Kākinī, protect my *māṃsa* (flesh) element; protect my *medas* (fat) element!
O you who bring all beings under control, [I worship] the venerable *pādukā* upon the *liṅga*.
The meditation on the *sākinī*.

In the lotus situated at the *mūlādhāra*, which is adorned with petals representing the Vedas, one should meditate upon her who has five faces and three eyes, who is golden-hued and seated upon a skeleton, and who, with her long, graceful arms, holds a trident, a lotus, a book, and the gesture of wisdom (*jñānamudrā*), as well as displaying the beautiful gestures of granting boons and fearlessness— she who is truly enchanting.
One should meditate upon that Ḍākinī, whose mind is attached to food offered with ritual gestures (mudrā) and who is delighted by the intoxication of honey.
Aiṃ Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ Smlvyūṃ! O Sākinī, protect me; protect my bone-element, O you who bring all beings under control, the venerable Sandal! [Abide] in the Foundation (ādhāra).
The meditation on Hākinī is as follows:
in the middle of the eyebrows, upon a two-petalled lotus of radiant white at the location of the *bindu*, she is white in color;
she holds a lotus of digits, the gesture of knowledge (*jñānamudrā*), a hand-drum (*ḍamaruka*), a lotus, a rosary, and a skull-cup.

One should meditate upon Hākinī, who has six faces, resides in the marrow, is adorned with three eyes, is joined with Haṃsavatī and others, is intent on yellow-colored food, and is praised by all the gods.
Aiṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ hmlvryūṃ! O Hākinī, protect me; protect my marrow-element, O Śrīpādukā who brings all beings under control! [To be placed] between the eyebrows.
The meditation of Yākinī.

Within the lotus situated in the hollow of the shaven head, endowed with all its petals, [I worship] that Bhairavī Yākinī, who possesses all weapons, whose limbs shine with splendor, who is the source of all colors,
who has faces beginning with the letter *Ḍa*, who bestows all happiness, and whose very nature is the essence of all elements.
One should meditate upon her who has a mind attached to all food, who is adorned by the grace of the Supreme Śiva, and who possesses every form.
Aiṃ yāṃ yīṃ yūṃ ymlvryūṃ! O Yākinī, protect me; protect my white constituent (semen); O you who bring all beings under control, [protect] the venerable sandals.
In the thousand-petaled lotus at the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra).
Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six Ḍākinīs.
Then follows the placement (nyāsa) of the eight Mothers (aṣṭamātṛkā).
Meditative absorption.
Holding a staff, a water-pot, and then a rosary and the gesture of fearlessness, Brāhmī has the luster of gold and wears a black antelope skin as an upper garment.
Aiṃ! In the sacred field of Prayāga, aṃ Aśitāṅgabhairava and āṃ Brahmāyaṇī Ambā—[I worship] the venerable sandals.
On the head.
Meditative absorption.
Carrying a trident, an axe, a small drum, and a human skull,
the auspicious Māheśvarī, white as snow, should be meditated upon.
Aiṃ! In the sacred field of Vārāṇasī, Kaṃ Ru Ru Bhairava and Kāṃ Māheśvarī Ambā—[I worship] the sandals [of these deities]. Meditation on the face.
Holding a goad, a staff, a khaṭvāṅga, and a noose in her hands, Kaumārī,
who resembles the bandhūka flower and bestows all desires, should be meditated upon.
Aiṃ! In the sacred field of Kolāgiri, Caṃ Caṇḍabhairava and Caṃ Kaumārī Ambā—[I worship] the sandals [of these deities]. Karṇa.
Meditative absorption.
Holding a discus, a bell, a skull-cup, and a conch in her hands, Vaiṣṇavī— dark as the tamāla tree and radiant with grace— is to be meditated upon.
Aiṃ! In the sacred field of Aṭṭahāsa, Ṭaṃ Krodhabhairava and Ṭāṃ Nārāyaṇī Ambā—[I worship] the sandals [of these deities] in the heart.
Meditative absorption.
Vārāhī, possessing the luster of a dark rain cloud, should be meditated upon with four hands holding a pestle, a sword, a shield, and a plough.
Aiṁ! In the field of Jayantī, [I worship] Him, Unmattabhairava; Her, Ambā Vārāhī—the Pādukā. [In the navel.]
Meditative absorption.
Holding a goad, a lotus, a mantra, and a vajra in her hands,
Indrāṇī, who resembles a sapphire, should be meditated upon as the bestower of all prosperity.
Oṃ, at the sacred field of conduct (caritrakṣetra), [I worship] the sandals of Paṃ Kapālīśabhairava and Pāṃ Śakrārī Ambā.
In the Svādhiṣṭhāna [cakra].
Meditative absorption.
Cāmuṇḍā, whose body is red and who is adorned with a garland of severed heads, should be meditated upon as holding a trident, a sword, a human head, and a skull-cup in her hands.
Aiṃ! In the sacred field of Ekāmra, I worship the sandals of Yaṃ Bhīṣaṇabhairava and Yāṃ Ambā Cāmuṇḍā.
In the support.
Meditative absorption.
Holding a rosary of beads, a seed-vessel, a skull, and a lotus in her hands,
Mahālakṣmī is described as being white like snow.
Aiṃ! In the sacred field of Devīkoṭa, obeisance to the sandals of Śaṃ Saṃhārabhairava and Śāṃ Mahālakṣmī Ambā.
At the feet. Thus is the placement of the eight Mātṛkās.
Khphreṃ, having recollected with suspended breath.

One should conceive of the state of Brahmā through the form of the Root Goddess (Āmūladevī), the state of Viṣṇu through the subtle [form], and the state of Rudra through the supreme [form]. Having thus generated the form by means of the Self, one should bring the Self— which is supreme bliss— into that form by means of inhalation (pūraka).
Having fixed [the breath] in the heart by means of *kumbhaka*, one should perform the sixfold deposition (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*). Therein, first:
The first sequence of placement on the left side.
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon the Goddess who assumes the form of one's desire, four-armed,
possessing a gentle form, and likewise assuming all forms.
The goddess is yellow in color, holding a lotus and a conch, endowed with a book, a rosary, and a garland;
she bears all weapons and is the shatterer of all magical diagrams.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, Ofeet of the Lord, at the aperture of Brahmā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, at the feet of Mother Mahālakṣmī; at the location of the Bindu.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, O Mother Vyomavāmeśvarī, [worship] the feet; [place Hrīṃ Śrīṃ] in the left eye.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the feet of Ambā Kṣacarī are in the left nostril.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, O Ambā Dikcarī, [worship] at the feet and in the mouth.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the feet of the Mother Gocarī; [this is] on the right nostril.
Hrīṃ, Ambā Bhūcarī, at the feet; [Hrīṃ], at the right eye.
Thus ends the first leftward sequence.
Now follows the gross assignment (sthūlanyāsa).
Meditative concentration.
That goddess, however, is in the form of sound (nāda), following upwards through the piṅgalā;
she is smokeless, like the essence [of light], peaceful, and established in the half.
Subtle, in the form of a lamp-flame, consisting of the nature of desire, and stainless;
the Goddess holds a sword and a shield, with her lotus-hands granting boons and fearlessness.
She, whose nature is truth, consciousness, and bliss, should be meditated upon as the bestower of all prosperity;
she resides in the center between the Suṣumnā and the Iḍā, arising from the splendor of Śiva.
Mounted upon the Resounding One, she follows after the mouth of Śiva;
O fair-faced one, she who is nameless has been explained by means of millions of names.
Having understood yoga to be of such a nature, one should thereafter perform worship externally.

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khaṃ in the heart; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Phreṃ in the throat; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Raṃ in the palate; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Eṃ in the two eyebrows; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Maṃ in the skin of the remainder—thus is the group of five on the left.
Now follows the placement of the twelve knots (granthidvādaśakanyāsa).
Meditative absorption.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! [I worship] the Goddess who possesses the luster of ten million full moons, who has five faces and wears a crown;
she is like the jasmine and the moon, with a radiance equal to a mass of milk.
The goddess on the right is known as Nāsikā, and the one on the left is Aśitasaṃnibhā;
the one in the west is Lohitā, and [the one in the front] is like pure crystal.
Endowed with fifteen eyes, resembling a solar disc,
with matted locks bound in a crown and a crescent moon serving as his crest-ornament.
Adorned with various jewels, her own gold, bone ornaments, earrings, necklaces, and anklets; graced by the tinkling sound of her girdle and feet, she wears a garland of the buds of the Daitya tree.
With a slight smile and a protruding tongue, her face was radiant with blazing fangs;
she was clothed in garments like a network of tinkling bells, and her small bells resounded beautifully.
The Supreme Goddess, adorned and clad in a tiger skin.
O Great Goddess, you hold [the weapons] in both your left and right hands.
In her right hands, the auspicious one holds an excellent trident with three prongs and a severed head;
in her left hands, she holds a water-pot, a noose, and a bell.
Seated upon the throne of Kālarudra, he is fierce, with one face and four arms;
he has three eyes, with terrible red eyes, and is well-established in the vīrāsana posture.
With her hands adorned by the *kattika*, the skull-bowl, the *ḍamaru* drum, and the trident,
she is thus seated upon the throne of Rudra, the exceedingly radiant Goddess Siddhilakṣmī.
Having meditated upon the Great Goddess Siddhilakṣmī, who is surrounded by garlands of flames, situated in the midst of the circle of Mothers, and the bestower of all accomplished aims.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Khphreṃ at the center of the eyebrows; Oṃ namaḥ sarvasiddhiyoginībhyaḥ at the throat.
Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment! [At the heart. Homage to her who is delighted by eternally arisen bliss! [At the navel.]
To the mistress of the entire wheel of families.
In the secret place: to the Blessed One Caṇḍakāpālinī. In the molasses: [to her].
Taṃ at the navel; dyaṃ at the heart; thāṃ at the end of the twelve [fingers]. This is the first section on the Mother (Mātṛkhaṇḍa).
Khphreṃ at the place of Brahmā; Hrīṃ at the left eye; Hūṃ at the right eye; Hāṃ at the left ear.
Phreṃ on the right ear; Kṣāṃ on the left nostril; Na on the mouth; Maḥ on the crest-lock.
The second section on hemorrhoids.
Khphreṃ Parahaṃsinī: at the aperture of Brahmā; bestower of the path to nirvāṇa; at the tip of the nose.
The pacifier of calamities arising from adversity; the palate; the destroyer of all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions.
On the head: O boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities. On the neck: O crusher of all enemies. On the chest: [O you who possess the mark of the Śrīvatsa].
O Goddess, come! [Enter] the heart! Laugh! [Enter] the navel! [Enter] the heart!
O consumer of human blood, entrails, and fat! O crusher of my own enemies! (Recite three times).
*Khāhi* (Eat! [at] the shanks; *Chindi* (Cut! [at] the genitals; *Khaḍgaṇa tāḍaya* (Strike with the sword! [at] the feet.
"May she cut [them] off at the two big toes. Thus ends the sixteen supports. "Until you fulfill all my desires," [at] the feet. "The supreme accomplisher," at the knees.
O Blessed One, who assumes the form of Mahābhairava; O you who are saluted by the best of the thirty gods; O you who are upon the two thighs.
O Secret One! O Mother of all mantras! [Salutation] at the navel. O You who are affectionate toward those who bow before You! [Salutation] at the heart.

O Goddess Mahākālī! [Be present] in the pit of the throat; O destroyer of Kāla, in the mouth! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Be gracious to her who is afflicted by passion! In the ears: act! In the eyes: [be present as] the daughter of the gods and demons! In the head!
Thus, in the twelve knots.
Now follows the nine-syllable placement according to the sequence of the staff (daṇḍakrama).
Meditative absorption.
Resplendent like ten million moons, resembling a snow-bank or the moon,
she is clothed in white garments, possesses nine faces, and has three eyes on each.
The goddess has eighteen arms and dark, curly hair;
she possesses her own natural form, a beautiful complexion, and full, elevated breasts.
She was beautiful with three folds like waves, possessed long and tremulous eyes,
a neck like a conch shell, lips red as the *bimba* fruit, and was a young woman of lovely smiles.
With all her limbs perfectly complete, marked by the hundreds of auspicious signs,
adorned with white flowers, and anointed with white camphor.
Pierced by the arrows of Kandarpa, situated in the midst of the lunar disc,
adorned with various ornaments, and wearing a serpent as a sacred thread.
The goddess, whose face is filled with betel, who smiles with the brilliance of lightning,
who bestows boons and protection, and whose hands are filled with nectar;
Holding with both hands the beautiful skull-bowl born of the house,
he carries the sword in his right hand and the skull-cup in his left hand.
In the right hand he holds a trident, and likewise a goad in the other;
in his left hand he holds the moon, and in his right hand the sun.
In her right hand is an arrow, and in her left is established a bow;
in her right hand is a conch, while in her left hangs a severed head.
In the left hand a mirror, and in the right a staff;
in the right hand a vajra, and in the left a bell of great sound.
One should contemplate her as possessing these mudrās, with a gentle form,
bearing such a countenance, the goddess well-seated upon a lotus throne.
And a lotus, very white and adorned with eight petals,
as well as a preta in the form of Sadāśiva, having three eyes and four arms.
With two arms dancing, two hands like lotus feet,
holding tridents in his two hands, and adorned with all ornaments.
Upon the back of a lotus, one should visualize the goddess Varṇā, the King of Pretas;
she is celebrated as that supreme goddess, the Fortune of Accomplishment (Siddhilakṣmī).
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Hrīṃ at the aperture of Brahmā; Śrīṃ at the point (bindu); Hūṃ at the face; Phaṭ at the heart; Phaṭ at the six seats (ṣaḍādhāra).
Phaṭ at the navel; Svā at the private parts.
Alas, my molasses!
Thus is the placement of the nine syllables according to the sequence of the staff.
Now follows the ritual placement of the five faces (pañcavaktranyāsa).
Meditative concentration.
And one should visualize the Preta situated within the pericarp, with the Goddesses positioned above him,
endowed with ten arms each and possessing five faces each.
Sixty-three eyes, resembling pure crystal,
with a form like jasmine or the moon, adorned with necklaces and armlets.
O fair-faced one, the trident, the gesture of granting boons, the bell, the axe,
and the skull-topped staff are said to be the weapons held in the left arms.
An elephant goad, the gesture of fearlessness, a shaven head, a sword, and a bowl—
these are the weapons held in the right hands for the purpose of slaying the Danujas.
One should meditate on that form situated within oneself and establish it at the end of the pericarp.
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Siddhi-yoginīs! The sandals of the Lord of the upward-facing mouth! Pādukāṃ!
Khphreṃ! Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment; the sandals of the Lord of the Eastern Face.
Khphreṃ! Homage to the eternally arisen bliss, the one who causes joy; to the Lord of the southern face, the venerable sandals!
KH PHREṂ: To the Mistress of the entire wheel of families, the Lord of the northern face, the venerable sandals!
KPHREṂ, to the Blessed One Caṇḍakāpālinī, the Lord of the Western Face, [I pay homage to] the venerable sandals.
Thus ends the ritual placement of the five faces.
Now follows the six-limbed ritual placement (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
Meditation on the heart.
Resembling the flower of the pomegranate tree, the heart-deity is worshipped by the gods;
the auspicious goddess holds a staff, a noose, a dot, and a skull-cup.
KH PHREṂ Paramahaṃsinī, Obeisance to the Sandals of the Heart-Lord, the Power of Omniscience.
Meditation by means of the channel.
The auspicious goddess Śirā is moon-colored, with hands in the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness;
likewise, she holds a sword and a shield, and bears a severed head and a trident.
Khphreṃ! O Giver of the Path to Nirvāṇa, O Eternal One, O Power of Satiety, O Lord upon the Head, [I worship] the Śrīpādukā.
Meditation on the crest-lock.
The goddess with the beautiful face, whose entire body is as dark-blue as the tamāla tree,
and who is praised by heroes, carries a mūśala and likewise a bell in her hand.
Khphreṃ! O Śikhānātha, who pacifies adverse calamities and possesses primordial awakening, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
The meditation on armor.
The highly fortunate Varmadevī, whose limbs possess the luster of white and red,
bears a serpent-noose, a plow, a thunderbolt, and a pestle.
Khphreṃ! O destroyer of all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions, whose speech is like the moon of sovereignty; meditate with the eyes upon the venerable *pādukā*.
Netradevī is consciousness-bliss, endowed with a smoky color;
she has two arms, wears yellow garments, and holds a small knife and a skull-cup.
Khphreṃ! The venerable sandals of the Lord of the Eye, the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities, whose power is never lost.
Meditation through the weapon-mantra.
I constantly worship the Goddess Astra, who possesses both white and black forms,
and who further holds a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), a bell, and a trident.
Khphreṃ! O crusher of all enemies, O infinite power, O Lord of Weapons, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
Thus concludes the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
Now follows the second [part], the gross placement (sthūlanyāsa).
Meditative absorption.
I meditate upon the supreme Goddess, who has lotus-eyes and a moon-like face, who holds in her lotus-hands the gestures of fearlessness and boon-granting, as well as a noose, a mace, a water-pot,
a skull-topped staff, a lotus, a mallet, a rosary, and a vessel; she is radiant like a hibiscus flower and is seated upon a lotus throne.
I pay homage to her who is worshipped by the liberated ones, praised by sages, and illuminated by three eyes.
O Goddess, come, O Śrī Varadanātha! Laugh, O Śrī Abhayanātha! O you who are not to be disregarded by men!
The venerable one who holds a jar in her right hand; at the left joint, she who devours human blood, entrails, and fat.
The sandals of Kapālanātha [are placed] on the left arm: "Crusher of my own enemies!"
At the feet of Khaṭvāṅganātha: Khāhi khāhi! At the feet of Muṇḍanātha!
On the right shoulder: O Lord of the Trident, pierce with the trident the sandals!
Cut [it], O Ankushanatha; at the right joint. Strike with the sword, O Khadganatha;
at the right wrist. Sever, O Pashanatha; at the palm of the right hand.
Thus ends the second [section], the gross placement (sthūlanyāsa).
Now begins the third [section], the subtle placement (sūkṣmanyāsa).
Meditative absorption.
The goddess, assuming illusory forms, is adorned with various garlands and ornaments;
the goddess bears all weapons and is resplendent with every kind of jewelry.
She has many faces, many arms, and many feet;
she is possessed of great strength, is the universal form, the Great Goddess, and has dark, curly hair upon her head.
Or one may visualize Mahālakṣmī in whatever form is desired, resembling her in appearance.
Or [one proceeds] from the forehead and so forth in a leftward sequence.
KHPHREṂ at the forehead; HRĪṂ at the eyes; HŪṂ at the cheeks; HĀṂ at the shoulders; KṢAUṂ at the arms.
*Kroṃ* on the fingers; *namaḥ* on the sides; *pratyaṅgire* on the thighs; *mahārāve* on the shanks.
Mahāśaṅkhā is at the feet; Vivipānā is at the toes of the feet; Haḍḍā and Maḍḍā are at the toes of the right foot; Macālinī is at the two feet; Mahākālī is at the shanks.
In the desire realm, [the lifespan] is vast; in the first [heaven] and the others on the sides, it is as follows: in the Knot, the Destroyer, and the Fingers, it is [one kalpa].
He causes extreme distress; he seizes him by the arm.

Indeed, *yau* is on the shoulder of Bhairika; *manova* is on the throat; *karma* is on the cheek of the face of Pratyaṅgirā; *ni* is on the eye of Nivajrasarja; *khphreṃ* is on the spinal column; *hrīṃ* is on the waist; and *hūṃ* is on the foundation (*ādhāra*).
Hāṃ at Svādhiṣṭhāna; Khphreṃ at Maṇipūraka; Kṣoṃ at Anāhata; Kroṃ at Viśuddhi.
Not at the place of the command; *maḥ* at the tip of the nose. Thus is the third subtle placement (*sūkṣmanyāsa*).
Next follows the placement of the supreme division.
Meditative absorption.
Behold her with one face, three eyes, and four arms,
white as snow, jasmine, and the moon, seated upon a corpse.
Holding a noose and a sword, with a lotus and a sharp arrow raised in her hands,
the Great Goddess is to be worshipped in due order in the location of the Bindu.
Khphreṃ at the foundation (ādhāra); Sphaṃ at the unstruck (anāhata); Maṃ at Tārūṇī; Hāṃ at the point (bindu); Caṃ at the half-moon (ardhacandra).
Ḍaṃ in Nāda; Yoṃ in Nirodhikā; Geṃ in Vyāpinī; Śvaṃ in Samanā.
Rikula-kure || Sphaṭ to Manonmanī || Vrīṃ to Unmanī || Sphaṭ to Śāmbhavānta ||
Ḍīṃ hrīṃ at the end of the sixteen; sphaṭ at the end of the subtle; vrīṃ at the end of the supreme; phaṭ in Kula.
Thus is the sequential placement upon another.
Now follows the secondary placement (paranyāsa) according to the sequence of the tonsured (muṇḍakrama).
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon her who is fierce, supreme, and terrifying, red-black and fearsome; whose limbs are mounted by a corpse, naked as the directions, and with a distorted face.
Her hair is tawny in color and bound with a skull as a crown;
she has eighteen arms, is formidable, possesses five faces, and has a slender waist.
The Goddess, assuming various forms, adorned with various weapons in her hands,
seated upon a red lotus, and endowed with two hearts.
In the center, one should meditate upon the goddess Kṛśodarī, the bestower of all accomplishments,
whose two hands are bound and hanging down to her ears.
In the left [hands], there is a skull-cup, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a staff, and likewise a bell; as well as a noose, a lotus, a shield, and the gesture of fearlessness.
In the right [hands], he holds a sword, a trident, a goad, and a thunderbolt;
likewise, a spear, a human skull, a mallet, and the gesture of granting boons.
Adorned with all ornaments and wearing a serpent as a sacred thread.
Thus concludes the section on meditation.
*Khphreṃ* at the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*); *Sphaṭ* on the skin at the end [of the spine]; *Maṃ* at the tip of the nose; *Hāṃ* at the *bindu*; *Caṃ* at the navel;
*Ḍaṃ* in the left ear; *Yāṃ* in the right ear; *Geṃ* in the left eye; *Śveṃ* in the right eye.
Riṃ in the left nostril; sphaṭ in the right nostril; vrīṃ in the left cheek.
*Sphaṭ* on the right cheek; *ḍvrīṃ* on the mouth; *sphaṭ* on the tongue; *rvrīṃ* on the teeth.
*Phaṭ* at the crest-lock. Thus ends the fourth supreme ritual deposition (*nyāsa*) according to the sequence of the *Muṇḍa*.
Now follows the nyāsa of the eight goddesses of the skin (tvag-aṣṭaka).
Meditative absorption.
The goddess has one face and eight arms, her form identical to that of the principal deity;
she is established upon the spokes of the wheel and holds a skull-cup and a goad.
Holding aloft in her hands a sword, a skull-topped staff, a heart-lotus, a severed head, and a trident, she has a great hand-drum; she possesses three eyes that resemble fire.
Or rather, what more shall I describe? The Goddess is manifest in her true form.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals of Ḍambaranātha and the Mother Brahmāṇī; [this is] on the skin, at the end.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O feet of the Lord born from the lotus, Māheśvarī Ambā, [rest] upon the red [lotus].
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, at the feet of the Mother Kaumārī, the Mistress of the Sky; in the flesh.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, at the feet of Śambhunātha, Ambā Vaiṣṇavī, [at] Medani.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! At the feet of Nīlāmbaranātha and Ambā Vārāhī: [the offering of] bones.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, O feet of the Mother Indrī, the Lord of the Gods (Aiṃ), [I] bathe you.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Khecaranātha, O Mother Cāmuṇḍā, [I bow at] your feet!
In the marrow.
KHPHREṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ, O Lord Saṃdhāyugeśvarīnātha, Mother Mahālakṣmī, at the feet; at the hair. Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the eight limbs.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the eight Yamalas.
Meditative absorption.
She has one face and six arms, with Mṛtīśvarī seated upon her left thigh;
she is as white as camphor and kunda flowers, adorned with all ornaments.
Seated within the mandala, he is served, holding a trident, a lotus, the gesture of fearlessness, and a conch.
His hand holds the digit of the new moon and is adorned with a pure pearl necklace.
Aruṇavarṇāmṛtā is Lakṣmī, who has one face and three eyes,
four arms, holds a conch, and carries a blue lotus and nectar.
Beholding the face of the God, she who holds the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness in her hands,
who is complete with all auspicious marks, and adorned with every ornament.
Thus they meditate by which all misfortunes are destroyed.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Ajinanātha; on the right foot: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Ānandāmbā.
Left foot: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Īpānātha. Right calf: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Īśvarī Ambā. Left calf: [Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Īśvarī Ambā].

Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Udayanātha; on the right thigh. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Ūrddhvagāminī Ambā; on the left thigh. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Ṛddhinātha; on the right side. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Mṛti Ambā; on the left side. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of Luptadevanātha; on the right hand.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ ḹ luṃ, the feet of the Lord and the Mother; Oṃ juṃ saḥ, the feet of the sole-limbed Lord (Ekāṅganātha).
On the right arm: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, at the feet of the mother Airāvatī. On the left arm: Oṃ juṃ saḥ, at the feet of Oghanānandanātha. On the right shoulder: Oṃ juṃ saḥ au, at the feet of the mother Kalālī.
On the left shoulder: Oṃ juṃ saḥ aṃ, feet of Amuranātha; kukudi. Oṃ juṃ saḥ aḥ, feet of Kṛśānu Ambā; hṛti. [Thus the sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa) is completed.]
Prajāpati is the seer (ṛṣi) of this mantra; Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas); Śrīsiddhilakṣmī is the deity (devatā);
its application (viniyoga) is for the recitation (japa) for the sake of accomplishing all aims.
Oṃ aṃ aṃ, salutation to the two thumbs. Hrīṃ taṃ taṃ, salutation to the two index fingers.
Hūṃ maṃ maṃ madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | Hāṃ naṃ naṃ naṃ anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
Phreṃ kaṃ kaṃ, salutation to the two little fingers. Kṣoṃ kaṃ kaṃ, salutation to the backs of both hands. Kroṃ, salutation to the left wrists and joints.
Homage to those bound at the right wrist; *vauṣaṭ*! [To the one] bound at the right wrist.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. One should clap the hands. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the nine gates.
Meditative absorption.

May that goddess, whose body is radiant with saffron, whose face is like the moon, and who has arisen from her nine mouths, be victorious; of those, her first face is full and plump, while the pair at its sides is one resembling a jasmine flower,
another smoky-grey, and yet another blue, situated above them.
The practitioner should always meditate on her whose complexion is like that of the kokaṇada flower and who possesses a heart of compassion.
One face is brownish-yellow, another has a pale-red luster,
and the third is described as a charming green color.
In her hands she holds a mace, a mountain, a beautiful bell, a mirror, a noose, a mallet, a spear, a long pestle, a severed head, and likewise a trident;
a shining sword, a beautiful shield, a *kāca* fruit, and a fly-whisk.
I worship her who holds joy, who displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and who wields a chisel and a raised index finger.

The Goddess, who dwells eternally within the bodies of the departed, whose face is smiling, who is radiant with various beautiful ornaments, whose limbs are delicate, whose eyes are like full-blown lotuses, who wears a human skin as her garment,
is intent on crushing the hosts of trembling Dānavas and is praised by the multitudes of world-protectors.
May she, the mistress of the house, who possesses beautiful lips, always protect the people from the distant past.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Oṃ at the aperture of Brahmā; Hrīṃ in the circle of the face; Hūṃ at the right ear; Hāṃ at the left ear.
Phreṃ at the root of the tongue; Kṣoṃ at the heart; Kroṃ at the penis; Namaḥ at the secret circle.
Thus concludes the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the nine gates.
Now follows the placement [of mantras] on the mouth and other parts.
Meditative absorption.
I bow to the goddess Pītagaurīśvarī, who delights in her massive body,
who emanates from the nine faces, and who is intensely intent on the salvation of the universe.
She bears seven circular eyes;
her primary face, according to its name, possesses a radiance equal to yellow and reddish-brown.
The first face, possessing a divine form, is the source of all accomplishments;
on both its sides is Rāvaṇa, the Daitya who is unbearable to others.
The second face on the right is of most wonderful form;
it resembles the stainless sky, like the sky filled with a multitude of rising stars.
One should contemplate the utter destruction of the hosts of Daityas— terrible, formidable, and supreme—
as the union of the highest state, most intensely fierce.
In brief, the subsequent [section] consists of Parabhāva, Vaktrasa,
Unnata, Karāla, Gahana, and Māhāsura-nipātana.
One should terrify all obstacles with the subsequent [mantra] Vikarālaka,
which possesses great power through the Kaula practice and is overwhelmed with the bliss of wine.
One should withdraw the face of the ten directions, as well as the right and the northern faces;
one should withdraw the supreme face of Mahocchuṣma, which arises from the causal source.
The fierce upper face roars loudly and intensely;
one should cause the lower [face] to resound above and below, which is considered the dissolution of sound and non-sound.
The right face constantly utters a loud roar, which is difficult to obtain;
it enters into all desires for one who is devoted to the one whose banner is the sea-monster (Kāmadeva).
The northern face, which eternally grants all desires, is divine;
she is endowed with celestial ornaments and adorned with various decorations.
She is endowed with eighteen arms and adorned with various ornaments;
she holds a mace, a tree, a javelin, and likewise a mountain.
In her right hands, she holds a bell joined with a mirror, an arrow, a deer,
a noose joined with a mace, and a trident.

She is joined with a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga) on her left, holding a sword and a shield; she is described as being endowed with a skull-bowl for libation and the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya).
Endowed with all the auspicious marks, adorned with various garlands of flowers,
wearing a tiger-skin girdle, seated upon a corpse,
she is the goddess who bestows accomplishment and supernatural powers, accompanied by the great wheel.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Oṃ, crush and devour my own enemies! Homage to the mouths of the root [deities].
Hrīṃ! Pierce and cut with the trident! Homage to the southern faces!
HŪṂ! Strike with the sword! Cut! Homage to Karavaktra and those on the right!
Hāṃ! O Bhāvanāmukha, fulfill all my desires this very day!
Homage to the Northern Faces! Phreṃ! O Supreme Compassionate One, O Blessed Lady who assumes the form of Mahābhairava, O Northern Face, homage to the sandals of Kālānala! Homage!
KṢOṂ: Salutation to the faces of the *Sakaramantramātā*, the *Kaulottara*, and the [faces] of the East and South, O you who are praised by the thirty-three gods.
Kroṃ! O Goddess of great and fierce countenance, who is as compassionate toward those who bow before you as a mother is to her child; homage to you, the Northern One.
Homage to Mahākālī, the destroyer of Kāla; homage to those with faces that utter the sound "phaṭ" from the right.

Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Make me, who am afflicted by passion, gracious; [I bow] to Makaranda at the mouths of the deities of the gods and asuras. Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the emergence of the faces.
Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
Meditation on the heart.
I worship the Goddess in my heart, who resembles saffron in hue, whose eyes are like darting wagtails, who holds a goad and a noose, and who displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
Oṃ, salutation to the heart of the Supreme Swan-like One, who bestows the path to Nirvāṇa.
The meditation on the head.
I eternally worship the Goddess whose head resembles a blooming bandhūka flower,
who constantly holds a sword and a shield, and who is ever-ready with hands granting boons and fearlessness.
Hrīṃ! To the one who pacifies the calamities of poison, svāhā to the head!
The topknot is meditation.
With joy, I worship the goddess Śikhā, who possesses eyes like sapphire gems,
who holds a skull and a trident, and who is supreme, bestowing boons and fearlessness with her hands.
HŪṂ! To the crest [mantra] that crushes all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions, VAUṢAṬ!
The meditation on the armor.
I worship the auspicious Varmadevī, whose limbs are as fair as a parrot, who has the eyes of a deer,
who holds a sword and a shield in her hands, and who bears a bow and arrows.
Hāṃ! O boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities, to the armor, hūṃ!
Meditation with the eyes.
I worship the Goddess of the Eyes, who is as white as camphor and possesses a pure smile,
joyfully bearing a chisel, a trident, a plow, and a thunderbolt.
Phreṃ! To the three eyes that pacify all enemies, vaṣaṭ!
Meditation through the weapon-mantra.
The weapon-goddess is smoke-colored, with blossoming and living eyes.
I worship the eternal one, who bestows boons and fearlessness, and who holds a trident and a staff.
*Kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ āgaccha hasa valga nararudhirāntravasābhakṣaṇi astrāya phaṭ.* Thus is the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the limbs and constituent parts.
Meditative absorption.
Possessing a terrifying beauty like that of the fierce cuckoo and other such beings,
she has four arms, one face, and shines with three eyes.
Mounted upon a great preta, holding an alms-bowl and a khaṭvāṅga staff,
with a noose and a mallet in her hands, she is greedy for fat and blood.
Extremely fierce, most terrifying, causing destruction, and making a loud noise—
such is the *kṛtyā* employed for the destruction of machines and the crushing of *khārkhoda*.
O Supreme Goddess, one should contemplate [the form] for the crushing of malevolent magic;
for pacification, however, one should contemplate her as being like the pure moon or the Himālaya mountain.
In rites for nourishment (pauṣṭika), she has a white and red luster, is withered, and has a withered face;
in rites for subjugation (vaśa), she has the luster of a pomegranate flower and resembles water mixed with saffron.
One should always contemplate [the seed-syllable] resembling vermilion for attraction;
for paralyzing, it resembles a rainbow; and for immobilizing, it is like a sapphire.
In the rite of paralyzing (jṛmbhana), one should visualize her as resembling gold; in burning (dāha), like a mass of flames;
in driving away (uccāṭa), like smoke; and in killing (māraṇa), as dark-brown.
For the purpose of curing disease, one should visualize her as variegated; for enchantment, like a parrot's plumage;
and for the sake of union, with the complexion of a crow or a cuckoo.
When agitating the opposing factors, she is fierce and resembles a mass of fire;
at the time of liberation, her appearance is like that of the pure moon, filling the sky.
One should meditate upon her who assumes any form at will, auspicious like a wish-fulfilling gem.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Oṃ, homage to all the accomplished yoginīs! [Located] in the aperture of Brahmā (the crown of the head).
Homage to all the Mothers who bestow accomplishments within the circle of faces! Homage to her who is gladdened by eternal, arisen bliss!
At the location of the small bell: "To the Mistress of the entire Kula-cakra," at the throat-piṇḍa.
And for the Blessed One Caṇḍakāpālinī, it is as follows: on the right arm.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. On the staff-like left arm.
Khphreṃ! O Supreme Swan, bestower of the path to nirvāṇa, [abide] in the heart!
On the right side: [She who] pacifies calamitous afflictions; [she who] shatters the enemy of misfortune, ill omen, and suffering.
On the left side.
[To the one] who shatters all misfortunes, calamities, and afflictions; on the left side.
The boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities—at the center of the navel. The subduer of all enemies—at the genitals.
O Goddess, come and laugh! In the secret mandala, dance, O you who devour human blood, entrails, and fat!
In the foundation mandala: "O crusher of my own enemies, eat! [This is for] the right thigh.
Pierce with the trident, cut with the sword; strike and sever the left thigh.
O Most Compassionate One, fulfill all my desires until they are complete.
On the right shank: O Blessed One, who assumes the form of Mahābhairava!
On the left calf: Oṃ tṛdaśavaranamite sakalamantramātare svāhā. On the right ankle: [Oṃ] svāhā.
O Goddess, who are affectionate toward those who bow before you—[place her] on the left ankle. O Mahākālī, destroyer of Time—[place her] on the right foot.
HŪṂ! Make her, who is afflicted by the passion of desire, compliant with your left foot; HRĪṂ! Make the daughters of the gods and asuras [compliant].
On the sole of the right foot: hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. On the left foot: [hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā].
Oṃ, homage to the foundation mandalas. Hrīṃ, homage to the navel mandalas, to the navel mandalas.
HŪṂ, homage to the heart-mandalas. HĀṂ, homage to the throat-pits.
Phreṃ, salutations to the locations of the uvula. Kṣoṃ, salutations to the right nostril.
Kroṃ, salutation to the nostrils; Na, salutation to the nose.
Salutation to the centers of the middle of the bow of Maḥ. Thus ends the assignment of the limbs and castes (aṅgajātinyāsa).
Through the non-difference of the Goddess and one's own self, one should contemplate the placement (nyāsa) of the body of phonemes, the body of mantra, and the supreme body.
Now follows the ritual deposition upon the body (dehanyāsa).
Meditative absorption.
The goddess has ten arms, possesses millions of faces, and is as white as jasmine and the moon; she is auspicious, adorned with tinkling anklets, moon-faced, and endowed with fifteen eyes.
She holds a trident, a vessel, a boon-granting gesture, a human skull, the gesture of fearlessness, a bell, and likewise a goad.
Śivā holds in her hands a sword, a shield, a lotus, and a stainless drop.
The Sovereign of the Gods, having mounted a preta situated within the ear,
assumes various forms for the benefit of practitioners.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Oṃ, homage to all the Yoginīs of all accomplishments; this is the ritual placement for the eastern face.
Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment; this is the ritual placement (nyāsa) for the southern face.
Homage to her who is gladdened by eternal, ever-arisen bliss; this is the ritual placement (nyāsa) for the northern face.
The placement of the western face is for the Mistress of the entire wheel of families.
The placement of the western face is for the Mistress of the entire wheel of families.
The placement of the upper face is for the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī.
Taṃ at the center of the eyebrows; Dyaṃ at the heart; Thauṃ at the navel. Thus is the bodily nyāsa.
Now follows the ritual placement of the doors (dvāranyāsa).
Meditative concentration.
She is radiant white, mounted upon a corpse, possessing nine faces, and terrifying.
She is endowed with eighteen arms and is clothed in a garment of tiger skin.
First, the face on the east is white; the one on the south is black in color;
the one on the north is said to be yellow; and the one above that is red in color.
On the right [face] it resembles saffron; on the left, it is beautiful and blue;
above that, it resembles smoke-colored; and on the right, it is the color of the pāṭala flower.
Likewise, one should visualize them as yellowish-green in color, with their respective weapons in the left [hands].
Likewise, a sword, a bell, a noose, a trident, and a severed head.
One should visualize in the right [hands] a bow, an arrow, a spear, and a vessel;
likewise, a sword, a mirror, a pestle, and a charming [object].

In the left hands of the Goddess, who is adorned with all ornaments, [he holds] a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya), a bow, a tree, and likewise a mountain, as well as a drop (bindu).
Having first performed the ritual placement of the doors for the sake of accomplishing all desires and goals.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Oṃ in the mouth; Hrīṃ in the left nostril; Hūṃ in the right nostril; Hāṃ in the left eye.
*Kṣoṃ* on the left ear; *kroṃ* on the right ear; *na* on the penis; *maḥ* on the anus—this is the door-assignment (*dvāranyāsa*).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six limbs.
Meditative absorption.

I bow to that Bhuvaneśvarī, the Goddess of the Heart, who has the luster of jasmine and the moon, whose lotus-hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and who dwells in the midst of a white lotus.
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption.
Oṃ, O Supreme Swan-like One, in the heart!
Meditative concentration.
I constantly worship the goddess Śirā, who is dark-complexioned,
auspicious, eternal, bestowing boons and fearlessness, and seated upon a beautiful lotus.
Thus ends the section on meditation.
To the one who teaches the path to nirvāṇa.
Meditative absorption.
The supreme goddess Śikhā is yellow in color, with a face like the autumnal moon;
seated upon a lotus, she indeed bestows both boons and fearlessness.
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption.
For the pacification of uneven calamities, [one should wear it] upon the crest-lock.
Meditative absorption.
May Kavaceśī, who possesses the radiance of a *pāṭala* flower, always protect [me];
she is slender, seated upon a lotus, and her hands shine with the gestures of granting strength and fearlessness.
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption.
In this armor that shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions.
Meditative absorption.
The goddess Netrā is smoke-colored, with a formidable and fierce countenance;
she holds the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, is pure, and sits upon a lotus.
Thus is meditation.
The eyes are the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities.
Meditative absorption.
I ever salute the supreme goddess of weapons, seated upon a lotus throne,
with eyes like the petals of a blue lotus, and hands granting boons and fearlessness.
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption.
O weapon that crushes all enemies in the ten directions!
Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six limbs.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the ten weapons held in the hands.
Meditative absorption.
With her ten lotus-like hands, she bestows supreme accomplishment,
holding the gestures of fearlessness and the granting of boons, as well as a water-pot, a khaṭvāṅga staff, and a severed head.
I worship the white goddess, who has three eyes, sits upon a corpse-seat, and holds ten weapons: a trident, a sword, vessels, and a noose.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
"O Goddess, come, salutation! Having meditated upon the invocation of the goddess Sakārā as residing within one's own body or within the musical instrument.
Laugh within yourself, having contemplated the supreme inconceivable grace.
Visualizing [the deity] who consumes human blood, entrails, and fat, [one should visualize] the skull-cup; [then] the right hand:
"Crush, crush my own enemies! Eat, eat! Visualizing the *khaṭvāṅga* staff.
On the left: "Bhidhi bhidhi with the trident!"—having visualized the trident.
"Cut, cut! Having visualized [the enemy] as a pillar with a sword, cover, cover!"
Having meditated upon the goad, [one should continue] until all my desires are accomplished.

Having visualized the hand granting boons on the right; having visualized the hand granting fearlessness on the left, [addressing her as] "O Blessed One, bearer of the form of Mahābhairava"; having visualized a human skull; having visualized a bell [addressing her as] "O you who are praised by the thirty gods, O Mother of all mantras"—thus is the tenfold set of weapons and ornaments.
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Now follows the placement [of mantras] upon the seat.
Meditative absorption.
O Great Goddess, she has four arms, with two hands joined in *añjali*;
she is seated upon a corpse-throne, red in color, and possesses great splendor.
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon the one who is compassionate toward those who bow down to him.
Thus ends the seat and the ritual placement.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the mantra-body.
Meditative absorption.
I ever salute her who stands upon the center of a throbbing lotus, atop which rests a corpse;
she who bears above it a blazing yellow skull-cup, and holds with her left hands the moon-faced goddess Pañcānanā,
a noose, a great sword, the syllable *Phet*, the gesture of granting boons, and a bell.
And [he holds] a garland, a goad, a lotus, a severed head, the gesture of fearlessness, and a bowl with his right hands.
Thus is meditation.
Goddess Mahākālī, destroyer of Time; of her who is formless, whose nature is Kuṇḍalinī.
The meditation on the Goddess: Hūṃ; one should contemplate the arising of the Goddess from the foundation of birth.
Khphreṃ: the visualization of the Goddess in the form of a flame, extending as far as the heart.
Khphreṃ: from the heart up to the point of the *bindu*. Khphreṃ: from the station of the *bindu* up to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).
Make her, who is afflicted by passion, gracious; make her so, O maiden of the gods and asuras!
By this, the capacity for subjugating the universe is stated. Hrīṃ at the seat of birth; Śrīṃ at the *liṅga*.
KROṂ at the location of the root; HŪṂ at the location of the navel; PHAṬ at the heart; PHAṬ at the mouth.
*Svā* at the place of the *bindu*; *Hāṃ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*). Thus is the placement of the nine syllables situated in the center of the navel.
Having thus performed the ritual of placement (nyāsa), this is the placement of the mantra-body.
Then follows the ritual placement of the colors upon the body.
Meditative absorption.
Resembling pure crystal, with five faces and ten arms,
she is mounted upon the lake of Mahāmudrā, possessing a beautiful body and a radiant form.
Her hair-ends are dark blue and curled, and she is adorned with a crown of matted locks;
her remaining head is decorated with large, various jewels and a *kādyamaṇi*.
White, reddish-brown, black, and red; bright with white khadira wood;
adorned with various jewels; well-proportioned, with excellent bones and beautiful earrings.
Having the reddish form of the solar disc, blazing with three or five eyes,
with a slight smile and a protruding tongue, her face radiant with bared fangs.
She who wears a garland of petals upon the throats of various wicked beings, such as the Daityas.
By this, [he beheld] her whose high breasts were rubbed by necklaces fashioned from jewels.
Beautiful in her waist, which is slender and enriched with the beauty of waves formed by the three folds;
she is adorned with a girdle of tinkling bells, fine garments, a tiger-skin loincloth, and a parrot.
In her right hands, she holds an excellent conch, a trident and so forth, and a skull;
and in her left hands, she holds a khaṭvāṅga, a fine vessel, a noose, and likewise a bell.
Her two feet are adorned with the *vīraghaṇṭhā* (hero’s bell) and the clattering of anklets (*ghargharī*), and are beautifully graced by a pair of knees that strike like parrots.
[He saw her] mounted upon the shoulder of Rudra, who was pure white, three-eyed, two-armed, and single-faced,
and who sat in the vīrāsana posture.
Resembling a blazing fire, a mass of gathered flames,
it issued forth from the pores of his skin, making the sky appear like the dawn.
She who dwells in the midst of the eight Mātṛkās, surrounded by Ḍākinīs,
thronged by many Siddhas, and worshipped as the Yoginī of Accomplishment.
Thus ends the flower of meditative concentration; homage!
Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the feet and the body.
Oṃ, salutation to the head. Salutation to all the Siddhi-yoginīs. [Salutation] to the circle of the forehead region.
Homage to all the Mothers of Accomplishment. At the tip of the nose: homage to her who is gladdened by eternal, arising bliss.
To the mistress of the entire wheel of families, in the left eye; in the right eye.
To the Blessed Lady; to the third eye; to Caṇḍakāpālinī; to the left cheek; it is as follows:
The Brahmakhaṇḍa in the right cheek.
Oṃ at the left ear; Hrīṃ at the right ear; Hūṃ at the lower lip; Hāṃ at the upper lip.
PHREṂ on the lower teeth; KṢOṂ on the upper teeth; KROṂ on the tongue; NAMAḤ on the mouth.
The Viṣṇukhaṇḍa.
O Supreme Swan! At the throat. O Bestower of the Path to Nirvāṇa! On the left shoulder.
To the one who pacifies calamities and misfortunes; on the left arm: to the one who shatters all evils, portents, and afflictions.
At the left wrist: O boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities! At the fingers of the left hand: [Obeisance].
O crusher of all enemies! On the nail of the left finger! O Goddess, come! On the right shoulder!
Laugh at the right upper arm; leap at the right wrist.
O consumer of human blood, entrails, and fat! Dakṣa [is] on her thumb! O crusher of my own enemies!
On the nail of the right index finger: *khāhi khāhi*. In the circle of the uprooted: *bhiṇḍi* with the trident.
On the left breast: *chindi chindi*. On the right breast: *tāḍaye* with the sword.
Then, on the left and right, one should cut at the navel-center.
O Kālānala, fulfill all my desires until that time.
O Most Compassionate One! Within the womb! O Blessed Lady! In the circle of molasses!
O you who assume the form of Mahābhairava! O you who strike the left buttock! O you who are saluted by the best of the thirty gods!
On the right buttock: *sakalamantramataḥ*. On the left thigh: *praṇatajanavatsale*.
"Vāmorāvadha" (slaying with the left arm) is for the goddess Mahākālī, the destroyer of Time; [this is] on the left knee.
Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ. [The mantra] for the left ankle: "O you who are distressed by the passion of desire. [The mantra] for the right ankle: [same as above].
Perform [the mudrā] on the toes of the left foot; [perform it] upon the maiden of the gods and asuras on the toes of the right foot.
Hrīṃ at the lower part of the right thigh; Śrīṃ at the right knee; Hrūṃ at the right foot; Phaṭ phaṭ.
*Phaṭ svāhā* on the toes of the left foot; *svāhā* on the back. This is the ritual procedure for the deposition (*nyāsa*) of the body and the feet.
The worship of the water vessel.
Then, having fashioned on his own left side a mandala consisting of a circle marked with the *māyā* syllable and a square, he worships the *aiṃ* syllable in the center of the triangle; then,
having washed the base (*ādhāra*) with the *astra-mantra*, he places it there.
Raṃ, salutation to the fire-maṇḍala, whose self consists of ten kalās.
Phaṭ! Having rinsed the water vessel, Khphreṃ! Having established the water vessel therein.
Haṃ, obeisance to the solar disc, whose self consists of twelve kalās.
The placement of the water vessel: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣlīṃ Klīṃ.
One should worship with water.
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī,
Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, please be present in this water!
Salutation to the lunar orb, whose essence consists of sixteen digits.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ, the goddess Varuṇā, Hsauṃ.
Meditative absorption.
The goddess Bhairavī has eighteen arms and four faces;
she wears black and red garments and is black and red in complexion.
Her hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and she likewise holds a noose and a goad;
in her right hands, she carries a sword and a skull-cup.
In the right hand there is a trident, and likewise in the other [right hand] a rosary;
in the left hand there is a book, and in the right hand a discus.
One should contemplate an arrow in the right [hand] and a bow in the left;
one should know a mace in the right and a pestle in the left alone.
Likewise, she holds the threatening gesture with her left hand and a bell in her right;
she bears a banner in her left and a vajra in her right.
The slender beloved of Mahādeva was adorned with great jewels.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, the sandals for the venerable Lord of the Water Vessel.
The Six Limbs: Khphreṃ, obeisance to the heart; Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head! Khphreṃ, hūṃ to the armor! Khphreṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes!
KH PHREṂ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ ||
Do not recite the nine-syllable root mantra.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
Having concealed the *matsyamudrā* with the *dhenumudrā*, one should sprinkle all objects and oneself with *tarjanya* water while reciting the *gāyatrī*.
*Khphreṃ*, let us know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon her ninety-plus [forms]; may that Lakṣmī inspire us. Thus ends the worship of the water vessel (*jalapātra*).
Now follows the ritual for placing the conch shell.
One should fill [the vessel] with water while reciting the mantra "namaḥ," beginning from the heart.
Khphreṃ, homage to the heart! Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head! Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock!
Khphreṃ, for the armor, hūṃ. Khphreṃ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Khphreṃ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
The rites beginning with invocation (āvāhana) [should be performed]. One should display the conch, cow, and yoni mudrās. Then, the sprinkling (prokṣaṇa).
Now follows the worship of the arghya vessel.
Having established the Goddess in the center of one's own self, [one should place] the heart in the fire of the wheel of that [wheel].
The head is in the northeast; the crest-lock is in the southwest; the armor is in the northwest; [the eye is] in the center.
And in the four directions, the Weapon [mantra]: "Homage to the seat of all mantras."
Aiṃ, obeisance to the sacred seat of Kāmarūpa. Klīṃ, obeisance to the sacred seat of Pūrṇagiri.
Sauṃ, salutation to the seat of the Jālandhara-pīṭha.
Having washed the vessel with the Astra-mantra, one should place the stream [of water].
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ. I accomplish the support for the vessel of Siddha-Mahālakṣmī. Mācate.

*Khphreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ rmlvryūṃ*, salutation to the seat of the *argha* vessel for the fire-maṇḍala, whose essence consists of the sixteenth digit that bestows dharma. Having thus worshipped the support (*ādhāra*), [one worships] upon it, proceeding clockwise.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to Dhūmrārciṣkalā, the venerable sandals!
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Raṃ, the sandals of Śrī Nīlaraktākalā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Laṃ, the sandals of Kapirā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vaṃ, the digit Visphuliṅginī, the venerable sandals.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Śaṁ, the digit Jvālinī, the venerable pādukā.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Ṣaṁ, [I offer] the venerable sandals to the digit Arciṣmatī.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Saṁ, the digit Havyavāhinī, the venerable sandals.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Laṃ, the energy of Raudrī, the venerable sandals.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣaṃ, the digit of withdrawal (saṃhāriṇī-kalā), the venerable sandals.
Having thus performed the worship, one should take a single vessel made of gold, copper, bell-metal, iron, brass, or silver, place it upon that [base], and wash it with the Astra mantra.
KH PHREṂ! O you who crush all enemies, PHAṬ to the weapon!
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Siddha Mahālakṣmī Ambā, I place the vessel for the offering water; homage!
In the bowl.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hāṃ Hīṃ Hūṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ. Salutation to the seat of the *argha* vessel for the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*), which bestows wealth and consists of twelve digits (*kalā*). Above that, turning clockwise:
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kaṃ Bhaṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the digit Tapinī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khaṃ Vaṃ, the digit Bhrāmarī, the venerable sandals.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Gaṃ Phaṃ, the moisture-bestowing digit (Kledinī Kalā), [worship] the venerable sandal (Śrīpādukā).
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ghaṃ, the digit Vantāpinī, [I worship] the venerable pādukā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṅaṃ Naṃ, [I worship] the Śodhinī-kalā, the venerable pādukā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Caṃ Dhaṃ, the digit Bodhinī, the venerable sandals.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Chaṃ Daṃ, the Śrī-pādukā of Varaṇyākalā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Jaṃ Thaṃ, the Śrī-pādukā of the Ākarṣaṇī-kalā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Taṃ, the digit of Suṣumnā, the venerable pādukā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṭaṃ Ṭhaṃ, the venerable sandals of the digit Jyeṣṭhā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vaṃ Ḍaṃ, the sandals of the venerable Hiraṇyākalā.
Having worshipped in this manner, one should offer incense.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Kṣlīṁ Klīṁ || Khphreṁ, having fumigated [with incense].
Then, having brought the water-pot and placed it on one's left side.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the seat of the Kula-vessel (Kulakumbhāsana).
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon the supreme goddess named Kumbhā, whose body possesses a slightly reddish luster,

whose face is like the moon, who has five faces, and whose eyes are as bright as arrows and the sun; she holds in her lotus-like hands a sword, a goad, a trident, a severed head, and displays the gesture of granting boons with her right hands, and likewise with her left.
I worship her who holds a skull-topped staff, a broad noose, a bowl, and a water-pot, and whose hands display the gesture of fearlessness.
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava!
Then, having placed the water-pot on the left, one should fill the vessel with the root mantra and the garland mantra.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! Bring forth the entirety of nectar produced from the fragments of the cosmic egg;
O great vessel filled to the brim, bring forth the essence of ambrosia.
Having cast *phreṃ khphreṃ hrīṃ* a second time with the *amṛtamudrā*, [place] *vaṃ*.
Having stirred it three times with *hrīṃ*, having purified the impurities therein,
having kindled it with *klīṃ*, having drawn it up through the channel of the eyes, and having brought it to the state of the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*),
one should contemplate the full vessel with the nine-syllable mantra.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ Smlvryūṃ Saṃ. Salutation to the lunar orb (somamaṇḍala), the bestower of desires, whose essence consists of sixteen digits, and which is the nectar of the water offering (arghyāmṛta). Above that:
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Aṁ, the digit Amṛtā, the venerable pādukā; Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Āṁ, Mānasī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ I Tuṣṭi; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ī Puṣṭi;
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Uṃ Prīti; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ūṃ Revatī; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Kalā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Śrīṃ Kalā | Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ḷṃ Kalī | Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ḹṃ Sudhā |
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Eṃ Jyotsnā. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Hemavatī. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ O Cchālā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Auṃ Saṃpūrṇā. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Vāmā. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aḥ Amā.
KHPHREṂ Sakalaśatrupramathani HŪṂ HŪṂ Astrāya PHAṬ ||
Having snapped the fingers in the four directions, one should stir [the contents] with the root mantra using the Amṛtamudrā.
The eye in the directions: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Glūṃ, obeisance to Gaganaratna.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Slūṃ, salutation to the Jewel of Heaven. Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Mlūṃ, salutation to the Jewel of Mortals.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Plūṃ, obeisance to the Jewel of the Netherworld (Pātāla-ratna). Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Nlūṃ, obeisance to the Jewel of the Nagas (Nāga-ratna).

In the center of that, having meditated upon the digit (kalā) in the form of Vāgbhava, resembling the rising sun, [and] Amṛteśvarī flowing from the lunar orb, one should draw a triangle counter-clockwise with the left ring finger;
having drawn the triangle in sequence with "aṃ kaṃ yaṃ," and having written "oṃ" and the pair "ha-lakṣa."
Having covered [it] with both hands.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O Amṛte, O you who arise from nectar, O showerer of nectar, cause nectar to flow! Sāṃ Jūṃ!
Salutation to Amṛteśvarī.

Aiṁ Hrīṁ Aiṁ! O Immortal One, born of the immortal, showering the immortal! Klīṁ! Make the nectar flow! Sauṃḥ! Destroy the flow of semen! Bestow the power of accomplishment upon the fourfold group of yogis! O Great Khecarī Mudrā, manifest! Hūṁ Svāhā!

Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One Rudra; Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ. Oṃ Īṃ Glauṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady Rudrā; Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ. Oṃ Ī Glauṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady Trailokyamohanī, the Concealer, the Great Sovereign of Maheśvara, the Binder of the speech of all bound souls (paśus), [and the binder] of the eyes, ears, tongues, noses, and feet of all bound souls.
"tiraskaraṇaṃ kuru svāhā. Having thus recited the Amṛteśvarī mantra three times:

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O you who bestow the bliss of the one undivided essence, O self of excellent nectar; O you whose form is Kula, manifest here now as the treasure of mantras that shine forth by your own will!
Hskṣmlvryūṃ, vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava!
Thus, having gratified Ānandabhairava and Sudhādevī with those very drops, one should worship.
O you who possess a moist form, bestow the state of immortality upon this object, which is the supreme Akula, whose nature is nectar and which brings about the knowledge of accomplishment.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the sandals for the seat of the argha vessel.
Having worshipped Punarnavātman Mithu with great reverence.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, vaṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava!
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, Vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairavī, the Goddess of Nectar.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Śvāṁ Saḥ Saḥ Saḥ, O Supreme Goddess, vomit nectar! Svāhā!
The purification of substances.
Meditative absorption.
The Goddess Śāṅkarī, who possesses the luster of ten million full moons and is mounted upon the body of Rudra.
Her limbs were adorned with every ornament; she was the Sovereign of the Universe, wearing a garland of severed heads.
One should meditate upon Maheśānī, who has ten arms and five faces, wears a crown, and holds a sword,
a trident, a goad, a gift-bestowing gesture, and a skull placed against her heart.
Holding a khaṭvāṅga, a noose, a severed head, the gesture of fearlessness, and a water-pot in each face, he has three eyes; his right [faces] are black and red.
In her left hand she holds a white chowrie, and her smile resembles the full moon;
she is the fulfiller of all desires and the bestower [of boons] when devotion is offered to her.
Having placed the noble arghya vessel, one should worship with the six-limbed [mantra].
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. The six-limbed mantra (ṣaḍaṅga).
Khphreṃ, homage to the heart. Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head. Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
KHPHREṂ KAVACĀYA HŪṂ ||
Khphreṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes! Khphreṃ, phaṭ to the weapon!
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the *yonimudrā*.
Right there, he should satisfy Gaṇa, Vatuka, and Kṣetrapāla.
One should offer libations starting from Brahmāṇī up to Mūlasvāmī.
Āṃ phīṃ phāṃ, O Mahāsṛṣṭicaṇḍalakṣmīsiddheśvarī, phe phaṭ!
With that, the libation is performed; with the nine-syllable mantra, the libation is performed nine times.
Then, one should place the lineage of gurus, beginning with the supreme guru, upon one's own head.
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Śrīkaṇṭhanātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Śaṅkaranātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Anantanātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Sākhyanātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Piṅgalanātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Lord of the Winged Kings, [I worship] Your sandals.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! The sandals of Kūrmanātha.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, the sandals of Maṅgalanātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Meghanātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Maśendranātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Koṅkaṇāmbā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Piṅgalanātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of the Mother Śavarī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of the Guru-Nātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of the supreme Guru-Nātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of the supreme preceptor, the Lord Guru.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! The sandals of the Lord, the Preceptor of the Ancients.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Ādisiddhinātha.
Having worshipped in this manner, one should display the five mudrās.
Aiṃ, the Yonimudrā; Hrīṃ, the Guhyamudrā.
Śrīṃ, the Drāvaṇī mudrā; Kṣlō, the Kṣobhiṇī mudrā; Klīṃ, the Jvālinī mudrā.
Purification of the Elements (Bhūtaśuddhi)
Meditative absorption.
The circle of the earth is described as square and yellow; the excellent circle of water as a white crescent moon;
the divine circle of fire as having six red spokes; and the one called wind as an excellent hexagon, deep smoky grey in color.
Where is there a reflection as clear as the sky? The five elements have arisen elsewhere in the scripture;
among them, Maheśa is established, white and peaceful in form, four-armed, holding a lotus and a sword.
With his right hand he holds a trident, and likewise with the other [hand] he bestows gifts in due order;
in his left hand he displays the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya*). By means of the five-fold mantras, he [is endowed with] hands, body, and faces.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hsauṃ Hsphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ. Thus ends the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Self-worship.
Meditative absorption.
The face of Mūladevī is known to be blue-red and black;
it possesses a white and yellow luster and always bestows the divine command and spiritual accomplishments.
[He holds] a goad, a sword, a trident, a severed head, and likewise a gift;
a noose, a skull-topped staff, a bowl, and a water-pot, together with [the gesture of] granting fearlessness.
Adorned with various ornaments, holding [attributes] in her right and left hands,
the Goddess— beautiful in every limb— is praised by the lords of the gods.
One should meditate upon the Mistress of Bhairava, renowned as Siddhilakṣmī, who is such an incomparable meditation that she bestows the fortune of the Self and the attainment of perfection.
Khphreṃ, salutation to sandalwood for myself. Khphreṃ, salutation to unbroken rice grains.
Khphreṃ sindūraṃ namaḥ | Khphreṃ sarvajanamohanī namaḥ |
Flower: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. Flower, salutation to the Self.
With the bee [mantra] at the three drops: *khphreṃ sakalaśatrupramathani astrāya phaṭ*.
Having brought it to a state of uniform essence through its own nature, which is eternal and so forth, and having remembered it as the form of supreme nectar, perform my manifestation again;
then, having consecrated it seven times with the *mala* mantra, protected it with the *astra* mantra, and veiled it with the *kavaca* mantra, one should display the *dhenu* and *yoni* mudrās. Thus.
The ritual procedure for the worship of the root vessel and the arghya vessel.
Then one should recite the *kṣetrabali* mantra.
Oṃ, homage to Siddhi Mahākālikā!

Salutations to you, O Trailokyā; salutations to you, O Kālikā, who are bowed to by the three worlds; O Viśvacaṇḍā, O Vāmā, who abide within the Vāma; salutations to the pair of feet praised by the best of the thirty gods.

Hraṃ! To you who are long and possess the visarga, whose nature consists of the letters a, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, śa, and kṣa; who abide within the light, who wear a skull-ornament, who possess a universal form, who grant boons to those who are supreme and beyond the highest, and who have a serpent as an upper garment—hūṃ!
The moon and sun are your earrings; cross over, cross over, O tremulous one! Save me, O cave-eyed one!
O Jyeṣṭhā and Vāmā, O Raudrī, O you whose crest-flames are ablaze, O Mātṛnandā, O Sunandā!

O Svāhākāra, O Viriñci, who brings welfare to those who bow before you; O destroyer of the multitude of diseases, O Kaṅkāla, O Kālakāla, O remover of the impurities of the Kali age, O Sadya-Vāmādi-ghora!

HŪṂ! To her whose faces are her own true form, who delights in my excellence, who dwells within the hollow of the lotus-center, in the space that carries the space of the heart, who is more fierce than Hara and Hara, who rends asunder, who is the vehicle of the spirits, the devourer, the deluder, the flame of the tongue—ŚA ŚA ŚA ŚA ŚA! O Śavarī, you who reside on the mountain of the Kora!
O Goddess, in this very abode of Viśveśvarī, churn, churn away my misdeeds through churning!
Drāṃ drāṃ drāṃ, O Drāviṇī! Kili kili, O Rabhasā! Carmamuṇḍe, O you who strike!
Klīṃ ṣluṃ raṃ, O carrier of the principles (tattva)! Kili kili, O Subhagā! O you who plunge into the knowledge of mantras!
O you who carry away the dead, *preṃ preṃ preṃ*; O you who cry out *kala kala*; O you at the tip of the noose and the cleaver;
O you whose abode is most divine; O you who move through the sky, *kha kha kha kha*; O you who are terrible with a gurgling roar!
KṢRĪṂ PHAṬ HŪṂ PHAṬ! O you whose nature is the self-form, ḌA ḌA ḌA ḌA ḌAMARE! HŪṂ!
O you who dwell in victory, cut through [the enemy] with the weapon on the left, ṬHA ṬHA ṬHA ṬHA ṬHAMARE! KṢAKṢAKĀRE! O Subhīmā!

I bow to you, O protector of the hollow, O bestower of excellent boons, O you whose form is composed of letters, O you who utter the sounds "he he" and "hūṃ," O burner, cook, cook! Release, release the one who is dying!

O Caṇḍākṣī, you of wrathful form! Tear asunder, tear asunder, O supreme one! You who are intoxicated by the essence of excellent wine, O hero, you who dwell in the fire of heroes, you who are flushed with the intoxication of honey-wine, O Jvālinī, whose mouth is ablaze!
O fierce one, of single-minded form, you who roar with a deep, guttural sound, of terrible appearance, destroyer of fear, *phaṭ phaṭ*!
You whose form is the sound *phreṃ*, who exclaim "kaha kaha," O delightful one, smeared with the ashes of the dead!
O Mārī, you whose form is the sound *kroṃ*, who utter "Kaha Kaha" with your tongue, O lute of the skeleton of Kṛṣṇa,
O you whose form is wrath with the syllables *kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ*, who laugh "Ha Ha Ha Ha" and take away [all things], I bow to you, O Caṇḍāsidhārā!
I worship you at all times, O you whose mouth is filled with human flesh, who dwell in the seat of conduct!
Hē hē hūṃkāra-nāde! La la la la lane cheda pheṭkāra-rūpe! I worship you!

Ḍāṃ ḍāṃ ḍāṃ! O Ḍāmarī, bestower of boons, grantor of boons, you whose speed is the terrible *hūṃkāra*, who binds the limits of the roar of *nāra*, victory, victory, O Padakā, you who dwell in Koṭikarṇa!

O Heroine, worthy of homage by heroes, who art ever restrained by the hosts of ṛṣis, you who have descended in beautiful form for the sake of desire— grant him, O auspicious one, the boon of the yoga-pīṭhas and upapīṭhas eternally.
O Goddess, by the power of your majesty, this auspiciously renowned Mantrasiṃha, who recites the *Kṣetrāvalī*, has been delivered from all divine and non-divine obstacles in this very existence.
[Thus ends the hymn to the Seat of the Kṣetrāvalī of Pratyagiri, within the Jayadratha, the Vidyāpīṭha, in the illustrious Śrī-Śrī-Śrī-Siddhilakṣmīmata Prakāśa.]
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Goddess who is both supreme and non-supreme, Khecarī, whose nature is the void;
O Mother, who acts for the welfare of all beings, come here, O Supreme Sovereign!
O Goddess seated upon the Mahāmudrā throne, whose movement is like the moon of consciousness in the stainless [expanse], O Mother who benefits all beings, come here, O Supreme Sovereign!
Be well-pleased and grant your presence in this maṇḍala; homage!
Thus, having invoked the digit of consciousness into the form of the Goddess while reciting the root-vidyā, [the practitioner should proceed].

Having performed the invocation (āvāhana), presence (sannidhāna), confinement (saṃnirodha), and manifestation (saṃmukhīkaraṇa), and so forth, and having formed the veiling mudrā (avaguṇṭhana), the cow-mudrā (dhenumudrā), and the womb-mudrā (yonimudrā), one should contemplate that the Goddess has arrived.
Then, having placed omniscience and the other [perfections] into the six goddesses, one should place the mantra-body into the goddess.
Then, having fumigated it with the nine-syllable mantra.
Āṃ phiṃ phāṃ, Mahāsṛṣṭicaṇḍalakṣmīsiddheśvarī, phreṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, homage to Siddhiyoginī Mahāmāyā!
She who always dwells in the *kanavīra* flower and in the cremation ground for the benefit of living beings, mounted upon the corpse-bearing Rudra,
white as the moon and snow, possessing five faces, and infallible— [to her I bow].
May she herself, the ten-armed Goddess Siddhilakṣmī, grant [it].

Victory, victory to the Mother of the Universe! O You whose lotus-feet are set in motion by the intense fragrance of the *mandāra* garlands from the crowns of the gods led by Hari, Hara, and Hiraṇyagarbha;
O Lotus-eyed One, whose pure *mandākinī* flows from the conch-like palms of Your hands!
O you whose bodily luster is as beautiful as a multitude of autumn moons, jasmine flowers, and white lotuses;
O Suprabhā! Victory, victory, O Mahākālī, destroyer of Time (Kāla), illuminator of the assembly of the wheel of the Samaya!
O Mother of the Siddhas, Gaṇas, Yoginīs, and Vīras, consort of the Lord of Munis, O lady with a multitude of arms!

O Virūpākṣa, O Mistress of the three worlds, who are being praised by the Kinnaras of the Kadamba grove, who bestow the fortune of spiritual perfection through the performance of the arts, who grant the essence of bliss through the service of Your eyes,
and whose dancing is radiant; O You whose ornaments— the rows of jewels and pearls and the shimmering bones of serpents— resound with a tinkling *jhanajhana* sound!

O Caṇḍī, intoxicated by the drinking of blood, whose creeper-like body is crimsoned by a dense mass of radiance that has turned the entire circle of the quarters red; whose cheeks are adorned with beautiful earrings of the sun and moon; and who is decorated with a garland of human skulls dangling between the pair of her high, full, and firm jar-like breasts!
