O you who are resonant with the clamor of the cries of throngs of *piśācas* flashing amidst the wonders of funeral pyres, where *ḍākinīs* circle in circles without fear, and which are filled with the sounds of the rustling forests of *kaca*, *tāli*, *kāṇḍava*, and *tāḍava* trees, along with *pretas*, *kalakas*, *lattas*, and *vetālas*.
She who dwells upon the cremation ground, mounted upon the shoulder of Rudra;
she whose interior abode is the central lotus within the six supports (ādhāras); she who is accompanied by the contraction [of the breath], appearing like a sleeping serpent;
she who is the family-coil (kulakuṇḍalinī) resembling a lamp-flame of power; she from whom the light of knowledge arises in the Suṣumnā.
O moon, whose orb is like a sky cleared of all clouds, from whom flows a torrent of nectar;
O you who are meditated upon by all practitioners with minds emerging from the ocean [of consciousness], who are well-cultivated, and who are honored by the circle of the *mātṛkā* letters;
O moon, whose body is anointed with saffron, agallochum, and musk!
In that pavilion, perfumed by the fragrance of jasmine flowers, where the broad mass of matted hair is adorned with the crescent moon,
and which is graced by the excellent hero’s necklace and a fresh garland of golden *mallikā* and *tatollikā* jasmines;
there, the wind— red with the movement of the fragrant *bandhūka* flowers and various scents beloved by the God of Love— intoxicates all.
Victory, victory to you, O Mother of the World! You who are like Mount Sumeru in your meditative form, and like the three-eyed Shiva in your majesty. Victory! Victory!
Victory, victory! O presiding deity of the garland of two hundred and twenty-one syllables, which surpasses even the nine-syllable mantra;

O Kālī, Kātyāyanī, Kāpālinī, you who are adorned with ten hands holding a skull-bowl filled with human blood, fat, and flesh, a sword, a trident, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a bell, a severed head, a noose, a goad, and displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
O Goddess Siddheśvarī, meditated upon by the Vidyādharas and the lords of the Uragas, seated in the easily assumed Vaddhavīrāsana;

O Goddess who is the very embodiment of the Śāmbhava-āveśa; O Mahādevī, known as Amā, known as Umā, known as the eternally full moon, and known as the shining star; O you whose form is the radiant sky within the interior of the letters A and KṢA!

O Mahāvyomavāmeśvarī, Khecarī, Gocarī, Bhūcarī, Digcarī, Samvarī; O you who are the wheel of power (Śakticakra), whose nature is action, will, and knowledge; O you who transcend the qualities (Guṇātīta), the eternal nectar, the bestower of eternal enjoyment; O you who delight in the play of the dance at the time of the conclusion of twilight; O Great Dancer! Ṭaṭa! Ṭaṭa! Mahānaṭa! (Great Dancer)!
O you who possess the weighty splendor of matted locks; O you whose intellect is abundant with the entire collection of poetic arts;

O bestower of the perfection of beautiful poetry through various compositions of the three qualities (guṇas); O giver of prosperity, giver of intelligence, giver of knowledge, giver of honor, and giver of liberation!

In the autumn season, that sixteen-syllable mantra— like a circle of forest groves on the riverbank where the sweet-sounding waters mingle with the fragrance of white flowers, where serpents dance, and where the enemy hosts are cast down—
possesses the splendor of a lamp for the ocean-treasury of deer and sea-monsters, shimmering with waves tossed by the wind.

Beyond that is the supreme [mandala] with four gates, adorned externally by cremation grounds resplendent with eight-petaled lotuses, sixty-four-petaled lotuses, and six-cornered wheels; where female jackals howl with *phat* sounds, terrifying the female spirits (*piśācikā*); where the night-roaming *caravināsinī* utters the loud, clattering sound of her terrible fangs; and from whose mouth flows the saliva of the female corpse-dwellers (*pretāṅganā*).

O Karālākarṣaṇī, O you who cause the clamor of strife, O you who are embraced by a swarm of bees, O you seated upon Kujā, O you whose delight is absorbed in the muttering of prayers, O you arisen from self-restraint, O Parā Mūrti, O Pratyamgirā, O Navākṣarī, O Savarī, O Sahasrākṣarī,
O you beloved of Śrīkaṇṭha, Vasiṣṭha, and Viśvāmitra!

With a heart delighted by the hymns to the lineage of the three types of gurus beginning with Bhava— namely Uvāsukī, Krodhamuni, Mīnanātha, Jayadratha, Jāvāli, Jamadagni, Jamadanu, Cāṇakya, Ālakācārya, Vimalabodha, Vicitrānanda, Devaprabhu, and others— and moved by compassion, [she was attended] by various Vidyādharīs and Kinnarīs.

And the Gandharva Apsaras, the daughter of a seer, was captivated by the virtuous conduct of King Kakutstha as he moved through the circle of time; she was devoted to the drinking of honey-wine and the company of Siddha maidens, and was enchanted by his lute,
which was stirred by the lotus-like buds of her breasts fragrant with the scent of the four-fold assembly of the Sarasvatī.

O Lord of the World, whose five-colored ears are filled with the sound of the flute; O Vaikuṇṭha, whose chest is embraced by the pair of arms of Lakṣmī; O you who cause the forest of Vṛndāvana to dance with joy through the words emerging from your mouth; O you whose hair-tuft is stirred by the wind as it brushes against the whirling *bainda* fans held by the circle of gopīs; O you who are surrounded by the abundant fragrance of the forest of matted locks shaken by the breeze.
O Mother, beautiful with a multitude of sweat-drops trickling down, wearing a garland of *ūmā* flowers and the crest-jewel of the Lord of Serpents;
O Victorious One, the progenitor of all, vast with every kind of garland!
You are the life-restoring herb for the practitioner whose body is scorched by the forest fire of insurmountable poverty.
O Mañjuka, whose slender form is like a cluster of blossoms, who possesses waves of the nectar of compassion—

look now upon me, your dweller in this grove of *sambaka* trees; look upon me who am helpless, unconscious, destitute, devoted to the words of others, always miserable, and without a protector, through the drinking of your lofty streams of side-long glances.
Be gracious, O Supreme Goddess, O Most Compassionate One, who assumes the form of Mahābhairava and is praised by the best of the thirty gods.

Oṃ! Homage to the sovereign of all *siddhi*-yoginīs; homage to the one who rejoices as the Mother of Accomplishment (*siddhimātṛkā*); O Sovereign Daughter who always removes the obstacles of those who bow before you; O Dispeller of the sufferings of the dense wilderness; O Giver of fear to thieves, tigers, and the wicked; O You whose heart is like the *dūrvā* grass!

In the dense forest of evil conduct, where the thickets of formidable difficulties are rent asunder by the mass of intense heat, amidst the tumultuous sounds of sharp *paṭaha*, *mṛdaṅga*, and *ḍamaru* drums and the resonance of various joyful shouts and debates, while the enemy of battle is being honored with the scent of great flesh, musk, and abundant camphor—
O Caṇḍī, O Caṇḍikā, beloved of excellent incense, illuminated by jewels in the great oil-house, arisen through knowledge, you who dwell in the pavilion; O Bhava, O Puṇḍarīka, O lotus-eyed one,
together with the multitude of gods headed by the thousand-eyed Indra.
O Mistress of the Kula, who art saluted with joined palms by various female disciples whose flower garlands have fallen in profusion;

who art compassionate toward those who bow before you with all their mantras; who art gracious toward the host of young women of the three worlds; who art known as Durgā; who art the destroyer of enemies; and who art mixed with human blood, fat, and flesh—be propitious toward me, who am afflicted by passion.

O Blessed One, who destroys the bonds of the multitude of bound animals through the intoxication of wine and meat; O Great Contemplation arisen for those practitioners who worship Bhava; O Bestower of desired prosperity upon those who meditate;
O You whose playful movements are like trees and creepers painted upon the continuum of every mind; O You who cut asunder the works of others; O You who are the sharp spear-point of Kṛtānta!

Forgive my offense, forgive me! O Śaktinātha, I am alone and destitute of attendants; having come for refuge at your feet, I bow to you, who have slain the Manarava demon. Indeed, I reflect upon you and seek your grace, O Siddhāmbā, you who are the fortress against the fear of the most powerful enemies.
O Śivā, you who are immeasurable by the multitude of planets at the forefront of the mandala, cut through and shatter [my bonds]; be gracious, be gracious; forgive, forgive my transgression.
[Thus ends the hymn *Siddhilakṣmītrikhaṇḍadaṇḍaka*.]
I shall invoke, I do invoke Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, Guhyakālī, and Tripurasundarī.
The worship of the three deities.
Khphreṃ, sandals for the human throne; Khphreṃ, sandals for the peacock throne.
KH PHREṂ, the sandals for the seat of the mouth.
Meditation by means of the field.
The guardian of the field (Kṣetrapāla) is a great crow, three-eyed and black-complexioned;
he has four arms, a massive body, and wears a long garland of bones.
One should contemplate [the deity] holding a *khaṭvāṅga* and a bell in the left hands, and a trident and a staff in the right;
all the *śaktis* are likewise, and one should meditate on them as sporting together.
KH PHREṂ THHSRAUṂ! To the goddess Dambhakī of Prastaradvīpa and the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa, [this] sandalwood (pādukā)! [This is] the offering (bali).
The meditation on the Baṭuka.
The god wears red garments, is red in color, and has four arms;
he has one face, red eyes, tawny eyebrows, and tawny hair.
Adorned with hands holding a staff, a trident, and a curved knife and skull-cup,
wearing a serpent as a sacred thread, he is the one who cuts through obstacles.
I bow to the one named Vaṭuka, who is seated upon a peacock throne, pervaded by blazing rays of light,
and the slayer of the demon Tāraka.
KH PHREṂ ŚRĪṂ HRĪṂ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha. Offering.
One should meditate with counting.
He has the face of an elephant, a single tusk, and is white in color; he has four arms, holding a staff, an axe, and a bowl, with a tusk and a serpent serving as his sacred thread.
Salutations to you, who are richly adorned with the ornaments of serpents, pot-bellied, short in stature, seated upon a rat, known as Ganādhyakṣa, and the bestower of spiritual accomplishments.
KPHREṂ GĀṂ GĪṂ GŪṂ GAḤ GLAUṂ, the sandals for Kulagaṇeśvara. The offering.
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the mudrās of the threatening gesture, the staff, and the elephant.
The worship of the Goddess’s seat.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti. Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Anantāsana.
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat (kandāsana). Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the human-seat (nārāsana).
Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat (patrāsana). Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-posture (padmāsana).

Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the seat of the filaments (keśarāsana). Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the seat of the pericarp (karṇikāsana). Obeisance to Dharma. Obeisance to Jñāna. Obeisance to Vairāgya. Obeisance to Aiśvarya.
Homage to Adharma. Homage to Ignorance. Homage to Non-enmity. Homage to Non-mastery. Homage to the Jewel Altar Seat. Laṃ, homage to the Oḍḍiyāna Seat.
Vaṃ, salutation to Jālandhara-pīṭha. Raṃ, salutation to Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha.
Salutation to Kāmarūpa-pīṭha. Khphreṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the Rudra-pretāsana.
Hsauṃ, obeisance to the one seated upon the great corpse.
Now, as for meditative absorption (dhyāna).
KHPHREṂ: Mahātejomayī Lakṣmī, possessing the radiance of ten million times ten thousand rays;
she has five faces, ten arms, and is endowed with fifteen eyes.
The great goddess of white complexion, seated upon a great preta,
is the Siddhiyoginī worshipped in the midst of the eight Mātṛkās.
With her gaping mouth, she licked repeatedly, and the world was scorched by her flames;
by the force of her repeated breaths, she shook the great mountain ranges.
In one place He hates, in another He is angry, and in another He forcibly withdraws;
in one place He creates, in another He protects—His independent will proceeds [thus].
The goddess is adorned with serpent-ornaments and decorated by the lords of serpents;
she holds a noose and a goad, and her hands grant boons and fearlessness.
In his left hands he holds a sword that causes the three worlds to tremble,
and in his right hands an extremely fierce khaṭvāṅga and an excellent trident.
Furthermore, he held a fierce head in his left hand, filled with blood; indeed, it was shaven, dripping with gore, and still possessed its hair.
In her left [hand], however, is a divine flask that illuminates with great jewels;
this is the goddess Pratyaṅgirā, according to the instruction of the King of Tantras.
This very Mahādevī Pratyaṅgirā, the Fortune of Success who bestows victory, abides pervading the divine realm through her manifold divisions.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Three handfuls of joined palms.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. I worship the sandals. [The offering: balih.
Gāyatrī: Khphreṃ! We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon her who possesses ninety [verses]; may that Lakṣmī inspire us. The Bali offering.
Now, the garland mantra (mālāmantra).

Oṃ, homage to all the yogins of all accomplishments; homage to all the mothers of all accomplishments; homage to the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakālī, the mistress of the entire wheel of families, who is gladdened by eternal, arisen bliss. It is as follows: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! Oṃ, O Supreme Haṃsinī, Goddess who bestows the path to Nirvāṇa!

O Goddess, who pacifies calamitous afflictions, who shatters all misfortunes and the eight afflictions, who is a boat across the ocean of all disasters, and who crushes all enemies—come! Laugh! Leap! O devourer of human blood, entrails, and fat, [devour] my own enemies!
Crush, crush! Eat! Pierce with the trident! Cut! Strike with the sword! Sever!
Accomplish all my desires until they are fulfilled, O most compassionate Blessed One, wearer of the form of Mahābhairava, praised by the best of the thirty gods, Mother of all mantras!
O Goddess Mahākālī, who are compassionate toward those who bow before you, O destroyer of Time (Kāla)! Hūṃ!
Make the daughter of the gods and asuras one whose sprout of passion is pacified; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! With this, the offering (bali) is made. Thus is the garland mantra (mālāmantra).
The Six Limbs: Khphreṃ, homage to the heart; Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head.
Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the topknot (śikhā). Khphreṃ, hūṃ to the armor (kavaca). Khphreṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes (tratrāya).
KH PHREṂ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ ||
Now follows the thousand-syllable mantra of Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, which restores lost people.

Oṃ hrīṃ! O Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, whose mouth is ablaze, whose tongue is a flame, who dwells in caves, O Bhīmā, O most terrifyingly formidable one, O Laṃbodarī, O ender of the universe, O devourer of time, O destroyer of Time, O Hrāsinī, O Mahābhairavī, O dweller in the fearsome great cremation ground, hūṃ! O Caṇḍamukhī!

O Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī! Hrīṃ Rkṣrīṃ Vrīṃ Phaṭ! O Mahāharjabharuṭṭi! O Mahārāvinī! Haṃsanī! Grāhinī! Māriṇī! Mohinī! Hūṃ Jāḥ! Devourer! O Drāvini! Go away! Rkṣrīṃ! O dweller in the lap of Mahābhairava! O eater of great flesh! Drive her away! Truta! O Mahākālī!

Thrāṃ dhraṃ hrīṃ! O you who hold a staff in your hand, O Khārvāri, Mahānauli, Brahmāṇī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, Yāmyā, Caṇḍamukhī, Āgneyī, Vāruṇī, Vāyavyā, Kolamukhī, Khphreṃ! O Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, Mahākāpālinī, Bhairaveśvarī!

O Caṇḍaśvarī, O you who arise from the great wind, O devourer of the Great Destroyer (Kṛtānta), O you who bring joy to the hearts of all yoginīs! [To you] whose body is ablaze with flames, HŪṂ R̥KṢRĪṂ PHAṬ!
O you who trample upon the skin of the great end-maker of men, O you who possess the sound of the great PHAṬKĀRA, Slay! HŪṂ! O Ḍamukhī, O burner, O you with the conch-like neck!

O you who wear earrings made of serpents; O most terrifying one with most terrifying armlets; O you whose face is most terrifying with wrath; O you whose hair and mouth are ablaze; O Mahācaṇḍā Cāmuṇḍā; O Mahācaṇḍālī; O you who bear the Kirāta and Ucchuṣma; laugh and dance! O you who cause terror to the three great worlds; O you who consume blood, fat, and marrow; drink!
O Vāmā! Strike! O Hā! Release! O Khallvā! Burst! Roar! Reel!

O you who possess great intoxication and other [states]! O you who dwell in the cremation ground! O abode of Mahābhairava! Laugh, O five-faced one! O you with ten staff-like arms! O wielder of all weapons! O Mahādāmarī!

O you whose great arms are adorned with a trident, a khaṭvāṅga, a sword, a skull-topped staff, a noose, a goad, a begging bowl, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness; O you whose body is decorated with great serpents; O you who possess many faces; O you who dwell in the sky, in lightning, and in the void; O you of great splendor; O you who are terrifying with your great fangs; O you whose face is a mouth of flames; O you whose mouth is a skull; O you who obstruct the vultures!

O you who dwell in the water of the heart-lotus, destroy the minds of all beings! *Rphrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. Seated upon the great skull-throne, *hūṃ pha*. O you whose body possesses the splendor of a thousand suns, *hūṃ phaṭ*. Pure as ten million moons, *hūṃ phaṭ*. O you whose body is like the fire at the end of the great dissolution, *hūṃ phaṭ*. *Turu hūṃ*.

*Phaṭ*! *Prasphura*! *Rhrūṃ rphraṃ phaṭ*, O Sovereign Queen of the Great Mantra-Kings, *phaṭ phaṭ*! *Meghamāle*, O Great Illusionist, *hūṃ phaṭ*! *Māheśvari*, O Goddess of the Ten Million Lightnings, *kṣe hūṃ phaṭ*! *Kṣapayaduritāma*, O Destroyer of Sins, *hūṃ phaṭ*! *Bhīme*, O Terrible One, come, come! *Hrūṃ hrūṃ phaṭ*! *Hrīṃ*, O Great Fierce One!
Yogeśvarī, Hūṃ Phaṭ! O you whose body is smeared with great ashes;
O Mistress of the *Ḍāmara* of the three worlds, whose limbs are filled with the entrails of the great *naraka* demons; O Beloved, who drinks the wine of blood;
O Devourer who swallows the three worlds; O Goddess seated upon a buffalo throne, whose body rests upon the limbs of a jar-born being; O Aghoreśvarī!

O you of excellent blue descent, O most terrible one with a mouth made fearsome by tusks, O you who are the thunderbolt for horses, elephants, and donkeys, O you who are the thunderbolt for great flesh, O intoxicated one, slay!
Hūṃ! O fierce-faced one, sovereign of all yoginīs, great illusionist of horrific form, Hrīṃ! O great fierce sovereign of yoginīs, Ṭhrīṃ Dhrāṃ Thrīṃ!

Phaṭ! O dweller at the end of the sixteen digits; O mover within half of half the letter *ha*; O abode of the universe, O devourer of the universe; O you who cause trembling, O you who cause [all] to tremble; O beloved of the one with the thunderbolt-like voice; O drawer-in of Time; O abode of all sciences; O infallible one; O unconquered one; O you whose face is that of the Mother of All; O mother of great bliss; O you whose ears hear the bliss of nectar; O eternal one! Phat! Svāhā!
Hrīṃ kroṃ nrjmhīṃ rvkṣrīṃ rvrūṃdra phaṭ svāhā! To those [deities] is this offering (bali).
[Thus ends the venerable, venerable, venerable Siddhilakṣmīsahasrākṣarī-vidyā.]
Now, one should not worship the Śrī-Śrī-Śrī-Lakṣmī Ayutākṣarī Vidyā [without this].
Oṃ, homage to Siddhilakṣmī! Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ || Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ ||
Oṃ tatsat || Oṃ tatsat || Oṃ tatsat ||

Oṃ. Of this Śrī Siddhilakṣmī Ayutākṣaramālā mantra, Bharadvāja is the ṛṣi; the meters are madhyā, apratiṣṭhā, supratiṣṭhā, gāyatrī, uṣṇih, anuṣṭubh, bṛhatī, paṅkti, triṣṭubh, jagatī, atiśarkarī, śarkarī, prakṛti, and atikṛti.

The deity is Śrī Siddhilakṣmī; *phreṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *khphreṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *kroṃ* is the heart-essence (*krīlaka*). This is the application (*viniyoga*) for recitation (*japa*) for the sake of attaining the accomplishments (*siddhi*) of worldly enjoyment (*bhukti*) and liberation (*mukti*).

Eṃ oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ, O Blessed One, Caṇḍakāpālinī, Siddhilakṣmī, Pratyaṅgirā! Kṣoṃ kroṃ klīṃ śrīṃ strīṃ! O you of the red face, you who laugh with a terrible roar, you who possess a fearsome sound, you who remove the suffering of those who bow before you! Āṃ krīṃ hauṃ kṣauṃ glauṃ! O dweller in the cremation ground, whose body is as white as a moonbeam, you who deliver devoted people!

Phreṃ khphreṃ hsphreṃ hskhphreṃ hsauṃḥ! O Kātyāyanī, who moves in the state of union with the supreme Sadāśiva; O Kāpālinī, Great Yoginī, white as a jasmine flower and the moon, possessing the form of Mahārudra, mounted upon a corpse; Kroṃ kṣroṃ glūṃ glauṃ vlūṃ! O you who delight the minds of all the gods, asuras, and kinnaras!
O shatterer of the pride of the Daityas and Dānavas; O bearer of five faces; O wearer of a garland of human skulls;

O bestower of the fruits of the four aims of life; O singer of the *carcarī* with hand-claps; O you who utter *hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hreṃ hroṃ*; O fierce one, more fierce than the fierce, most terrifying with a dreadful roar; O illuminator of the knowledge of the three great principles!

O you who cause great laughter that terrifies the fourteen worlds; thrīṃ thrīṃ hrīṃ dhrāṃ nrīṃ; O you adorned with ten staff-like arms bold in granting fearlessness to the three worlds; O you who are the source of supreme sovereignty; O beautiful-eyed consort of Bhūteśvara; O you resplendent with three eyes; phreṃ phreṃ khphreṃ hsphreṃ hskhphreṃ.
O Pracaṇḍacaṇḍinī, whose body is as white as snow and the kunda flower yet possesses the luster of a great sapphire cloud,

you who are the descent of the Śakti-tattva of Pratyaṅgirā, most terrifying, with long, hanging limbs, you who perform the *carcarī* dance and clapping of hands, and who have terrified the three worlds by the observance of the *samaya*, [you who are] accumulated through births beginningless.
O you who cause the accumulation of evil, O you who ferry one across the ocean of the great hells!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! O Royal Lakṣmī, Victory Lakṣmī, Great Lakṣmī, Wealth Lakṣmī, Siddhi Lakṣmī! Conquer! Live! Speak! Flash forth! O crusher of all enemies, O Great Illusion! Hrīṃ!
HŪṂ PHREṂ PHAṬ! O you who devour millions of cosmic eggs, O Great Roar! HRĪṂ HŪṂ PHREṂ PHAṬ!
O you who consist of the supreme state of union with Śiva, O Great Terrifying One! HRĪṂ HŪṂ PHREṂ PHAṬ!
O you who roam the great cremation grounds, O Fortunate One! HRĪṂ HŪṂ PHREṂ PHAṬ!

O you who shatter the suffering of great poverty, *mahāhāse*! *Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ*! O you whose form is absolute liberation (*kaivalya*), who illumines your own state, *mahāghore*! *Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ*! O you who bestow the fruits of the four aims of life, *mahācaṇḍe*! *Hrīṃ hūṃ pheṃ phaṭ*! O you who are radiant with the burden of a great mass of matted hair, *mahāgrāse*! *Hrīṃ hūṃ*!
Phreṃ Phaṭ! O Great Compassionate One, Mistress of the entire wheel of Kula and Akula, Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ!
O Great Vidyā, whose body consists of the qualities of pure *sattva*, Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ! O Liberator from the bonds of *saṃsāra*, who has transcended all parts (*kalātīta*), Hrīṃ Hūṃ!
Phreṃ Phaṭ! O you who have created the five-fold fire of time, in the great light, Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ!
O you adorned with the circle of great staff-like arms, in the abode of Rudra, Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ!
O you whose splendor protects the fourteen worlds, O you of great power, Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ! O you whose face is a blazing fire!

O you of terrible form, observer of the great vow! Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O crusher of gods and demons! O you of great cosmic cycles! Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O you whose power is manifested in the Age of Truth! O great dancer! Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ!
O you who recline on the couch of Rudra! O victor in battle! O you who are absorbed in the Supreme Brahman! Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, obeisance!

O companion of Paraśiva, wearer of a garland of human skulls, granter of the fulfillment of desires, Oṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ, obeisance! O you who are as white as a conch shell, camphor, or cow’s milk; O you whose curved fangs are as bright as snow and long-sharpened;
O you whose state is known by the gods beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, Oṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ, obeisance!

O bestower of auspiciousness upon the entire world, bestower of various and complete sovereign powers, resting on the body of Your own beloved in the form of Śiva; Oṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ, salutations to You whose form consists of ninety million mantras, who have subdued all the hosts of Daityas, and who extend grace to those who possess devotion; Oṃ!

KṢOṂ KROṂ NAMAH! O you whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire; O liberator from the bonds of saṃsāra; O you who cause the Śikhin-āgama to shine forth! OṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ NAMAH! O you who dwell in the most terrifying wilderness; O you of the fierce laugh that produces fear in the three worlds; O you who sport in the state of identity with Paraśiva! OṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ NAMAH!
O you whose majesty is renowned in the Vedas and Vedāntas, who dwell within the great forest [of the heart], where the great roar of the terrifying elephant [of Māyā] resounds; Oṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ, homage!
You who have utterly uprooted the opposing views fabricated by the imagination through your skill in the conceptualization of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
O protector of devotees! Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! You who are neither too tall nor short, yet full-figured; you who possess the wisdom of the ocean at the time of universal dissolution;
you who wear the rags from the shrouds of corpses in the great cremation ground! Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! You whose waist is encircled by a tiger-skin garment;
you who dance at the time of the great dissolution; you who are a warrior-hero in the battle against the seven oceans unified as one!

Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! Victory, O Mahāyogeśvarī, born of yoga, attainable through yoga, transcending yoga, whose form is yoga! Śrīṃ klīṃ strīṃ svāhā! Victory, victory, O Mahājñāneśvarī, born of knowledge, attainable through knowledge, transcending knowledge, whose form is knowledge! Śrīṃ klīṃ strīṃ svāhā!
Victory, victory, O Great Mistress of Mantras! O You who are born of mantra, accessible through mantra, transcending mantra, and whose form is mantra!

Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Great Mistress of Siddhis! O You who are born of siddhi, accessible through siddhi, transcending siddhi, and whose form is siddhi! Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Great Sovereign of All!

O you who transcend desire, O you whose form is desire, Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Great Mistress of Liberation, O Source of Liberation, O Goal of Liberation, O you who transcend liberation, O you whose form is liberation, Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Great Mistress of Nirvāṇa, O Source of Nirvāṇa, O Goal of Nirvāṇa, O you who transcend Nirvāṇa!

In the form of Nirvāṇa: Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Mahākālyeśvarī! O source of Kaivalya-Śambhu, O she who is to be attained through Kaivalya, O she who transcends Kaivalya, O you whose form is Kaivalya! Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ! Victory, O Jīva! O Triśūlinī! O Mahābalinī! O devourer of the world! Hūṃ Phaṭ! Namaḥ!

Svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! O you who cause life to live! O you who transcend the qualities of nature! O deluder of the supreme Sadāśiva! O bestower of the essence of liberation! O you who cause the bliss of consciousness and pure sattva-attribute to flourish!
Hūṃ phaṭ! Namaḥ svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! O you who cause life to live! O you who cause life to live!

O you adorned by the great Naga kings, with ten staff-like arms, who have severed the bodies of all Daityas and Dānavas with a most fierce and terrible sword, whose bow is drawn incessantly with hard arrows—HŪṂ PHAṬ!
NAMAH SVĀHĀ! OṂ HRĪṂ HŪṂ HĀṂ PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ! Victory! Victory! Live! Live!
O you who are beyond the reach of the mind, the senses, and the domain of speech;
O you whose entire body consists of the three *guṇas*; O you clad in a tiger skin—*hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā*.
*Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ*, victory! Victory! Live! Live! O you resplendent with a mass of trembling matted locks, [white] as snow and jasmine...

O Candraghana-sākambhu, far from old age, birth, death, and the snares of saṃsāra, HŪM PHAṬ NAMAḤ SVĀHĀ OM HRĪṂ HŪṂ HĀṂ PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you who are hidden within the supreme secret, O you who are the reality of the Śiva-Śakti principle, both transcendent and immanent, O experience of self-bliss! SVĀNANDĀNUBHAVA!
Hūṃ Phaṭ Namaḥ Svāhā! Salutation to the one who is established in the state of self-luminosity, seated upon the couch of the play of aesthetic harmony (sāmarasya).

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ jaya jaya jīva jīva, O you who transcend both Prakṛti and Puruṣa, O witness of the supreme liberation, O protectress of the three worlds, O devourer of Daityas and Dānavas, hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ jaya jaya jīva jīva, O you who set in motion the entire wheel of the Kaula doctrine!
O you who cause fear to all the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas; O Great Plague, who turns back the terror of enemy armies, famine, and great portents!
Hūṃ Phaṭ! Namaḥ Svāhā! Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ! Victory, victory! Live, live!
To her who has mastered the employment of various divine weapons; who is a bird within the cage consisting of mantras of the six Āmnāyas;
who has made all serpents her ornaments for her entire body; *hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ jaya jaya jīva jīva*.

O you who transcend all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), who are partless and of the nature of the fourth state (*turīya*), who are an unbroken stream of the nectar of supreme self-awareness and bliss, the essence of the truth of the Vedas and Agamas—*Hūṃ Phaṭ Namaḥ Svāhā*. Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ! Victorious, victorious! O bestower of the eight supernatural powers (*siddhi*) beginning with the Great Sky-walker (*mahākhecarī*), you who have arisen from the Ocean of Milk! *Jīva Jīva!* (Be alive, be alive! *Namaḥ Svāhā*. *Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Jaya Jaya Jīva Jīva Mahākhecarīprabhṛtisiddhyaṣṭakapradāyini Kṣīrodārṇavodbhūta*.
O Goddess Sudhā, who drinks the essence of the supreme nectar; O Illusionist, who binds the multitude of beings born within the belly of the three worlds;
Hūṃ Phaṭ! Homage! Svāhā! Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ! Victory! Victory! Live! Live!
O You whose lotus feet are to be worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; O You who have gone forth adorned with offerings of human skulls!

O you who are capable of enduring all gods and asuras, O you of great strength! Hūṃ Phaṭ! Namaḥ Svāhā! Victory, victory in the Satya Yuga, O Pratyamgira! Victory, victory in the Tretā Yuga, O Siddhilakṣmī! Victory, victory in the Dvāpara Yuga, O Rājyalakṣmī! Victory, victory in the Kali Yuga!

O Caṇḍakāpālinī! Oṃ aiṃ āṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃ! O Blessed One, be gracious! Blaze! Flare up! Quiver! Tremble! Crack! Crackle! Sing! Laugh! Dance! Kaha! Kili! Kici! Hasten! Run! Hūṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ hrīṃ! O you with hair like the sky, with hair like lightning, with tawny hair! Phaṭ svāhā! Hūṃ phreṃ!

*phaṭ svāhā hūṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ hrīṃ*, O You who have overturned the seven continents with a kick of Your foot; *phaṭ svāhā hūṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ hrīṃ*, O You whose lotus feet are worshipped by the gods, O You who have made the tortoise bow down beneath the weight of Your tread, O You who preside over the inner hearts of all beings, O You whose true nature is beyond the scope of the Vedas, Āgamas, Itihāsas, and Purāṇas; *phaṭ svāhā hūṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ hrīṃ*.

O dispeller of the heart’s torment of devotees; O savior of all beings, both moving and unmoving, who are overwhelmed by the threefold suffering; O Sun-disk that alone illumines the lotus-heart of the God of gods; *phaṭ svāhā*. *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ chrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ strīṃ hūṃ hauṃ hoṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ phreṃ khphreṃ*.
All the Daityas, Dānavas, Asuras, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, Kuṣmāṇḍas, Ḍākinīs, Śākinīs, Skandas, Vināyakas, Ghonakas, Kṣetrapālas, Vetālas, Brahmarākṣasas, Gandharvas,
Guhyakas, serpents, Nāgas, planets, lunar mansions, spirits, and the three kinds of portents.
The paralyzing, deluding, and subjugating [of threats] such as thieves, fire, forest-dwelling beasts of prey, war, thunderbolts, lightning strikes from the clouds during rain,
poison, secondary poisons, malevolent magic, epidemics, *śaraka* (fever), deceit, famine, the destruction of cities, and regional calamities.

And out of hatred, [he may cause] expulsion, possession, roaring, whirlpools of rivers and oceans, or being carried away by wildernesses; or by day or night, [he may cause harm] to worms, insects, moths, land-dwelling creatures, spiders, lice, two-footed beings,
four-footed beings, six-footed beings, eight-footed beings, many-footed beings, terrible darkness, or great pestilence.

O Goddess, protect me, guard me, preserve me, sustain me, save me, and shield me from those who seize by the hair, from those who cause harm, from those who steal all possessions, from deceitful and wicked people, from thieves, from rogues, from those who roam by day, from those who roam by night, from those who roam at twilight, from horned beasts, from those with fangs, from firebrands, and from various other calamities.
Uplift! Grant fearlessness! Be gracious! [Name], drink! Subdue the enemies!

Eradicate them! Cut them down! Break them! Slay them! Destroy them! Kill them! Expel them! Paralyze them! Grind them to pieces! Annihilate them! Pierce them! Wither them! Put them to flight! Terrify them! Delude them! Cause them to wander in confusion!
Split! Smash! Seize! Agitate! Crush! Intoxicate! Turu! Hilī! Kici! Burn!
Devour! Cut! Grind to powder! Pound! Steal! Break! Reduce to ashes! Draw forth! Cast down! Shake! O Uddhe! Conquer! Cause to enter!
Madden! Terrify! Mow down! Leap upon! Release! Drink! Consume! Establish [it] in your own skull! *vlauṃ* O Blessed One! *glauṃ* O Great Fierce One! *kṣauṃ* O Tearer!
*kṣrīṃ* O She Who Wears a Garland of Heads! *kṣrūṃ* O Great Devourer! *rhrīṃ* O Pārvatī! *rhrūṃ* O Great Elemental One! *rkṣrīṃ*!
O serpent-like one, O you with tinkling bells, *ṛkṣrūṃ*, O dweller in the netherworld, O you who move within the nine seed-syllables, O Kokāmukhī, *hūṃ*;
O red-beaked one, *hūṃ*; O support of Rudra, *hūṃ*; O bear-eared one, *hūṃ*; O Jālandharī, *hūṃ*; O you of lightning luster, *hūṃ*;
O moon-faced one, *hūṃ*; O Śavarī, O Kirātī, *hūṃ*; O wielder of the corpse-weapon, *hūṃ*; O beloved of the milk-ocean, *hūṃ*.

Hūṃ! O you who crave the state of equanimity; Hūṃ! O you who wander upon Kailāsa; Hūṃ! O you who are the wish-fulfilling vine for devotees; Hūṃ! O you who grant all desires; Hūṃ! O you who bestow the eight great supernatural attainments; Hūṃ! O you who confer the sovereignty of a kingdom; Hūṃ! O Queen of the Kings of Kings; Hūṃ! O you whose side-glances are like lightning; Hūṃ! O you who are immersed in the ocean of nectar; Hūṃ! O bearer of jewels, wielder of the thunderbolt; Hūṃ! O Mahāḍāmarī!
Hūṃ, O you who are intent on the service of devotees! Hūṃ, O bestower of the fruits of the four aims of life!
Hūṃ, O you who grant liberation to those who have offered half [of their merit]! Svāhā!
Oṃ, O you who are beyond the senses! Grant me the attainment of siddhis! Svāhā!
Oṃ, in the state beyond the fourth, reveal your own nature, svāhā!
Oṃ, in the form of consciousness and bliss, bestow the essence of knowledge, svāhā!
Oṃ, in the nature of sound and the point, manifest yoga, svāhā!
Oṃ, O you whose form consists of pure consciousness, manifest omniscience, svāhā!
Oṃ, O you whose body consists of mantra, contemplate the state of equilibrium between Śiva and Śakti, svāhā!
Oṃ, O little lamp of knowledge, dispel the darkness of ignorance, svāhā!
Oṃ, O you who consist of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahma), establish all knowledge; svāhā!
Oṃ, O you who are the form of the forest fire of saṃsāra, remove birth and death; svāhā!
Oṃ, O you who are like a mother to your devotees, pacify my miserable state; svāhā!
Oṃ, O you whose nature is the triple Veda, liberate me from sin, svāhā!
Oṃ, O you who dwell within all as the inner controller, grant devotion unto me, svāhā!
Oṃ, O you who know all intentions, unite me with the three aims of life (trivarga), svāhā!
Oṃ, O you of gracious and beautiful countenance, bestow the excellence of form, svāhā!
Oṃ, O lioness of the Vedas, scriptures, and forests, dispel my sense of "mine" and egoism, svāhā!
Oṃ, having been empowered by the nine-syllable mantra, deliver me from all calamities, svāhā!
Oṃ, O shatterer of all calamities, bring about welfare for us all, svāhā!

Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃ, obeisance to you who are upon the solar seat, whose form is radiance, phaṭ! Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃ, obeisance to you who are upon the lunar seat, whose form is moonlight, phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauḥ sauḥ, obeisance to you, O Jvālārūpā, seated upon sin, phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you, O Sṛṣṭirūpā, seated upon the golden womb (Hiraṇyagarbha), phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you, O Sthitirūpā, seated upon Nārāyaṇa, phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you who are seated upon the Great Bhairava throne, whose form is dissolution; phaṭ.
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you who are seated upon the Vedic throne, whose form is Gāyatrī; phaṭ.
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you who are seated upon the sacrificial throne, whose form is the fire-oblation; phaṭ.
Oṃ klīṃ āṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you, O seat of conduct, whose form is Dharma; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you, O seat of rain, whose form is rain; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you, O seat of food, whose form is life-force; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you, the seat of mantra, whose nature is initiation; phaṭ! Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you, the seat of the vow, whose nature is austerity; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you, the infinite seat, whose nature is the earth; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you who are seated on the formless seat, whose nature is space; phaṭ.
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you who are seated on the seat of the three worlds, whose nature is all-power; phaṭ.
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, obeisance to you who are seated on the seat of all sentient beings, whose nature is movement; phaṭ.
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, salutations to you, O Yogarūpā, seated upon the Mūlādhāra; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ, salutations to you, O Nityoditānandarūpā, seated upon the Brahmāsana; phaṭ!
Aiṃ rphrīṃ rphrūṃ rchrīṃ rchrūṃ trīṃ thrīṃ drīṃ dhrīṃ nrīṃ aiṃ, [salutations to] Pravṛtti...

O Pratyamgirā *Phreṃ Khphreṃ*, you are the one who sets the two paths in motion, who reveals the three forms, and who is the greatness within the Vajra-mantra that is to be known through the six traditions beginning with the Vedas; *Phreṃ Khphreṃ*, you are Siddhilakṣmī;
*Phreṃ Khphreṃ*, you are Rājyalakṣmī; *Phreṃ Khphreṃ*, you are Caṇḍakāpālinī.

Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Guhyakālī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, Bhadrakālī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Kāmakalākālī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Tripurasundarī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Rājamātaṅgī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Kubjikā; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Harasiddhā; Phreṃ.

Khphreṃ! You are Bālā; Phreṃ Khphreṃ! You are Tārā; Phreṃ Khphreṃ! You are Bhairavī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ! You are Cāmuṇḍā; Phreṃ Khphreṃ! You are Chinnamastā; Phreṃ Khphreṃ! You are Ugracaṇḍā; Phreṃ Khphreṃ! You are Caṇḍeśvarī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ! You are Bhuvaneśvarī.

Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Mahiṣamardinī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Vāgeśvarī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Śivādūtī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Mahālakṣmī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Rājarājeśvarī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are Svarṇakūṭeśvarī; Phreṃ Khphreṃ, you are...

O Jayajhaṃkeśvarī, *phreṃ khphreṃ*, you are Uchiṣṭacāṇḍālinī; *pheṃ khphreṃ*, you are Kālarātrī; *phreṃ khphreṃ*, you are Kṣamaṅkarī; *phreṃ khphreṃ*, you are Vābhravī; *phreṃ khphreṃ*, you are Raktadaṃtikā; *phreṃ khphreṃ*, you are [such-and-such].

Aparājitā pheṃ khphreṃ eṃ oṃ auṃ hyaḥ sphāṃ. O you whose form is Nivṛtti, your form is impossible to drink; oṃ, you are bodiless, without senses, and devoid of form, taste, smell, touch, and sound—oṃ oṃ, you are without birth or death, and beyond speech.
You are the state of speechlessness, non-grasping, non-going, non-excretion, and non-sexuality—of the feet, anus, and genitals;
*om om*. You are that which pervades the three functions, consisting of three syllables, and having three eyes; *om om*, you are that reality (*tattvam asi*).
You are the salutation (*namaḥ*) of the Vedas (*nigama*), the beginning of all things, devoid of the letter 'a'; *om om*, you are that reality.
Oṃ Oṃ! You are changeless, stainless, desireless, limbless, and devoid of qualities;
you are the Reality—Oṃ Oṃ! You are eternal, the witness of all, hidden within all beings, the sovereign of all, and the one to be worshipped by all;
you are the Reality.
Oṃ Oṃ! You are Existence-Consciousness-Bliss, eternal, composed of the quality of purity (sattva), accompanied by your retinue, possessing equal vision; "That thou art," Oṃ Oṃ!
You are absolute, the very form of liberation, beyond all conceptualization, pervading time yet devoid of time; "That thou art," Oṃ Oṃ!
You are undivided, unperceived, unattached, beyond the senses, non-dual, indivisible, blissful, and without cause.
That art thou.

Om Om. You are devoid of temporal relation, immutably fixed, free from mental construction, devoid of conceptualization, beyond causes, not accompanied by karma, and knowable through pure experience alone; That art thou.

Oṃ Oṃ! You are free from conceptual proliferation (*niṣprapañcā*), pure, awakened, eternal, true, and liberated by nature; you consist of immediate consciousness (*pratyakcaitanya*), are devoid of modification or transformation, are abandoned by the powers of concealment and distraction, and are free from the delusion of ignorance consisting of maturation, hatred, and passion—you are That (*tat tvam asi*).

Oṃ Oṃ! You are the perfect reality (tatva), consisting of eternal knowledge, will, action, great prosperity, cessation [of worldly activity], dispassion, and sovereignty. Oṃ Oṃ! You are the reality devoid of limiting adjuncts (upādhi), egoism (ahaṅkāra), mind (manas), latent impressions (vāsanā), the womb (yoni), consciousness (citta), intellect (buddhi), and natural emission (nisarga).

Oṃ Oṃ! You are that which is connected to the means of valid cognition (pramāṇa), conviction (pratyaya), existence (sattā), the ultimate truth (paramārtha), subtle manifestation (sūkṣmābhāsa), and the causal sign (nimitta-hetu).

*Tattvamasi* (That art thou). *Oṃ Oṃ*. You are the witness of the dissolution of the mind into the unity of consciousness, which is the cessation of both the existent and the non-existent, and the awakening of memory. *Tattvamasi* (That art thou). *Oṃ Oṃ*. You are that which is denoted by the word "Brahman," the one, attributeless, and ineffable. *Tattvamasi* (That art thou).
Oṃ Oṃ! You are the Reality (Tattvamasi), established in the relationship of the signified and the signifier, the bestower of the secret of the covenant between Śiva and Śakti.

Oṃ Oṃ! In the succession of states consisting of Nirvāṇa, Kaivalya, Amṛta, Mukti, Niḥśreyasa, Apavarga, Mokṣa, Layasāmarasa, Sāyujya, and the experience of the inner bliss of identity (Pratyagānanda-tādātmya).
O giver of the state [of liberation], "That thou art" (tat tvam asi),

Oṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ Hauṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Phreṃ Khphreṃ Hsphreṃ Hskhphreṃ, salutations to the Mother of all mantras, the progenitor of the universe, O you of supreme compassion, whose mind is filled with mercy!
O you who bring benefit to all, who rescue [beings] from the ocean of saṃsāra consisting of the latent impressions of birth and death,
who move in two forms, who are sung under various names to reveal those respective states— *aiṃ*, you are the ground of yoga; *oṃ*,
you are beyond the reach of the senses.

Hrīṃ, you are free from conceptualization; Śrīṃ, you are the state of Śambhu; Klīṃ, you are the fourth state (turīya); Strīṃ, you are liberation (nirvāṇa); Śrīṃ, you are beyond rebirth; Hūṃ, you are the supreme Self, the essence of sound and the point; Hauṃ, you are eternally manifest, the indivisible supreme bliss; Kṣoṃ, you are the form of inward-consciousness; Kroṃ, you are changeless and stainless; Phreṃ.
O Śuddhanityā, you are the totality; *khphreṃ*. You have transcended the three times; *hsphreṃ*.

You are non-different from the individual self (*jīvātman*) and the supreme self (*paramātman*); *hskhphreṃ*. You are the experience of the unmanifest; *namaḥ*. You are the nectar of liberation (*kaivalya*); you are the accomplishment of the enjoyment of form (*sākārābhoga-siddhi*), the bestower of heaven; *rhkṣmlvryū īṃ*.

You are intent on the desire to create; rhkṣmlvryūṁ, you perform the act of primordial creation; śkṣmlvryīṁ, you perform the act of elemental creation; śkṣmlvryīṁ, you perform the act of the transverse creation; hskṣmlvryūṁ, you perform the act of protection; hskṣmlvryūṁ, you perform the act of protection; hskṣmlvryūṁ, you perform the act of withdrawal; hsklhrīṁ, you perform the act of establishing order; hskhlhrīṁ.
Sklhrīṃ, you who perform the six postures; Rjjhrkṣrīṃ, you who maintain the boundaries; you who perform the qualities through union with clothing;
you who are beyond qualities yet possess qualities; you who are formless and inconceivable; Phreṃ Phreṃ Phreṃ, O Yoginī of all Siddhis;
Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Hrīṃ, O Mother of all Siddhis; Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ, eternally arisen and rejoicing in bliss; Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ.

O leader of the entire circle of families! *Kroṃ kroṃ kroṃ*, O Blessed One Caṇḍakāpālinī! *Hauṃ hauṃ hauṃ*, O Supreme Haṃsinī, bestower of the path to Nirvāṇa! *Hāṃ hāṃ hāṃ*, O pacifier of all calamities and misfortunes! *Kṣoṃ kṣoṃ kṣoṃ*, O destroyer of all evils, portents, and afflictions! *Āṃ āṃ āṃ*, O savior from the ocean of all dangers!

Śrīṃ Śrīṃ Śrīṃ, the destroyer of all enemies; Klīṃ Klīṃ Klīṃ, the consumer of human blood, entrails, and fat; Strīṃ Strīṃ Strīṃ, the accomplisher of all desires; Khphreṃ Khphreṃ Khphreṃ, the supremely compassionate one who assumes the form of Mahābhairava.
Hskhphreṃ hskhphreṃ hskhphreṃ! O you who possess the excellent speech of the thirty [gods], the bestower of the mantra of the syllable *sakara*;

Aiṃ Aiṃ Aiṃ! O you who are affectionate toward those who produce virtues; O destroyer of time! Glūṃ Glūṃ Glūṃ! O you who rain down a stream of nectar; O you with a gracious countenance! Kṣrauṃ Kṣrauṃ Kṣrauṃ! O you who set in motion the wheel of the samaya of the family of the *nigamas* and *āgamas*.
Delighting in dwelling in great wildernesses, *hrauṃ hrauṃ hrauṃ*, she who removes poverty, suffering, and miserable states;
*praṇa-nena-ja*, destroyer of the despair of the Daityas, *phroṃ phroṃ phroṃ*;
adorned with ornaments of garlands of human skulls and bones, smeared with fierce, tawny, and heavy unguents, *haiṃ haiṃ haiṃ*.
Surrounded by ten million fire-mouthed spirits, she dwells in pure conduct; *hsauṃḥ hsauṃḥ hsauṃḥ*.
Her face blazes like ten million fires, her tongue and belly are a mass of flames, and from the corners of her eyes she emits sparks with fierce side-glances;
*jhraiṃ jhraiṃ jhraiṃ*. She has massive, thick, and pendulous breasts and a protruding belly.
With a navel whirling in deep eddies, she who is like a white lotus, the devourer of Time and Death,

the slayer of Yama and Antaka; *Rjhrīṃ Rjhrīṃ Rjhrīṃ*, she whose form is filled with blazing flames, the most terrifying dweller of the cremation ground, roaring like elephants, jackals, lions, and Aruṇḍa birds.
Subduer of the wicked, destroyer of Daityas and Dānavas, *rkṣrhrīṁ rkṣrhrīṁ rkṣrhrīṁ*,
you who delude all classes of living beings, dweller on the lap of the great mudrā as pure as the Milky Ocean,
eater of great flesh, *hmlvryūṁ hmlvryūṁ hmlvryūṁ*, Brahmāṇī, Māheśvarī.
Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, Nārasiṃhī, Aindrī, Cāmuṇḍā, Śivadūtī, Caṇḍayogeśvarī,
Mahākāpālinī, Kālamukhī, Yamaghaṇṭā, Karālī, Mahāyoginī, Vāruṇī, Vāyavyā, Āgneyī, Aiṃśānī, Mahātrāsakāriṇī, and Mahāpralayakāla.

Raṅganartakī, *hmkhrlhrīṃ hmkhrlhrīṃ hmkhrlhrīṃ*, she who utters the terrible roar of *hūṃ* and *hūṃ*, whose entire body is covered with a fresh human skin, whose tongue lolls out, who wields a sword as her weapon,
and whose parasol is made of a cock, a vulture, a crow, and an owl.

Sklhrkhrīṃ sklhrkhrīṃ sklhrkhrīṃ! O Mahāḍāmarī Phetkāriṇī, whose body is white, blue, yellow, and red; whose form is adorned with the coils of serpents; who possesses infinite millions of faces, eyes, hands, and feet; hsgkṣmlvryūṃ hsgkṣmlvryūṃ hsgkṣmlvryūṃ! You who are fashioned from the syllables A, U, and M.
Moving within the house, seated upon the great lion-throne of the vast sky, garlanded with skeletons and bones, roaring terribly—
*mglkṣmhrhrū(-)īṁ mglkṣmhrhrū(-)īṁ mglkṣmhrhrū(-)īṁ*— the plump one, the fisherwoman, the *ḍākinī*,
the *śākinī*, the yoginī, the womb-born, the enjoyer, she who intoxicates with passion, and she who destroys misfortune and suffering.

Rkṣrmchrīṃ Rkṣrmchrīṃ Rkṣrmchrīṃ! Jambhinī, Stambhinī, Mohinī, Dohinī, Nāyikā, Gāyikā, Tapinī, Tāpinī, Karālī, Vikarālī, Āveśinī, Praveśinī, Dharaṇī, Dhāriṇī, Rjjhrkṣrīṃ Rjjhrkṣrīṃ Rjjhrkṣrīṃ! O Sarvabhūtadamanī, Mahādaṃṣṭrākalālā, Kalarātri!
She whose radiance is equal to ten million suns,

who is adorned with the unbearable flames of the fire of the great dissolution, who holds all weapons in her hands, who is the one who subdues the three worlds by force, who is the bee at the lotus-heart of Śiva, she is Śvetavārāhī and Raktacāmuṇḍā.

khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ, O Sovereign of all Vidyās, White Sarasvatī! oṃ oṃ oṃ hrīṃ oṃ hūṃ oṃ hāṃ oṃ phreṃ oṃ kṣoṃ oṃ kroṃ oṃ na oṃ maḥ, O you who cause the joy of the universe by roaring within the world, O refuge of the world, O embodiment of the world, O protectress of the world, O destroyer of the world, O one worthy of the world’s worship! hrīṃ oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hāṃ hrīṃ.

Phreṃ hrīṃ kṣoṃ hrīṃ kroṃ hrīṃ na hrīṃ maḥ | O Durgā, crusher of the Daitya Durga, deliverer from distress, shatterer of difficulties, destroyer of misfortune, accomplisher of difficult tasks, compassionate toward those in distress! Hūṃ oṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hāṃ hūṃ phreṃ hūṃ kṣoṃ hūṃ kroṃ hūṃ na hūṃ namaḥ.

O you who observe the vow of Kaula conduct; O promoter of the Kulamārga; O crusher of the three families (trikula); O protector of the Kaulikas; O leader of the wheel of Kula and Akula; O you who find satisfaction in the substance of Kula; O destroyer of those who hate the Kula; Hāṃ Oṃ Hāṃ Hrīṃ Hāṃ Hūṃ Hāṃ Hāṃ Hāṃ Phreṃ Hāṃ Kṣoṃ Hāṃ Kroṃ Hāṃ Na Hāṃ Maḥ; O illuminator of the path of the Vedas!

O You who are to be known through the Vedas and Vedānta; O You who are to be manifested by perception alone; O You who take away all sensation; O You whose greatness is sung by the Vedas; O You who consist of the Vedas; O You who are mounted upon Rudra; O You who are established by the Vedas; O Bestower of the fruits of action—Phreṃ Oṃ Oṃ Phreṃ Hrīṃ Phreṃ Hūṃ.

Phreṃ hāṃ phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ phreṃ kroṃ phreṃ na phreṃ maḥ! O Yogīśvarī, whose abode is made in the lotus-heart of the practitioners of yoga; O you who consist of yoga, who illuminate the body through yoga, and who bring about both union with and separation from yoga; O you whose dwelling is established in the channels that bestow yoga; O you who are intent upon the granting of yoga!

KṢĀṂ OṂ KṢOṂ HRĪṂ KṢOṂ HRŪṂ KṢOṂ HĀṂ KṢOṂ PHREṂ KṢOṂ KṢOṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ KṢOṂ NA KṢOṂ MAḤ! O you who move in the supreme ultimate sky, O you whose circle of arms is supremely fierce, O illuminator of the supreme state, O initiation into the sequence of the syllables of the supreme mantra of Parāparā!

O Mistress of the fourteen worlds! O You whose form consists of the knowledge of Yoga; O You who are the primordial nature (*prakṛti*) of the Supreme Person (*paramapuruṣa*); O You whose state is colored by the transformation of supreme bliss-consciousness; O You who deliver from the greatest of perils! *Kroṃ oṃ kroṃ hrīṃ kroṃ hūṃ kroṃ hāṃ kroṃ phreṃ kroṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ kroṃ kroṃ na kroṃ maḥ*.

O you who bestow the fruits of the four aims of life; O you whose nature consists of the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of eighty-four million cosmic eggs; O you who originate the impressions of the three types of karma; O Four-faced One and Four-armed One; O you whose lotus feet are served by hosts of gods such as Bhū; O you whose observances consist of the proper conduct prescribed for the four goals of life and the four stages of life.

O you who delight in the dharma of sacrifice and oblation, O you who take pleasure in the fourfold activities of the Saṃvara cycle, O Mahābhairava, together with your consort Dharmacāriṇī; O you who dwell upon the circle of the earth encircled by the garland of the four oceans; O you who preside over the hearts of all living beings; homage to Pratyāṅgirā! Homage to her whose nature is manifest in every individual!

Salutations to you who impel the karma of perception; salutations to you who have warded off all the misfortunes of those who bow before you; salutations to you whose wisdom reflects the power of *māyā*; salutations to you in whom the mantras and yantras are worshipped limb by limb; salutations to you who are meditated upon through intuition by your devotees; salutations to you who take away the fruits of the gods as they are individually offered! Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ.

Phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. [This] nine-syllable [mantra] is formed within the entire body: Oṃ at the form-prāṇa; Hrīṃ at the head of the form; Hūṃ at the heart of the form; Hāṃ at the arms, back, and belly of the form; Phreṃ at the sides, hips, thighs, and genitals of the form; Kṣoṃ at the shanks and feet of the form; Kroṃ.

Homage to the form of the hands, feet, fingers, and nails; homage to the form of all limbs and minor members. Om! By means of the syllables A, U, and Ma, you are Nārāyaṇa, Hiraṇyagarbha, and Sadāśiva. Hrīṃ!
By means of the syllables Ha, Ka, Ra, and Pha, you are Vyoma, Agni, and Ramā. Hūṃ! By means of the syllables Ha and U.

In the form of the onset of wrath, she is "Hā," by the syllable *hā* representing the bondage of the five elements; "Phreṃ," by the syllables *pha*, *ra*, and *e* representing the splendor of the knowledge of the four aims of life; "Kṣoṃ," by the syllables *ka* and *ṣa* representing creation, maintenance, and withdrawal; and "Kroṃ," by the syllables *ka* and *ra*.

The syllable *namaḥ* consists of the letters *na*, *ma*, and the *visarga*, which take the form of the destruction of birth, old age, and death; through the *devamantra* and *homānna*, it takes the form of vital breath (*prāṇa*), life-span (*āyus*), and time (*kāla*). By means of the reverse yoga (*viparīta-yoga*), it is the Brahmā-astra, Vaiṣṇava-astra, Pāśupata-astra, Āgneya-astra, Vāruṇa-astra, Yāmya-astra, Garuḍa-astra, and Saṃhāra-astra.
O Dhāriṇī, in direct and reverse order, [there are] the forms of the thirty-three gods,
the forms of the eighteen sciences, the form of the treasure of men, the forms of the eight siddhis, the forms of the five elements,
and the forms of the three syllables. From the single form of Brahmā, Tāra is the first, Lajjā the second, and the third is [the third].

The fourth is *roṣa* (anger), the fifth is *śākinī*, the sixth is *dhāraṇā*, the seventh is *argala*, and the eighth is *praṇāma*. It is called *tāra* because it delivers one from the three types of suffering—delusion, birth, old age, death, and dwelling in the womb—and from the cycle of existence (*saṃsāra*). It is called *pāpāri* (enemy of sin) because it destroys the sins of taking what belongs to others and violence.
"From backbiting, falsehood, and disputes, one feels shame regarding the *dharmas*";
thus, from shame, pride, disrespect, humiliation, censure, joy, envy, wretchedness, and hatred, one causes anger;
[this applies] to the Vedas, *dharma*, conduct, sacrifice, austerity, mantras, foundations, and merit.
The path of the song of meditation, or its experience, is able to sustain— through the excellence of latent impressions (*vāsanā*), discipline, knowledge, dispassion,
and the certainty regarding dharma and artha— the *śākini* from among those who move on earth, in the air, in fire, in water, in the mountains, in the interior of houses, and within the limbs.

Salutation to those who cause the removal of obstacles—those consisting of false retention, weapons, evil doctrines, improper conduct, bad instruction, wrong paths, perverted intellect, faulty crafts, and flawed logic; who cause the bowing down of pride, the stabilization of the mind, and the severance of the distress of remedies and despair;
and who are opposed to all that is contrary—to them he offers salutation (*praṇāma*). This is the essence of all the *Nigamas* and *Āgamas*: Oṃ Hrīṃ.

"Hūṃ hā phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ"—this is what should be worshipped; this is the truth, the truth, the truth. "Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ" is for the Satya Yuga; "hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ" is for the Tretā Yuga; "kroṃ namaḥ" is for the Dvāpara Yuga; and "oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ" is for the Kali Yuga.
This very [mantra] is practiced by those who know the Parvas, the Nigamas, and the Āgamas.
Those desiring liberation should not study this again for the sake of rebirth; rather, this *Gāyatrī*—the essence of all the *Nigamas* and *Āgamas*—should be studied daily:
*khphreṃ*, let us know the *Siddhilakṣmī*, let us meditate upon the *Kārikā*, may that *Saṃkarṣaṇī* inspire us.

This Gāyatrī indeed consists of twenty-five syllables; it transcends the twenty-five principles. He who studies this [mantra] as the "Unfallen Companion" (anavākṣī sahacarī) attains Brahman like one who knows Brahman. *Oṃ, let us know Caṇḍakāpālinī, let us meditate upon Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī; may that Siddhilakṣmī inspire us.*

This *gāyatrī* consisting of thirty-one syllables is joined with these syllables; by studying this, one attains union (*sāyujyatā*) with Brahman: *hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ chrīṃ hsauṃḥ krīṃ kroṃ phreṃ strīṃ śrīṃ phroṃ juṃ vlauṃ vrīṃ svāhā*. This nine-syllable [mantra] is indeed the same; it is indeed studied separately.

That very mantra of sixteen spokes brings about that fruit; it attains the sixteen digits and bestows all sixteen enjoyments. Though formless and gentle, she is also most fierce; she is the bestower of the accomplishment of happiness in this world and the next. Oṃ aiṃ āṃ, giver of all knowledge! Śrīṃ hrīṃ phreṃ chrīṃ khphreṃ!
The bestower of abundant wealth, *klīṃ strīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ kroṃ vlu aiṃ kṣauṃ strīṃ*,
the cause of happiness in the home, health, and long life, *rchrīṃ njauṃ glūṃ hauṃ khroṃ hsauṃḥ sauṃḥ*,
the giver of victory over all and the destruction of enemies, as well as sovereignty, *kṣchrīṃ kluṃ glīṃ rykṣrīṃ vlauṃ*, [the destroyer] of diseases, calamities, serpents, enemies, and pestilence.

O Destroyer of Fear! Oṃ oṃ oṃ hsaḥ śauṃ! O Bestower of absolute liberation! Aiṃ aiṃ hauṃ hauṃ! O Nourisher of self-restraint, observances, austerity, yoga, knowledge, and dispassion! Hskṣmlvryūṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ! O Bestower of all undertakings, all heart’s desires, and all accomplishments! Khphreṃ khphrīṃ khphruṃ khphraiṃ!
Khphrauṃ! O you who pacify the possession by *bhūtas*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, *yakṣas*, *rakṣasas*, and *gandharvas*: Hskhphrāṃ Hskhphrīṃ Hskhphrūṃ Hskhphraiṃ Hskhphrauṃ!
O crusher of the fears of famine, pestilence, death, and foreign armies: Khāṃ Khyuṃ Khyaṃ Khaiṃ Khaiṃ!

Khauṃ! O remover of the fear of planetary afflictions, fever, sorcery, strife, hatred, eradication, and poison; O remover of the fear of thieves, wild beasts dwelling in the wilderness, venomous insects, scorpions, and the poison from the fangs and hair of serpents! Kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣaiṃ kṣaiṃ kṣaiṃ!
O you who destroy deceivers, cheats, thieves, and murderers; O you who pacify various calamities; Bhaṃ Bhaṃ Bhaṃ Bhairṃ Bhairṃ Bhairṃ;
Oṃ Aiṃ Phreṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Chrīṃ Strīṃ Hsauḥ; Salutations, salutations to the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī; Hāṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Hauṃ Āṃ; Salutations to Pratyaṅgirā, [the goddess] of ten million [mantras].
To her who is adorned with staff-like arms, who dwells in the most terrifying cremation ground,

who sits majestically upon the heart-lotus of Mahārudra, [I offer salutation] to Krauṃ Glauṃ Phreṃ Khphreṃ Hsphreṃ Hskhphreṃ Rhrūṃ Rkṣhrūṃ Rkṣhrūṃ Rkṣrmchrūṃ Rjjhrkṣūṃ, the one who carries forth great corpses.

Caṭa caṭa! Pracaṭa pracaṭa! Kaha kaha! Dhama dhama! Hasa hasa! Gāya gāya! Jaya jaya! Jīva jīva! O you who wear a tiger-skin garment, you of terrifying form, you who wear a garland of skulls, *phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ*, *kṣoṃ kṣoṃ kṣoṃ*, *kroṃ kroṃ kroṃ*! O supporter of the earth, O expounder of Brahman, O you who consist of the nectar of Brahman, homage be to you!

Homage to you, O Pratyaṅgirā; homage to you, Siddhilakṣmī; homage to you, Caṇḍakāpālinī; homage to you, the presiding deity of sovereignty. Homage to you, Mahāmāyā, who are formless, manifold-formed, universal-formed, multiformed, and beyond all forms; you who destroy all gods, Daityas, and Dānavas, and who are the Kṛtyā of malevolent magic.
O destroyer of the evils of planets and constellations; O shatterer of yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, vetālas, pretas, ḍākinīs, and kūṣmāṇḍas;
O Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, Mahitrī, Avitrī; O cutter of the fear of fire; O lightning and thunderbolt!

O you who do not allow the waters of the rains to overwhelm; O deliverer from the tossing of the ship upon the ocean's waves; O you who carry one across the perilous flood of suffering in the wilderness of the darkness of night;
O pacifier of the poisons of royal families, of venomous snakes, of fever, and other diseases; O fearless one, remover of fear; O sinless one, destroyer of sin.

O you who are not dejected, who shatter wretchedness; O inconceivable one, who dispel anxiety; O unfailing one, who remove delusion; O non-inert one, who take away dullness; O guileless one, who bestow pride; O unbound one, who sever bonds; O healthy one, who uproot disease; O compassionate one, who shatter the fear of birth and death; O indefinable one, who grant defining characteristics; O unmanifest one, who bring about manifestation.

O bestower of the fruit of immortality, O Truth, O giver of the state of truth, O eternal creator of perpetual bliss, O Awakening, O source of awakening, O beyond the reach of mind and speech, O fulfiller of desires, O unconquered by effort, O accomplisher of all endeavors!

Incomprehensible by the means of valid cognition, yet the one who brings about the establishment of those very means; devoid of attributes and form, yet worshipped through the meditation upon attributes and limbs;
having the color of snow, a conch, or a kunda flower; five-faced, with three eyes on each face;
adorned with a crown of tawny matted locks; and clad in a tiger skin.
Wearing a garland of human skulls, seated upon the heart of Rudra, her two knees bound by a yogic cloth,

possessing ten hands holding a trident, sword, skull, goad, khaṭvāṅga staff, skull-cup, noose, and bell, with hands displaying the gestures of boon-granting and fearlessness, she is of inconceivable and immeasurable strength and prowess.

She who delights in the flesh and blood of Daityas, Dānavas, and Asuras; she who brings about victory in battle; she who grants heaven and liberation to her devotees; she who dwells in cremation grounds; she of most terrible roar; she who utters great, boisterous laughter;
she who is a Yoginī, a Ḍākinī, Cāmuṇḍā, and Bhairavī; she who is ever accompanied [by her attendants]; she whose belly is large and pendulous.
O Sovereign of the fourteen worlds, including the heavens, the earth, and the nether regions;
whose body consists of ninety million mantras; who assumes an exceedingly terrifying form;
O remover of dwelling in the womb, birth, old age, and death; O secret of secrets, supreme and non-supreme, the state of equilibrium between Śiva and Śakti!
The Samaya is the secret supreme reality of the Kula and Akula wheels; by its very nature, it bestows the fruit of Nirvana upon the Supreme Śiva.

It possesses a terrifying row of thirty-two teeth that pulverizes millions of cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍas). It takes the form of a four-gated square with three lines, an eight-spoked wheel, a twelve-petaled lotus, an eight-petaled lotus, a hexagon, a triangle, and a Bindu.

Dwelling in the center of the house, she is to be worshipped through the king of mantras consisting of nine syllables; she bears a peak-form (kūṭamūrti) composed of ever-new syllables; she transcends all speech and all branches of knowledge (vidyā); she possesses the digit of the nasal bindu (nādabindukalā) which is the unfailing form beyond time and the like; and she is the gatherer of the application of thirty-three million weapons and missiles.
She who is to be worshipped by the teachers of all the Āgamas;
she who reveals the Mahākhecarī Mudrā; she whose artistic ornaments are fashioned from the great conch;
she who intoxicates with passion; she who eradicates all suffering; she whose ornament is a garland of skulls; she who is like ten million flashes of lightning and the sun.

O you whose form is difficult to behold, who offer oblations of pieces of human flesh, whose face is adorned with a circle of blazing fire, who are surrounded by ten million jackals, who terrify the three worlds with the clapping of hands and cymbals, and who cause the coils of Śeṣa and the tortoise to rise and fall as your feet strike out in dance—dance! Kulyā, Kuṇapacchatrā, Ulūkapoṣiṇī, Narakaṅkālakaraṅkiṇī,
Raktatuṇḍī, Śvetamukhī, Caṇḍā, Aticaṇḍī, Yamaghaṇṭā, Jvālāmālinī, Bhuvanabhayaharī, Vetālānanā, Skandaghonakasavāsā, Kaumāravratinī, Kulakuṭṭanī, Mahāraudrī, Sarva... [all these goddesses].

She who brings forth all seeds, the Mistress of Time, the Deceiver of Time; the Great Bhairavī, Mother of the World, Bestower of Joy to the World; she whose mouth is the fire of universal dissolution, who sports with Death and Yama; she who fondles the young cock, who has a peacock feather as her crest-ornament; the Great Terrifier, the Great Whirler.

Red-eyed one, who brings supernatural power, increase, peace, well-being, and contentment; sovereign lady of the gods of gods; destroyer of all that is auspicious; swift bringer of fear to all: rhkṣmlvryūṁ śkṣmlvryīṁ hskṣmlvryūṁ rhkṣmlvryūṁ śkṣmlvryīṁ hskṣmlvryūṁ rhkṣmlvryūṁ śkṣmlvryīṁ hskṣmlvryūṁ rhkṣmlvryūṁ śkṣmlvryīṁ hskṣmlvryūṁ oṃ hrīṁ hūṁ hāṁ.

Phreṃ kroṃ namaḥ hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ chrīṃ hsauṃḥ krīṃ kroṃ phreṃ strīṃ śrīṃ phroṃ jūṃ vlauṃ vrīṃ svāhā namaḥ. O beloved of the worship of the nine-syllable, nine-lettered, and sixteen-syllable mantras; O Mahāmāyā, whose form is gentle and foremost, who accomplishes the four aims of life beginning with *haloki*, *kapāla*, *laukiṅka*, and so forth, and who grants joy.
Fulfilling the individual desires of each person: *hrīṃ kṣmlvryūṃ*, obeisance to you, O Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, *phaṭ svāhā*.
Obeisance to you, O Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, *phaṭ svāhā*. Obeisance to you, O Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, *phaṭ svāhā*.
[Thus ends the ten-thousand-syllable garland mantra of Siddhilakṣmī within the Śrī Kālānala Tantra.]
Then, having taken a small fragment, |||

"By my own respective mantras, I satisfy the lineage of gurus beginning with Gaṇa and Vaṭuka, together with their limbs, up to the end of Bhagavatī. With this, one should satisfy the venerable Pādukā; then [one satisfies] the Root Goddess.
One should perform the libation with the nine-syllable mantra according to one's capacity.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ. Welcome, most welcome!
Then first, the water for washing the feet.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, the Mother Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons—this water for the feet is offered to the Blessed Lady; obeisance!
Then, the water for honoring (argha).
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, the Mother Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons—this arghya is offered to the Blessed Lady; obeisance!
Then follows the ritual rinsing of the mouth (ācamana).
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons—this seat made of ācamaṇīya, obeisance to the Blessed Lady.
Then follows the ritual bath.
Having bathed the Goddess of Devas, who is affectionate toward her devotees, with devotion using milk while reciting "Aiṃ," one is thereafter honored in the world of Indra after enjoying the earth.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, together with her retinue, together with her weapons—this milk-bath is offered to the Blessed Lady; obeisance!
The bath with curd.
One who bathes the Goddess, the beloved of Bhairava, with curd according to the prescribed rite,
is glorified in the world of Śiva by means of a silver celestial chariot.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! Salutation to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons; salutation to the Blessed Lady, this is the curd-bath.
Clarified butter, honey, and sugar.
He who bathes the Lord of Gods with ghee mixed with honey and combined with sugar obtains a fruit that is free from all taint.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons, [this is] the bath of ghee and sugar; obeisance to the Blessed Lady.
The bath with pure water.
Having bathed the queen with pure water while being endowed with devotion,
one who is afflicted by all burning fevers is liberated from that great disease.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, and her weapons; to the Blessed Lady, this is the water-bath.
But...
Wine is Śakti and meat is Śiva; their union is supreme. I grant you prosperity, accomplishment, the merit of the vow, and the bathing with bees.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! Salutation to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her attendants and retinue, and her weapons; salutation to the Blessed Lady, [this is] the bathing with bees.
Therein, one should recite the root-mantra (mūlavidyā). Then follows the wiping of the limbs (aṅgaproñchana). Then the sandalwood [ointment].
O Queen of Gods, accept this self-anointing unguent for the purpose of anointment, consisting of sandalwood, saffron, camphor, and musk.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady,
together with her limbs, her attendants and retinue, and her weapons; to the Blessed Lady, [this is] sandalwood unguent, obeisance.
Sindūra.
O Goddess, this supreme vermilion, reddish like the dawn, is endowed with the great hero Vīreśvarī and the ashes of heroes; it is the magnet that draws in the three worlds.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her attendants and retinue, and her weapons; [I offer] vermilion to the Blessed Lady.
Clothing, clothing, a supreme protection that bestows happiness and good fortune; O Mother of the World, accept this cotton garment; salutations to you!
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her attendants, her retinue, and her weapons—to the Blessed Lady, obeisance; [I offer] clothing.
The sacred thread.
O Goddess of gods, accept this sacred thread (yajñopavīta), provided with the Brahma-knot and consisting of nine strands,
which was fashioned by Brahmā in ancient times.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the Blessed Lady for the sacred thread.
View.
Please accept this vision-granting [mirror], which reveals the fourteen worlds— Heaven, Earth, and the Netherworld— for the sake of attaining the fruit of the divine eye.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the Blessed Lady together with her limbs; salutation to Dṛṣṭikā.
The Ear-flag.
The one with five banners.
O Goddess, for the sake of attaining the fruit of the five accomplishments, one should accept this excellent banner with its pair of ear-like ends and its five-colored pennants.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, obeisance to the Goddess, together with her limbs, [offering] the ear-banner and the flag.
Durvā grass, unhusked grain, and flowers.
O Mother, O Ambika of the universe, accept these durva grass, unhusked rice, and fragrant substances, which bestow fortune, splendor, and victory,
and grant success and prosperity.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady with her limbs and retinue; [I offer] this dūrvā grass, unhusked rice, and flower.
A flower for a garland.
O Goddess of the gods, please accept these various flowers, fragrant garlands, and diverse ornaments offered by me with devotion.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her attendants and retinue, and her weapons; [I offer] this flower garland.
Then, having worshipped ten times with the Gāyatrī mantra for the Root Deity in the Ugrakrama rite.
Khphreṃ! We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon her who is nine times greater; may that Lakṣmī inspire us.
One should worship with three handfuls [of flowers] while reciting the root mantra.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
Then one should place the bali offering before the Goddess, and separate offerings for each member of her retinue.
Then, as an offering (bali), flattened beans, coarse meat, liquor, and so forth should be given.
Then, one should request permission from the primary deity for the purpose of performing the worship of the retinue.
Oṃ! O Goddess consisting of pure consciousness, O Supreme Nectar, O Beloved, move forth! Grant me permission, O Surabhi, for the worship of my retinue.
Having thus made this supplication, [performs] the worship of the retinue.
The worship beginning with the causal [deity].
Meditative absorption.
Homage to you, Hetuka, who are yellow in color, four-armed, wielding a sword and a trident, and holding a skull and a severed head in your hands.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, salutation to Hetuka Kṣetrapāla.
Meditative absorption.
Red in color, with six arms, holding a sword and a shield,
a khaṭvāṅga and a ḍamaru in his hands, and bearing a mudrā and a skull-cup.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ! Salutation to Tripurāntaka Kṣetrapāla.
Meditative absorption.
He is black in color, four-armed, holding a hand-drum (ḍamaru) and a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga),
with a skull and a trident in his hands, and adorned with a garland of severed heads.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, salutation to Agnivetāla Kṣetrapāla.
Meditative absorption.
The god is smoke-colored, possesses eight arms, and holds a hand-drum and a skull-topped staff;
he bears a noose and a goad, and carries a trident and a bell.
Homage to you, Kṣetrapāla, who holds a skull-cup and a garland of human heads, who wears ornaments of bones and a living serpent.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, salutation to Agnijihvā Kṣetrapāla.
Meditative absorption.
Obeisance to you, O deity Kṣetrapāla, white in color, four-armed, bearing a skull and a severed head, and holding a battle-axe and a noose.
Hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Kaṅkāla Kṣetrapāla.
Hūṃ, homage to Kalālaka Kṣetrapāla.
Meditative absorption.
O Lord Kṣetrapāla, smoke-colored, four-armed, bearing a skull and a sword, and clad in an elephant hide— homage be to you!
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, salutation to Kapāla Kṣetrapāla.
Meditative absorption.
I bow to Kṣetrapāla, who is black in color, four-armed, holding a skull and a sword, and with a skull-bowl and a staff in his hands.
O Great Goddess, [worship] Mahādeva, who has eight fields, whose face is terrifying with fangs,
who is seated upon a corpse, and who is adorned with ornaments of skulls.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ! Salutation to Ekapāda Kṣetrapāla.
Meditative absorption.
One should worship Dhātaka, who is the color of water and holds a trident, a hand-drum, a skull-cup, and the king of serpents in his hands.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, salutation to Hāṭaka Kṣetrapāla.
Meditative concentration.
I worship the Immovable One (Acala), who resembles a cloud, with my hands as lotuses,
and [worship] Dundubhi, who holds a trident and a noose, a vessel, and is the foremost among the hosts of gods.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, obeisance to the immovable Kṣetrapāla.
This is the bali for them. Thus [ends] the section on Hetukā and others.
Then follows the worship of the six dūtīs beginning with Dhāmā.
Meditative absorption.
All [the goddesses] beginning with Dhāmā have one face and two arms, possess dark complexions,
hold small knives and swords, and are to be meditated upon as having three eyes.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Ḍhāṃ, the sandals of the Mother Dhāmā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of the Mother Dhāmavatī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Dhāṃ, the sandals of Mother Dhāmnī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Vāṃ, [I worship] the sandals of Ambā Vedhānamaṇḍalā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Rāṃ, the sandals of Mother Raviprabhā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Viṃ, obeisance to the sandals of the Mother Virājantī.
This is their offering.
Then [the mantras] beginning with Kākatuṇḍa.
Meditative absorption.
I worship the supreme goddess Kākāsyā, whose limbs are black in color, who is seated upon a corpse, and who holds a hand-drum, a mirror, a skull-bowl, and the gesture of granting boons.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Mahākamalacaṇḍinī of the fierce face, Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Kāṃ!
[I worship] the venerable sandals of Śrī Kākamukhī.
Meditative absorption.
Śrī Caṇḍavaktrā is indeed blue in color, seated upon a corpse, possessing four arms, and exceedingly fierce;
she holds a skull-bowl, a mirror, a peerless boon-granting gesture, and a beautiful drum.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Cīṃ, the venerable sandals of Śrīcaṇḍamukhī.
Meditative absorption.
I worship her who makes the sound "ṭāṃ," whose limbs are red in color, who stands upon a corpse, and who displays the mudrā;
she holds a hand-drum, a severed head, and a choice fruit in her lotus-like hands.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Ṭūṃ, the sandals of Śrīṭāṅkarī.
Meditative absorption.
Mounted upon a *preta*, worshipped by the king of the gods, she is captivating and endowed with an ashen hue;
always holding a boon-granting hand, a trident, a *ḍamaru* drum, and a mirror, she is both stainless and purifying.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Tṛṁ, the sandal of the venerable Tāpinī.
Meditative concentration.
I worship the Mistress of the Pretas, whose hands hold a skull-bowl, a hand-drum, a bell, and the gesture of granting boons, while she joins her [other] hands, which resemble fire, with lotus petals.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Ptṛ, the sandals of the venerable Pāvakī.
Meditative absorption.
Yamaghaṇṭhā is shaped like a preta, while Tamālavana and Merakā are likewise.
Holding an excellent khaṭvāṅga, a ḍamaru drum, and likewise a mirror.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Yaiḥ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Yamaghaṇṭhā.
Meditative absorption.
I bow to Śivādūtī, who resides in the realm of the hungry ghosts (pretas), whose body is red in color, and who holds a hand-drum,
a boon-granting gesture, a severed head, and a skull-bowl in her hands.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Śauṃ, [I worship] the sandals of Śivādūtī.
Meditative concentration.

I always salute Śivā, who holds a hand-drum, a mace, a sword, and a beautiful mirror in her hands; she whose body is yellow, whose eyes are like lotus petals, who brings about destruction, and who sits upon an excellent seat of a corpse.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Kṣaṃḥ, the sandals of the Mother Śrīkṣayaṃkarī.
Meditative absorption.
She is Mahāghorākṣī, who always causes delusion to all enemies; she is tawny-hued, skilled in bringing supreme delight to Hara who is afflicted by love,
and holds in her lotus-like hands a boon-granting gesture, a conch, a skull-bowl, and a hand-drum (ḍamaru).
Victorious is the one who, having attained the state of a preta, possesses knowledge that is well-guarded within his family.
