KHPHREṂ ĀṂ KROṂ PHREṂ MAHĀSIDDHISAMAYE KHPHREṂ BHAIRAVĪ GHORĀKṢĪ VARAPRADE SVĀHĀ. Starting from the east and ending at the center.
Then [the worship of] Karaṅkiṇī and the others.
Meditative absorption.
She is dark-complexioned, most terrifying, and fierce, adorned with a garland of bones;
she has one face, three eyes, wears a necklace of severed heads, and possesses four arms.
She bears a shaven head and a lotus, is radiant, and holds a noose and a goad;
alternatively, she holds a sword and a dagger—these six constitute the visualization that has been set forth.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable mother Karaṅkiṇī, [I worship] the Śrī-pādukā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the sandals of Ambā Krodhinī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable sandals of the Mother Saṃkarṣaṇī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Ambā Lelihānā.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the Mother Khecarī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I worship] the venerable Bhairavī Ambā, the Śrīpādukā.
This is their offering.
Śaṅkhinī is the messenger of Śiva.
Meditative concentration.
Śaṅkhinī and Śivādūtī are situated on the left and the right.
Śivādūtī is the supreme vidyā; now learn of Śaṅkhinī.
Śaṃśinī was previously [established] through Māyā, beginning with the Praṇava and ending with "Namaḥ."
And here, two hands are bound together, with a corpse-ear hanging down from them.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the Mother Śaṅkhinī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the Mother Śivādūtī.
Bali.
Then follows the worship of the six dūtīs, beginning with the heart and so forth.
Meditative absorption.
The Goddess resembles black collyrium and is like a dark blue cloud;
she is as dark as the petal of an indīvara lotus and possesses the luster of a blue water-lily petal.

Resembling the flax flower in hue, with a luster like that of lapis lazuli, she has a face with beautiful, tender features; her countenance is composed in meditation, and she is adorned with earrings.
She wears a mass of matted locks, is divine, and is adorned with a crown of lordly serpents;
she is endowed with the eight mudrās and embellished with various jewels.
In her left hands she holds a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), a serpent, and a noose;
and [in her right hands] she holds a trident, the gesture of granting boons (varada), a rosary, and a small knife.
A hand-drum and a large drum shine upon her right side;
she possesses uplifted breasts adorned with a long, hanging necklace of serpents.
The goddess, seated upon a corpse vehicle, is exceedingly beautiful from her hips downward, situated amidst the waves of her three folds, and draped in garments of black cloth.
Having meditated thus, O lady of excellent limbs, [one should contemplate her] situated in the center of the city of Śṛṅgāṭapura.
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption.
Aiṃ hskhphreṃ! O Kālikāli! Hrāṃ! O consumer of flesh and blood! Hūṃ! O goddess with red and black faces!
Hrauṃ! Let the enemies see me! [I offer] the venerable sandals of the Heart Messenger, the goddess Heart-Kālikā.
Meditative absorption.
Deep red and intensely radiant, with hair standing erect, she was terrifying;
a garland of bones was bound around her neck, and two bones hung down from her ears.
The three-eyed one, the destroyer of those [demons], with creeper-like eyebrows and various distorted forms.
Terror-inspiring to behold and exceedingly fierce, she was chewing off the finest heads.
Four-armed and of great splendor, with a radiance like the fire of cosmic destruction,
she holds a skull and a severed head in her left hands, and a trident and a flaying knife in her right hands.
Adorned with a garland of skulls and draped in a human skin.
Standing upon a skeleton, she is exceedingly fierce, as if swallowing all that is moving and unmoving.
Having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess standing in the midst of the corpse, [one should proceed].

Aiṃ aiṃ! Homage to the Blessed One, the Wicked Caṇḍālī, who devours the blood and flesh of enemies, who bears a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff! Strike! Burn! Vomit! Cook! Hūṃ! Kill so-and-so! Devour!
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! At the location of the head is the Wicked Caṇḍālī.
Meditative absorption.
He has five faces and ten arms, radiant with fifteen eyes;
he wears a mass of matted hair, is divine, and is adorned with earrings.
In the right [hands], he holds a trident, the gesture of granting boons, a noose, a sword, and a shield;
and [in the left], the gesture of fearlessness, a mirror, a serpent, a citron, and a large snake.
In his left [hand], he holds divine weapons; he is endowed with various ornaments, enriched by the splendor of diverse jewels, and adorned with many kinds of gems.
Resembling the color of cow’s milk, similar to a mass of snow or the moon,
with the king of serpents as his sacred thread and hanging garlands of jewels.
Having thus meditated upon Śiva, the supreme cause, who is complete in all his limbs and endowed with all the auspicious marks, O lady of excellent hips.
Having installed the Lord of Devas according to the Śikhāśvacchandas, one should worship him upon that [pedestal].

Aiṃ Aghore Hrauṃ Tha-ghore Hsphreṃ Ghora-ghorantare Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Sarva Sarve Hsphreṃ Namaḥ te Rudra-rūpe Hsauṃ Pādukāṃ. [I offer my sandals] at the place of the crest-lock (śikhā) to the self-willed (svacchanda) Aghora.
Meditative absorption.
She has one face and three eyes, appearing slightly terrifying to behold;
she wears a divine mass of matted hair and is adorned with a multitude of earrings.
Endowed with eight arms and adorned with various ornaments,
O beloved, she holds a trident, a hand-drum, a serpent, and a spear in her right hands.
A skull-bowl, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a noose, and a flaying knife are held in her left hands;
she resembles a cochineal insect and possesses full, elevated breasts.
The goddess, seated upon the throne of Kiṣkindhā, is adorned with beautiful hips, clothed in blue garments, and stands amidst the waves of the Taptī river.
Having thus meditated upon the divine Mahādevī, the supreme Śivā, who wears a garland of severed heads, who threatens [all], and who dwells in the center of the city of Śṛṅgāṭapura;

Aiṁ Hrīṁ, you who have been uplifted; Hrīṁ, you who have expanded over the entire earth; Hrīṁ, you who have been drawn in the form of a line; Hrīṁ, you who have been inscribed as the circle of all things—Pādukāṃ! Thus ends the section on the Śrī-Bhālikā-kavaca.
Meditative absorption.
Resembling white, blue, and black collyrium, she is greatly radiant with supreme luster;
she has one face and three eyes, and her countenance is slightly smiling.
Abounding in the splendor of divine earrings, adorned with a crown of matted locks, four-armed, possessed of great majesty, and decorated with various ornaments and gems.
O Dear One, [visualize] the Goddess holding a noose and a goad, wearing a conch-shell and a sacred thread,
adorned with necklaces and anklets, and possessing full, elevated breasts.
The Goddess, seated upon a lotus throne, rests on a lotus seat; she is richly adorned with the beauty of waves of light rays and embellished with garlands of jewels.
The goddess, clad in white garments, resides in the center of the city of Śṛṅgāṭapura.
Aiṃ Guhyakubjike hūṃ phaṭ hrīṃ Rakte Cāmuṇḍeśvarī aiṃ he svāhā.
O you whose eyes are like those of the blood-drinking Cāmuṇḍā!
Meditative concentration.
She has five faces, is exceedingly fierce, and possesses fifteen eyes;
her eyes are slightly reddish, and she is adorned with ears and a prominent nose.
The eastern face of the Goddess is white in luster, the northern face is red in luster,
the western face is yellow in luster, and the southern face is black in luster.
One should behold [the deity] who is formidable and fierce, tawny-eyed and of terrifying form,
with a luster like a conch or the moon, upward-facing, and the bestower of liberation.
It is renowned as Gaganāvatī, the cause of the creation and dissolution [of the world]. The eastern face is indeed the most excellent, while the northern face is the left one.
Having spoken thus, the western face is Raudrī, situated on the right;
adorned with the thirty-eight kalās, she shines resplendent, residing within the faces.
Siddhā, Śuddhā, Prabhā, Dīptā, and the fifth is remembered as Kāmadā;
O Goddess of gods, these five digits (kalās) in the upward-facing [lotus] bestow emanation.
The goddess is proclaimed to have eight digits (kalās): Siddhidā, Karṣaṇī, Raudrā, Saumyā, Bhīmā, Susiddhidā, Bhogadā, and Yogadā.
O lady of excellent limbs, she who dwells there shines in the mouth of Jyeṣṭhā;
she is Sūkṣmā, Asūkṣmavatī, Raktā, Atiraktā, and Padmajā.
Suprabhā, Vimalavarṇā, Suśilā, Tapanā,
as well as Bhrāmaṇī, Śoṣaṇī, and Kriyā as the thirteenth.
In the left face is the goddess Kalā, blazing with great splendor;
she is Bhuvanā, Veginī, Līlā, and Kṛṣṇā as the fourth.
O Goddess Kalā, these must be diligently understood within the mouth of Vativatī:
Krūrā, Krodhanī, Krodhā, Tamā, Mūrcchā, and Kṣapāparā.
O beautiful lady, Kālī— terrible as death, fierce, and possessing eight faces with eight kalās each,
endowed with thirty-eight kalās— is the bestower of perfect accomplishment when meditated upon.
Endowed with ten arms and adorned with various ornaments,
she holds a trident, a mace, a noose, a goad, and an excellent sword.
O lady of excellent hips, in her right hands she holds a weapon with the brilliance of the fire of cosmic destruction, a sword, a shield, and two spears;
she is the bearer of a severed head and a mace.
[He holds] divine weapons of the left-hand path, blazing with a luster like molten gold,
and a divine garland of *ka* letters, well-knotted, hanging down from his feet.
Resembling the rays of moonlight, auspicious, and like the color of a palm fruit.
She is adorned with a garland of human skulls and beautified by long, pendulous breasts.
Indeed, Citrā, Kṛtamālā, Nāgarājopavītinī,
Vṛkodarī, Nālavarṇā, and Aṭaśīpuṣpasaṃnibhā— [these are the rivers].
Clad in black garments, seated upon the back of a lion,
adorned with a garland fashioned from various jewels, and resplendent with a girdle bound at her waist.
A rosary fashioned with yantras and mantras shone upon her neck,
and she wore two stainless anklets resembling liquid gold.
Having thus meditated upon her, O lady of excellent hips, as complete in all her limbs and adorned with all ornaments, situated in the center of the city of Śṛṅgāṭapura;
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.

Aiṃ hskhphreṃ śkhphrīṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ! Strike, burn, and destroy all those who have performed, are performing, or will perform any misfortune through the application of mantras, yantras, powders, or other such means—
O Hana Daha Daṃṣṭrākarālī, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ, Ṅlauṃ Ṅlūṃ Ślīṃ, Guhyakubjikā, [grant] the sandals (pādukā)!
Astradūtī and Guhyakubjikā, [offer] the sandal (pādukā). To these, this is the bali offering.
Hanu Bhairava.
Meditative concentration.
Oṃ! Five-faced and most formidable, with fifteen eyes, possessing the brilliance of ten million suns, monkey-faced and of great splendor.
He is endowed with ten hands, possesses rows of sharp claws,
has a face adorned with fangs and a snout, and his eyes are curved with a frown.
With his beard blazing, his mustache blazing, and the hair on his body blazing,
he bore a flame at the opening of his mouth capable of burning the three worlds.
A sword, a trident, a skull-topped staff, a noose, a goad, and a mountain;
likewise a tree and a bear, as well as a shaven head, a mallet, and a fist.
Bringing down this fierce, blazing, and supreme weapon,
let them stand upon their seats, adorned with various jewels.
Clad in red garments, adorned with red garlands and red unguents,
the Brahmin was seen blazing with a radiance equal to ten million suns.
His very right face is the Nārasiṃha, possessed of great strength,
with a body of exceedingly fierce splendor, terrifying and the leader of fear.
In the west is the face of Garuḍa, with a vajra beak and great power;
it pacifies all spirits and cuts through the mass of poison.
His northern face was that of a boar,
a terrifying boar’s face resembling black collyrium, fierce, blazing, and possessed of great power.
The *draṃṣṭrā* is deformed by the sound of its fangs, the destroyer of all weapons;
the *tāla* grants success (*siddhi*) and is the blazing eradicator of disease.
The mind that pacifies seizure and epilepsy, the subduer of planetary spirits, the sky-farer, Rūpikā, Ārāmā, and the Mothers— these are the subduers.
They made his face upward, terrible, fearsome, and of a fierce form; and with a harsh cry, the Dānavas burst open his heart.
His mantra is of great brilliance, and he is the Lord of the Kings of Kings;
it is a mantra that accomplishes all siddhis and bestows the fruit of all desires.
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Oṃ rhrphreṃ hūṃ bhañja rhrkṣmrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
By Nāṭeśvarī.
Meditative absorption.
He has one face and three eyes, adorned with serpent earrings;
he wears a mass of matted hair with the moon as his crest, is white in color, and possesses great splendor.
One should meditate upon the Supreme Lord performing the *tāṇḍava* dance, endowed with sixteen arms,
with uplifted arms in a dancing posture, holding a hand-drum (*ḍamaru*) and a trident (*triśūla*).
He holds a triple staff, a vajra with a jewel, a flaying knife, and a rosary; likewise, his left side is in a dancing posture, holding a khaṭvāṅga and a lotus.
He holds a serpent, a bow, a bell, a skull-cup, and a water-pot;
he resembles a thousand suns and has the luster of black collyrium crushed by time.
Seated firmly upon the bull-throne, joined with dance and song,
Bhairava appears in the form of a dancer, adorned with every ornament.
Having thus meditated upon Mahādeva, who bestows perfect accomplishment through the performance of the dance.
For the benefit of human beings, it is the destroyer of all suffering.
Thus concludes the section on meditative concentration.
Oṃ hūṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the glorious Nṛtyeśvara Mahābhairava, together with the Śakti Hrīṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ Śrī Nṛtyalakṣmī, [I offer] the sandals.
The fifth is Vārāhī.
Meditative absorption.
Seated upon a great lion-throne, her body resplendent with a blue hue, the great heroine has eight arms; in two of her staff-like arms she holds a sword and a shield.
The goddess holds a discus, a conch, and a trident in her hands; she wields a mallet and bears [the skull-topped staff];
she bestows boons and fearlessness, and is adorned with a garland of skulls.
Her limbs are adorned with pearl necklaces; she has three eyes and the peacock as her vehicle;
she stands in the midst of a blazing funeral pyre; she is the fifth [letter] who has cast out the serpent.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Glūṃ Āṃ Īṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One Vārtālī, Vārāhī, Vārāhimukhī! O Andhye, salutation to you, O Andhinī! O Ruṃdhya, salutation to you, O Rudhinī! O Jambhe, salutation to you, O Jambhinī! O Stambhe, salutation to you, O Stambhinī! [Bind] all those who are wicked and extremely wicked—[bind] the speech, mind, sight, hearing, mouth, and movement of all of them.
O tongue, become paralyzed quickly; bring [him] under control! Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Ṭha Ṭha Ṭha Oṁ Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā. Bali.
West.
Meditative absorption.
The five-faced one is eternally blue, seated in the upright paryaṅka posture,
appearing about sixteen years of age, and adorned with jewels, serpents, and bones.
Bhairava is seated upon a lotus situated at the navel of the fire; he has his big toe tucked [within], holds a *kaṭṭāraka* knife, wears a tiger-skin garment, and possesses a smiling countenance.
He bears in his right hands a trident, a discus-banner, and the gesture of generosity,
while his other hands hold a pārijāta flower, a rosary for recitation, a book, and the gesture of fearlessness.
With his body covered by a hide and possessing two arms,
he always remains fresh, dwelling eternally in the god-frequented cremation ground.
I shall now describe, in due order, the sequence of the weapons and the mantras as they arise from this context;
through the trident, there is the attainment of all principles, and through the Krama, it becomes imperishable.
Through the *dhvaja* one attains the state of going to all worlds; from giving, omniscience shall arise.
Through the *pārijāta* there is the acquisition of fortune, while through the *jāpyaka* there is the accomplishment of the mantra.
Until omniscience is attained, one who has become free from fear through the absence of fear may experience the concealment of obstacles within the skin of Brahma.
The Lord is praised as being liberated yet playful, possessing a gross form of Lakṣmī,
the Lord of Gods who is intent upon remaining tasks and is perfectly endowed with whatever is desired.
In the case of subjugation, the color should be yellow; for the purpose of bringing under control, it should resemble saffron;
for expulsion, it should have a smoky hue; and for creating enmity, it should have the luster of rock salt.
The *mohana* stone is to be known by its leaf-like appearance; it is considered like a gem for subduing. Resembling sapphire (*indranīla*), it is the sovereign of all rites.
Cool and peaceful, he is described as resembling pure crystal in the *Muktikāpāṭha*;
he is said to be reddish-white in the *Śrī* [Tantra], while in the *Kṣobhaka*, he is the color of a lotus.

One should contemplate the Supreme Knower (Paramaśāna) as a youth when performing rites for the accomplishment of a group; however, in rites for pacification, he should be seated upon the shoulders of a bull, and in rites for nourishment, mounted upon a lotus.
For expulsion (uccāṭana), [the deity] is mounted upon a camel; for enchantment (mohana), he has an island as his vehicle;
for victory (jaya), O Lord, he is mounted upon a ram; and for muteness (mūka), he is on a hide.
By paralyzing the army, one should subdue the lord of the city; against a sharp foe, one should employ a sharper means, while for the sake of wealth, one should act against a deer-like opponent.
One shall conquer a stable kingdom, knowledge, and one seated upon the lion-throne.
Aiṃ! She has the luster of a blue lotus, the form of a hunchback, and a large belly;
she has six faces, twelve arms, and is adorned with serpents, bones, and jewels.
Wearing a garland of severed heads, fierce, with terrifying fangs and a loud roar, the Goddess possesses eighteen arms and hair that stands upright in matted locks.
Clad in a tiger skin with a lion skin as her upper garment,
her limbs adorned with divine ornaments, she laughs with a loud, boisterous laugh from her mouth.
Its water is yellow, its northern face resembles the color of a dark cloud,
and its southern face, which is presented facing forward, is black in color.
The upper face, born of Īśa, should be red; its seat is crystal.
Resembling a thousand suns, that upper face possesses supreme radiance.
In the caulakūpa, on the left, in the right ear and the hearing-organ,
at the tip of the nose, and on the forehead and the crown, as well as on the palms, it is sequential.
I declare that the stone-painting,
the plaster, and the face have reached the water, the gentle one, the left side, the east, and the right ear.
The face turned away is in the region of the fool; that which is called "Supreme" (Parā) is on its head.
Śambhu has stated that all the faces are formidable with fangs.
I shall proclaim the great missiles of this Kubjikā;
understand them according to their application on the right and likewise on the left.
One should place the trident, wheel, and vajra, as well as the hook together with the hand and the chisel,
in the right [hands], and the blue lotus with its star in the left.
Furthermore, the other [hands] are said to hold a shaven head, a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), a bell, a book, and a bow; while on the left side are a skull-cup, a lion-throne, and a corpse-eater.
From the *śūla* (spear), the attainment of reality (*tattva*) occurs; from the *cakra* (wheel), the destruction of the self (*ātmāya*) occurs.
From the *vajra* (thunderbolt), there is the destruction of all diseases; from the *aṅkuśa* (hook), torment is considered [to arise].

The destruction of enemies occurs through the arrow; the removal of obstacles through the hand-drum (kartari); the attainment of prosperity through the lotus; and the accomplishment of the eight siddhis through the skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga).
As long as the state of being a bearer of the meaning of mantras arises from the bell,
and as long as the state of understanding the meaning of the scriptures and mastery over the purposeless occurs through the book.
O Mahāmati, from the skull comes the great accomplishment of weapons;
Brahmā is said to be at her soles, and Viṣṇu at her hips.
Rudra dwells in the heart; Īśvara is in the circle of the throat;
Śiva is situated above him, on the forehead of Śaṅkara.
One should imagine the fierce sun and fire as the eyes, with the stars as the circle of constellations, and the sevenfold heaven above the lotus, all situated over the corpse.
One should contemplate the element of earth in the *svādhiṣṭhāna* and water at the navel;
one should conceive of fire in the center of the heart and air in the throat.
Ākāśa is in the forehead; he is established within all of them.
Thousands of millions of families have ascended to the teaching of the family.
An investigation into its mass is difficult even for the gods;
its extent is proclaimed to be infinite, both in length and in breadth.
The *karkoṭa* is proclaimed as the *mekhalā* (girdle) and the *kaṭibandha* (waist-band);
the *takṣaka* is the *upavīta* (sacred thread), while *vāsuki* is the *hāra* (necklace).
Kūlika is said to be located in the two ears, adorned with tortoise-shaped earrings;
Padma and Mahāpadma are likewise situated between the eyebrows.
Upon all his staff-like arms, he was adorned with a thousand hoods,
blazing with a mass of flames like thousands of millions of lightning bolts.
One should contemplate the illustrious Kubjikā in this manner, as Lakṣmī, Āpūrṇā, and Antā.
Thus ends the flower of meditative concentration; homage! [With] three *añjali* gestures.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To the sovereign hero Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, Yhkṣmlvryīṃ!
The sandals of the venerable Bhaṭṭārikā of the original seat of the West (Śrīpaścimamūlasthāna). [Offering of] bali.
Uttala: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, salutation to the sandals. Bali.
Kāli!
Meditative absorption.
Mahākālī is exceedingly secret, ten-faced, and three-eyed;
she is black in color, possessed of great splendor, eight-armed, and slender-waisted.
The goddess, whose face has various colors, should be meditated upon as the solar nature;
she is clothed in a tiger skin and adorned with ornaments of human bone.
In his right hands, he holds a trident, a goad, and a vajra, as well as a club;
in his left hands, he holds a khaṭvāṅga staff, a noose, a vessel, and likewise the head of a corpse.
They traverse the king of sequences, which resembles a thousand suns;
it proceeds toward the single accomplishment for the sake of the essence of the center of this [world].
In the midst of the family of mental formations, birth and form are entirely absent;
Nirvana is the supreme knowledge, transcending all states of being and beyond the reach of the mind.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Oṃ oṃ Siddhikarālī hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā pādukāṃ. Bali.
By Tripurā.
Meditative absorption.
One should worship the Supreme Goddess, who possesses the luster of the orb of the rising sun, has four arms and three eyes,
and holds a noose, a goad, an arrow, and a bow.

Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ Kvlhrīṃ Hykdlhrīṃ Yklhrīṃ! In the Wheel of Brahman (brahmacakra), at the seat of the Great Garden (mahodyānapīṭha), which is the essence of the venerable Carya-Āsana, presiding over the fourteen states beginning with the Fourth (turya), and whose nature is the power of the Supreme Brahman— consisting of the forms of waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and that beyond the Fourth (turyātīta), as well as will, knowledge, action, peace, and that beyond peace.
The goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the sandals, and the sacrificial offering.
Then one should worship the illustrious Mahābhairava, the Lord of Siddhas.
Meditative absorption.
On one [face] is the three-eyed [Lord], with the crescent moon as his crest-ornament;
O Great Goddess, he has four hands, while she has two hands joined in *añjali*.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, I worship the sandals of Ānandabhairava Siddheśvara.
Then, [the offering is made] to the primary deity.
RJJHĪṂ! O Great Fierce One, O Splendor, O Attractor, O Kālī, O Churner of Passion! [The Color].
One should worship the three tufts of hair.
PHREṂ ĀṂ KROṂ PHRIṂ MAHĀSIDDHISAMAYA KHPHREṂ BHAIRAVI GHORALAKṢMĪ VARAPRADE SVĀHĀ || VARṆA || TENA TRI ||
Āṃ phriṃ phrāṃ, O Mahāsṛṣṭicaṇḍalakṣmīsiddheśvarī, pheṃ phaṭ! [The syllables.]
Hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ svāhā.
KHPHREṂ NAMO BHAGAVATĪ SIDDHILAKṢMĪŚVARĪ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ || ||
Then, having worshipped Gāyatrī tenfold, one should proceed.
Khphreṃ! We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon Kālikā; may Saṃkarṣaṇī inspire us.
Then, with twenty-nine syllables, one should worship the Root Sovereign in five ways.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ. May these most secret and yet most manifest Yoginīs, the venerable Bhairava, the Kṣetrapālas, the Gaṇas, the Vaṭukas, and the rest who dwell in the cremation grounds, together with their seals (mudrās), accomplishments (siddhis), weapons, vehicles, and retinues— worshipped with all ritual offerings in the glorious Wheel of Siddhis that fulfills every desire— be pleased.
HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. One should perform worship everywhere with these three syllables.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the worship of the retinue.
Now follows the worship of the wheel (cakrapūjā).
Meditation on Indra and the others in the ten directions.
Śakra has a four-armed body, and likewise Sacī has two arms;
the lotus and the goad should be depicted in the two right hands of Śakra.
The left hand is placed behind Śacī, while the second [hand] is joined with a vajra;
in the left hand of Śacī, a beautiful cluster of *santāna* blossoms should be fashioned.
One should visualize the right [hand] of the Lord of Gods resting upon his back.
Aiṃ lmlvryūṃ luṃ, to Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand and is the sovereign of the gods, [I offer] the sandals.
Meditative absorption.

Oṃ. One should visualize the Fire-god in the southeast, possessing the brilliance of a full-blown *kiṃśuka* flower, holding a white spear, radiant, and with great arms raised with a sacrificial ladle.
Seated upon a goat in blissful ease, united with Svāhā,
his face is for all the gods, and he wears a crown of divine jewels.
Aiṃ Rmlvryūṃ Ruṃ; to Agni, who holds a spear in his hand and is the lord of splendor, [I offer] the sandals.
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon Yama, who is dark blue, possessing a deep blue luster, whose body is like that of a buffalo,
who wields the staff of Time (Kāladaṇḍa), and whose eyes are long and reddish-brown.
One should meditate on the Lord of the Southern Quarter, who always shines by his own power while seated upon the left lap [of his consort], and who holds a noose in his left hand.
Aiṁ Mmlvryūṁ Mūṁ! To Yama, who holds a staff in his hand, the lord of the pretas, [I offer] the sandals.
Meditative concentration.
Oṃ! [I visualize] the Rākṣasa, dark as the petal of a blue lotus, with blood-red eyes, bearing an extremely sharp sword, and possessing a formidable, wide face.
One should meditate upon the Lord of the Rākṣasas in the southwest, his left side adorned by a woman, his body composed of a hundred corpses, richly arrayed in various ornaments.
Aiṁ kṣmlvryūṁ kṣuṁ: [I offer] this sandal to the Lord of the Rākṣasas, the Sovereign of the South-West, who holds a sword in his hand.
Meditative absorption.
Varuṇa, who resembles an autumn cloud or the moon, is seated upon a water-lily;
he holds a shimmering noose, is peaceful, and is well-honored by hosts of aquatic creatures.
One should meditate upon the Lord of the Western Quarter, adorned with cheeks rubbed by jeweled earrings, and endowed with supreme devotion.
Aiṁ Vmlvryūṁ Vūṁ, the sandals to Varuṇa, who holds a noose in his hand and is the lord of the waters.
Meditative absorption.
[He visualizes] Prāṇa, the lord of the northwest direction, with the luster of a fresh blade of durvā grass,
mounted upon Varasamvara, and adorned with necklaces of jewels.
I worship the Lord of Procreation, who holds a banner and a goad in his left and right arms,
and whose lap is occupied by his own body-born consort.
Aiṁ Ymlvryūṁ Yuṁ: Obeisance to the sandals of Vāyu, who holds a banner in his hand and is the lord of the wind.
Meditative concentration.
Oṃ! [I invoke] Kubera, who resembles a mass of gold, whose single eye is tawny, and who is surrounded on all sides by yakṣas and treasures.
One should worship the Lord of the Northern Quarter, who is mounted upon a man-vehicle, endowed with a beard and a spear, and whose staff-like arms are brandishing a mace.
Aiṁ Smlvryūṁ, to Sukubera, who holds a mace in his hand and is the lord of wealth, [I offer] the sandals.
Meditative absorption.
In the northeast, one should meditate upon Īśvara, possessing the brilliant luster of a silver mountain,
three-eyed, four-armed, having the bull as his emblem, and adorned with the crescent moon.
Holding a trident, the gesture of fearlessness, and a bowl with the *jñānamudrā*,
his left side is honored by Śivā and he is adorned with sacred ashes.
Aiṁ Hmlvryūṁ Hūṁ! To Īśāna, who holds a trident in his hand and is the lord of spirits, [I offer] the sandals.
Meditative absorption.
Oṃ, one should meditate on the infinite Tortoise-throne, resembling the autumnal moon,
enriched by the splendor of jeweled earrings, and adorned with four great arms.
Adorned with the conch, the white lotus, and the mace of Hara,
covered by seven hoods, he dwells in the depths of the netherworld.
Aiṃ aṃ aṃ aṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Ananta, the lord of serpents, who holds a discus in his hand.
Meditative concentration.
Brahmā is surrounded by goddesses, situated in the upper region of the mandala;
he is yellow in color, possessing four arms and four faces, and is resplendent.

One should meditate upon [the deity] seated on a swan-throne within the treasury, characterized by the water-pot (kamaṇḍalu), the gestures of boon-granting (varā) and fearlessness (abhaya), and the gesture of knowledge (jñānamudrā).
Aiṃ Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ, sandals to Brahmā, who holds a lotus in his hand and is the sovereign of heaven.
This is the bali offering for them.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the worship of the guardians of the directions.
Then follows the worship of the doors.
Meditative concentration.
One should meditate upon the Lord Kramagaṇeśa as white and four-armed,
holding a skull, a trident, an axe, and a rosary of beads.
One should meditate upon that most beautiful Great Goddess named Vallabhā, who embraces a betel-roll and is joined with her Śakti.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of Kramagaṇapatinātha.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I offer] the sandals of Ambā, the beloved of Kramagaṇapati-nātha. Bali.
The seat of the syllable Oṃ.
Meditative absorption.
Three-eyed and resembling a white water-lily, the supreme Lord holds a noose and a staff;
likewise, he holds a spear and a sword, and is adorned with a loosened turban and other ornaments.
Seated upon the seat of the syllable *oṃ*, he shone, assuming various forms,
endowed with diverse ornaments, and beautified by manifold limbs.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the venerable sandals of the Okāra-pīṭha, [this is] the offering (bali).
The Kaṅkāla-pīṭha.
Meditative concentration.
I worship the one who holds a skeleton white as snow or a jasmine flower, who has three eyes, who is affectionate toward his devotees,
and who wields a sword, a staff, a noose, and a spear.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I offer] the venerable sandals of Kaṅkālapīṭha. Bali!
The western gate: withdrawal; meditation.
One should meditate upon Saṃhārabhairava, who is golden in color, four-armed,
and holds a hand-drum (ḍamaru), the gesture of knowledge (jñānamudrā), a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), and likewise a sword (kādyam).

One should likewise visualize the supreme goddess Saṃhāriṇī, dark-complexioned, standing at the western gate, holding a sword and a noose in her hands, and bestowing the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the reverend sandals of Saṃhāra; [offering of] bali.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the Mother who destroys all, the venerable sandals—oblation!
O Lord of the Tree Convention!
Meditative absorption.
This Lord of the Convention (Saṃketanātha) resides in the tree; he is dark-complexioned and four-armed.
Holding a sword and a *pheṭa* with two hands, she holds a small knife and a skull-cup with the other two.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the venerable sandals of Vṛkṣasaṃketanātha, [this] offering.
The Northern Gate: Vaṭuka; Meditation.
One should indeed meditate upon Vaṭukanātha, who is beyond the sequence of the prior and the posterior,
two-armed, red in color, and bearing a skull and a staff.
With one hand embracing her husband and with the other offering betel,
the Great Goddess sits upon the lap of Vaṭuka.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I offer] the venerable sandals of Kramavaṭukanātha. Bali.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To Kramavaṭukanāthavallabhā Ambā, the venerable sandals; [offering of] bali.
The all-withdrawing one.
Meditative concentration.
I worship the dark goddess who holds in her hands the all-withdrawing [noose],
the sword, the gesture of supreme knowledge (sujñānamudrā), and the khaṭvāṅga staff, among other things.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, Mother Sarvasaṃhāriṇī, [I offer] the venerable sandals; oblation.
Eastern Gate: Yoginī; Meditation.
The goddess Vetālī has a face like the moon; she is a Yoginī of jasmine-like complexion, possessing lotus-eyes and long arms with which she holds a beautiful hand-drum (ḍamaru),
a ritual knife (kartṛkā), a skull-bowl (khaṭvāṅga-pātra), a white water-lily (kumuda), and likewise various weapons.
The Lord, holding [the weapons] with his arms, conquers the world while mounted upon a heroic Vetāla.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Yāṃ, [salutation] to the Yoginīs; the sandals; the offering.
The Yoginī: Meditation.
The goddess Yoginī, seated upon a lion-throne, with a red body, three eyes, richly adorned with necklaces and ornaments, and wearing a garland of pure skulls and bones.
One should meditate upon her as an eight-year-old girl, holding in her hands a vessel, a noose, an axe, and a goad, with lotus-feet adorned with jeweled anklets.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Heṃ Heṃ, the sandals of the Yoginī. Bali.
The Kanavīra cremation ground. Meditation.
One should meditate upon the Lord, four-armed, red in color, with a beautiful form,
the all-pervading one who holds a skull, a trident, a khaṭvāṅga staff, and a shield.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I offer] the venerable sandals of Mahākanavīra, Lord of the Cremation Ground. Bali.
Then, at the head of the street, the meditation on the lineage of gurus.
Red in color and two-armed,
with a rosary for recitation in the right hand and a begging bowl in the left, he is clothed in a saffron robe.
Adorned with a crown and seated upon a black antelope skin,
the Lord is likewise established in the lotus posture and holds a staff in his right hand.
I bow to that Lord of Heroes, whom they honor everywhere.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Vīranātha.
Green in color, as before, the essence is *kāra*.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Daśakandanātha.
Blue in color, as before, adorned with ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Krodhamuninātha.
Red in color, as before, adorned with arm-ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of the lordly sage Vaśiṣṭha.
Harivarṇa is as before, adorned with armlets.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Jayadrathanātha.
These are the divine lineages.
Dark-complexioned, with his former arms adorned with ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kaṅkāla Ombā Ambā Pādukāṃ.
Saffron-colored, with arms and ornaments as before.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable Mother Mātaṅgī, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
Red in color, as before, adorned with arm-ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vārāvalī Ombinī Ambā, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
Yellow in color, as before, with arms adorned with ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Tribhuvananandanātha.
Red in color, with arms and ornaments as before.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Vijayanātha.
Red in color, as before, with arms adorned with ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Vāmadevanātha.
Blue in color, as before, with arms adorned with ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Garbhānandanātha.
He is black in color, as before, and adorned with arm-ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! Bhadrā Gaurīśvaranātha, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
Saffron-colored, as before, with arms adorned with ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Pakṣānandanātha.
White, as before, with arm-ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Icchānandanātha.
Saffron-colored, with arms and ornaments as before.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Ājavaktrānandanātha.
Red in color, as before, adorned with arm-ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, the venerable sandals of Bindanātha.
Red in color, as before, adorned with arm-ornaments.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! [I worship] the venerable sandals of Bodhānandanātha.
Thus concludes the worship of the lineage of gurus at the front of the street.
In the four corners, beginning with the northeast (īśāna), is the worship of Jambhanī and the others.
Meditative absorption.
Holding a sword, an arrow, a large drum, the gesture of granting boons, a skull-cup, a skin, a bow, a beautiful bell,
and the syllable *hyaṃ* joined with a dot (*bindu*), she who bestows accomplishment upon her devotees, seated upon a corpse, dark in color, and possessing lotus-like hands.
One should meditate upon the Mother of the three worlds, who is delightful with her ornaments, the subduer of obstacles, and worthy of universal veneration.
KHPHREṂ RMYŪṂ JAṂ Jambhanī, the sandals! Bali!
Meditative absorption.

I worship her who is red in hue, holding a sword, excellent arrows, a goad, a boon-granting gesture, a vessel, a flaming shield, a bow, a *kila*, a noose, and the gesture of fearlessness; she bears the *bindu* (dot), stands upon a corpse, possesses beautiful eyes, grants all desires, and paralyzes [enemies] with her tender sprouts.
She is the excellent *pārijāta* creeper for her devotees, praised by the hosts of radiant gods.
Khphreṃ Mmyūṃ, the subduing sandal; the offering.
Meditative absorption.
I worship Her who holds in Her lotus-like hands the sword, the discus, the arrow, the noose, the beautiful rosary, the vessel,

the shimmering *phetkāra*, the conch, the bow, the mace, the book, and the *bindu*; She who bestows bliss, who is praised by the hosts of gods, and who destroys the flood of suffering for Her devotees.
Blue in color, mounted upon a corpse, renowned throughout the three worlds, enchanting, and possessed of beautiful eyes.
KH PHREṂ KṢMYŪṂ MAṂ, [I offer] the sandals of Mohanī. Bali!
Meditative absorption.

I worship the Supreme Goddess, who is radiant white, holding a sword and a mace, and bearing a thunderbolt and a garland; she holds a vessel, a *pheṭaka*, along with a conch and a bell in her other hands;
she is accompanied by a book and a dot (*bindu*), bestows happiness, is the power of attraction, and resides upon a corpse.
She was worshipped with joy by hosts of gods and was endowed with compassion for her devotees.
KHPHREṂ SMYŪṂ ĀṂ ĀKARṢAṆĪ PĀDUKĀṂ || BALI ||
Then, on the eight petals, there is the worship of Brahmāṇī and the others, as well as Asitāṅga and the rest.
Yellow in color, with four arms and adorned with four faces,
she holds a book and a rosary for recitation, while displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
To the Great Goddess seated upon a swan, who is devoted to the four Vedas,
the goddess who delights in yellow flowers and is anointed with yellow perfumes.
Yellow in color, four-armed, holding a trident and a bell,
with a flaying knife and a skull-cup in his hands, he stands upon a corpse and wears a garland of severed heads.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ. Salutation to the sandals of the venerable Akṣa-Aśitāṅga-Bhairava, who is Maṅgalā the courtesan, the Brahmāṇī power, and the one known as Ākhyā at Prayāga.
Meditative absorption.
O you who resemble the snowy mountain and the moon, who hold a trident and a rosary,
who carry a water-pot and extend a hand in the gesture of giving, whose seat is the bull— salutations to you!
Red in color, with four arms, holding a banner and a goad,
a skull-cup and a hand marked with a bindu, standing upon a corpse, and adorned with a garland of severed heads.
Aiṁ Kaṁ Khaṁ Gaṁ Ghaṁ Ṅaṁ. Salutation to Varuṇā, Ilā, Carcikā, Sundinī, Māheśvarī, Āgneyī, Ikṣa, and Rurubhairava, to the venerable sandals (śrīpādukās).
Meditative absorption.
The supreme goddess is intensely red, four-armed, and holds a spear and a trident;
she possesses the vessel of accomplishment and rides upon a peacock.
The god of black complexion and great splendor, holding a staff and a skull-cup, bearing a sacrificial knife and a water-pot, seated upon a corpse, and wearing a garland of severed heads.

Aiṃ Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ. Salutation to the sandals of the venerable Caṇḍabhairava, who is in Kolāpura, [accompanied by] Ūhāyī, Yogāyī, Kevartī, and Komārī, and [presiding over] the southern [direction], the bull, and the [syllables] Ūkṣaḥ.
Meditative absorption.
O Great Goddess Harivaṇā, who bears the conch, discus, and mace,
holding blue lotuses and lotuses in your hands and seated upon Garuḍa— salutations to you!
I always worship him who is smoke-colored, four-armed, holding a noose and a goad, with a skull and a chisel in his hands, and whose vehicle is a corpse.

Aiṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ. Salutation to Aṭṭahāsa, to Ṛśāyī, to Harasiddhā, to Khaṭakā, to Vaiṣṇavī, to the Nairṛta direction, to Ṛkṣa, to Krodhabhairava, and to the venerable sandals (śrīpādukās). Namah!
Meditative concentration.
The goddess Vārāhī has a terrifying, blood-red body; she holds a fish and a goad, and bears a skull-cup and a staff, seated firmly upon a buffalo.
Dark-complexioned, four-armed, holding a sacrificial knife and a staff,
with a skull in his hand as a banner, and adorned with ornaments of severed heads.
Aiṁ taṁ thaṁ daṁ dhaṁ naṁ. Salutation to Jayantika, Ḷśāyī, Bhaṭṭāyī, Kaṃdhakī, Vārāhī, Vāruṇī, Ḷkṣaḥ, and to the sandals of Unmattabhairava.
Meditative absorption.
The goddess, resembling yellow orpiment, holding a parasol and a bell,
and bearing a great vajra and the gesture of granting boons, stands upon the elephant of the [southeastern] direction.
Blue in color, with four arms, holding a bell and a ḍamaru drum,
with a skull and a drop in his hands, seated upon a corpse, and adorned with a garland of severed heads.
Aiṃ Paṃ Phaṃ Baṃ Bhaṃ Maṃ. Salutation to Caritrā, Airāyī, Kīlikīlā, Rajakī, Māhendrī, Vāyavya, Ekṣa, and to Kapālīśabhairava and the Śrīpādukās.
Meditative absorption.
Draṣṭrākalā has red limbs, carries a sword and a shield,
holds a skull-cup and a chisel in her hands, stands upon a corpse, and wears a garland of severed heads.
The god is white in color, four-armed, holding a trident and a vessel, possessing three eyes, bearing a mallet,
with a serpent in his hand, and most beautiful.
Aiṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ. Salutation to the venerable sandals of Ohāyī, Kālarātrī, Chipinī, Cāmuṇḍā, Kauberī, Aukṣa, and Bhīṣaṇabhairava at Ekāmraka.
Meditative absorption.
Resembling a dark blue cloud, the Great Goddess holds a conch, a discus, and an excellent mace;
she is three-eyed and rests upon the moon.
Red in color with red eyes, holding a trident and a vessel,
wearing a garland of severed heads, the Great God is well-seated upon a corpse-throne.
Aiṃ Śaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Kṣaṃḥ. Salutation to the sandals (śrīpādukā) of Devīkoṭa, Ahlāyī, Bhīṣaṇī, Koṣaṭī, Mahālakṣmī, Īśānī, and Aṃ Kṣaḥ Saṃhārabhairava. [Offer] this *bali* to them.
Thus ends the worship of Brahmāṇī and the others.
Then, on the twelve petals, there is the worship of Śiva and the others.
Meditative absorption.
Śivādūtī, Vegavatī, Māyā, Bhadrā, and Khiṅkinī.
Viḍālī, Yamahihvā, Ṛkṣakarṇī, and Ghaṇṭodarī.
Cauramātā, Ulūkī, and Karaṅkinī— these twelve are of all various complexions and are adorned with four arms.
Others hold a skull-cup, a bell, a khaṭvāṅga staff, and a human skull;
they are red, white, blue, and another is green in color.

She has the luster of saffron and is deep yellow; she has the radiance of a kunda flower and a red glow; she resembles snow and appears smoky; she has the hue of durva grass and the brilliance of saffron.
These goddesses, who bestow all accomplishments, should be meditated upon and worshipped.
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, the venerable sandals of the Mother Śivādevī.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, to the venerable mother goddess Vegavatī, the auspicious sandals!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable Mother Māyādevī, the glorious pādukā.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, the venerable mother Bhadrādevī, [I worship] the auspicious sandals.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Khiṃ, to the Mother Goddess Khinī, the venerable sandals!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the Mother Goddess Viḍālīdevī.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable mother goddess Yamajihvā, [I worship] her venerable sandals.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Ambā Ṛkṣakarṇā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! To the goddess Ghaṇṭodarī Ambā, the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, to the venerable sandals of the Mother Goddess Caulamātā Ambā.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, the Mother Goddess Ulūkī, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the Mother Goddess Karakiṇī, the venerable sandals!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the Mother Goddess Kākinī, the venerable sandals [of the deity].
This is the bali offering for them. Thus ends the worship at the twelve petals.
Then follows the worship of the three worlds.
Meditative absorption.
One should worship her who holds a mace, a conch, and a discus in her hands, who has a dark-complexioned body, eyes like blue lotuses, and who resides within the first enclosure.
Hrīṃ, the sandals. The offering.
Meditative absorption.
I always salute the supreme Śvetā Devī, who is embraced by two [consorts];
I worship her as she holds a trident, the gesture of granting boons, a vessel, and the gesture of fearlessness.
The auspicious sandals. The offering.
Meditative absorption.
One should visualize the goddess of the third enclosure, red in color and with a lotus face,
holding in her lotus-like hands a lotus, a beautiful garland, a staff, and a water-pot.
KH PHREṂ PĀDUKĀṂ || BALI || Thus is the worship of one’s chosen goddess (strīṣṭapūjā).
Then, according to the statement regarding the hexagon, there is the worship of the deities of the six limbs.
In the southeast: meditation.
One should place the supreme Heart-Goddess, whose entire body is white, holding a noose and a goad,
and bestowing the [mudrās of] skull-bowl, trident, fearlessness, and boon.
Khphreṃ! O Supreme Swan-like Goddess, Power of Omniscience, Heart-Lord, the venerable sandalwood slipper!
Īśāna | Meditation |
One should place on the head the goddess Śirodevī, yellow in color, adorned with the previously mentioned weapons, endowed with all ornaments, and the bestower of success.
Khphreṃ! To the one who bestows the path to nirvāṇa, the eternal power of satisfaction, the Lord of the Head, I pay homage to the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā).
In the southwest: meditation.

And upon the crest [of the head], one should always install the goddess Śikhā, who is red, surrounded by her primary weapons, fish-eyed, eternally bestowing happiness, and saluted by the lords of heroes.
Khphreṃ! O pacifier of adverse calamities, O Lord Śikhānātha of primordial awakening, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
In the northwest: meditation.
The goddess Varma was yellow in color and adorned with weapons as before.
One should place the slender maiden dressed in red garments, who is uniquely honored by hosts of heroes.

KH PHREṂ! O you who shatter all enemies, misfortunes, and afflictions, O Sovereign Power of Independence (Svatantratā-Śakti), [I worship] the venerable sandals of the Lord of Armor in the east, southeast, and the center. Meditation:
One should place the eternal Netradevī, who is black in color, endowed with weapons,
beautiful in all her limbs, into the eyes.
Khphreṃ! To the boat for crossing the ocean of all calamities, to the power of non-deprivation, to Netranātha, to the venerable pādukā!
In the intermediate direction between the west and the north: meditation.
One should always install upon one's limbs the goddess Astradevī, who has the luster of crystal and holds weapons as before; she bestows all desired objects.
Khphreṃ! O Śakti who crushes all enemies, infinite in form, Mistress of Weapons, the venerable sandals!
This is the *bali* for those [deities]. Thus is the six-limbed [ritual].
In the hexagon, there is the worship of the six Ḍākinīs.
Meditative absorption.
The goddess resembles black collyrium and is like a dark blue cloud;
she is endowed with eight arms, possesses three eyes, and is of great strength.
With a formidable face, she is terrible, with slightly protruding fangs and a fierce, terrifying appearance;
she is adorned with *kiṭiṭi* and vajras, and her ear-ornament is a bone seal.
O lady of excellent hips, she who is fierce in her strength holds in her right hand a trident, a knife, a sword, and the terrifying king of serpents as weapons.
In her left hands, she shines with the gesture of fearlessness, a shield, a noose, and a spear;
she stands in the prime of youth, intoxicated with passion, and reeling with the bliss of wine.
Endowed with various ornaments and adorned with diverse finery,
O Goddess, you have the face of a cat and are always fond of raw flesh.
Mounted upon the back of a cat, adorned with a dangling garland of bones,
a Ḍākinī has arisen and is stationed in the eastern corner.
Aiṁ ḍmlvryūṁ, the venerable mother Ḍākinī, [I worship] the holy sandals.
Meditative absorption.
Rākiṇī is red in color, stained crimson with blood;
the goddess has the face of an owl and is endowed with eight arms.
Adorned with a variegated crown and earrings,
she holds in her left hands a skull-bowl, a conch, a trident, and the gesture of fearlessness.
In her right and left [hands], she holds a vajra, a staff, a noose, and a mace;
she is enriched with the splendor of various ornaments and adorned with diverse decorations.
Perched upon an owl, most terrifying, and drinking the blood and flesh,
the goddess went to the southeast corner, blazing with great splendor.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Rmlvryūṃ, the venerable mother Rākinī, [I worship] the Śrīpādukā.
Meditative concentration.
Lākinī is yellow in color, with a slightly reddish glow;
she has the face of a vulture, is exceedingly fierce, and is attended by both divine and non-divine beings.
Adorned with a variegated crown and divine earrings,
she possessed eight arms, was celestial, and could travel through the sky.
In her left hands she holds a skull-bowl, a bell, and likewise a trident and a shield; in her right hands she holds a chopper, a severed head, a sword, a conch, and a cord.
Endowed with various ornaments and adorned with gold and jewels,
their minds were intoxicated with wine, and their eyes were slightly rolling.
Complete with all the [auspicious] marks, flesh-eating, and possessing a garland of skulls;
seated on a vulture-throne, most fierce, she stands in the southern corner.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Lmlvryūṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of the Mother Lākinī.
Meditative absorption.
Kākinī has the form of a crow and possesses a luster like black smoke;
she is the color of a crow, most terrifying, and fearsome with the cry of a crow.
Endowed with eight arms and adorned with divine earrings,
she wears a variegated crown composed of various jewels.
A garland made of divine jewels shines upon her neck;
intoxicated by youth, she is adorned with flesh and beautiful garments.
Richly adorned with all ornaments and complete in all her limbs,
she holds a bow, a spear, and likewise a thunderbolt, while extending the gesture of fearlessness with her left hand.
Holding an arrow, a sword, a thread, and a conch shell, she stands to the right;
most terrible, she threatens [the enemy] while perched upon the back of a crow.
Residing in the southwest corner, she bestows the fruit of all accomplishments.
Aiṁ KMLVRYŪṂ, [I worship] the sandals of the Mother Kākānī.
Meditative absorption.
The *sākinī* has the luster of smoke-colored [clouds], the color of wine, and great strength;
she has the face of a lion, a mighty roar, and is terrifying with a tongue and the tips of fangs.
Adorned with a variegated crown and decorated with earrings,
she is endowed with eight arms and embellished with various ornaments.
O beloved, a trident, a sword, and likewise a discus, as well as a staff, are positioned on the right; while a skull-bowl, a water-pot, a thread, and a vajra are raised in the left hands.
Adorned with all ornaments and beautiful in every limb,
they were in the prime of youth, intoxicated with passion, with eyes fixed upon him, and possessed of great strength.
Mounted upon a lion, always fond of marrow liquor,
she stands stationed in the western corner, making a threatening gesture.
Aiṁ Smlvryūṁ: [I worship] the venerable sandals of the Mother Sākinī.
Meditative absorption.
Hākinī has the complexion of a lotus and a radiance that is somewhat yellow;
she has the face of a tiger, is most terrible, and is fearsome with her quivering, sharp fangs.
Yawning and devouring her [victim], she possessed thick hair and great luster;
she was endowed with eight arms and adorned with various ornaments.
The right hands, raised upward, hold a banner, a noose, a trident, and a mallet; likewise, the left hands, following the path of the left, hold a skull-bowl, a spear, and a fruit.
Mounted upon a tiger, she is of great luster, in the prime of youth, and intoxicated with passion;
she is eternally fond of the liquor of semen, voracious, and capable of assuming many forms.
Situated in the northwestern corner, she constantly dispels all obstacles.
Aiṃ Hmlvryūṃ Hāṃ, the venerable mother Hākinī, [I worship] the Śrīpādukā.
Thus ends [the section on] the six Ḍākinīs.
The *ojāpūkā* worship is in the right triangle.
Meditative absorption.
Resembling a dark blue cloud, longing for the waves of water, the goddess has three eyes and four arms; she is the bestower of boons, holding a spear and a noose.
The goddess Kambudharā holds a noose, adorned with various garlands of flowers;
she is endowed with every auspicious mark and decorated with all ornaments.
Khphreṃ, the sandals for the sacred seat of Jālandhara.
The meditation on the left [triangle].
The Great Goddess has the form of the moon, with a radiance equal to ten million flashes of lightning;
she has four arms, one face, and three eyes, and is none other than Śivā.
Adorned with earrings resembling jewels and crowns embellished with gems,
they hold spears and goads in their left hands, while in their right hands they hold lotus mandalas.
A garland fashioned from various jewels shines upon her neck;
she is complete with all auspicious marks and beautiful in every limb.
Adorned with various ornaments, she possessed full and rounded breasts;
in the midst of her waves-like triple folds, she was graced by a line of hair.
Khphreṃ, the sandals for Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha.
At the apex of the triangle: meditation.
Dark as the petal of a blue lotus, with lips like the *bimba* fruit and a beautiful smile,
she has one face, three eyes, and two arms, assuming forms at will.
Her hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness; she is adorned with various armlets, a variegated crown, and earrings that grace her ears.
A necklace of jewels, rich with radiant luster, shines upon her neck;
a string of pearls hangs down as far as her feet.
Slender-waisted, with ample hips and full, rounded breasts,
she was endowed with every protective grace, her face lit with a gentle smile.
Endowed with all ornaments and possessed of all limbs,
she bestows all accomplishments and grants the fruits of all desires.
Seated upon the throne of the wind-element, they reveal the various divisions of the winds.
Khphreṃ! To the seat of Oḍiyāna, the sandals!
The inner triangle: meditation.
White as snow, jasmine, and the moon, with a luster like camphor,
she has four arms and three eyes, and her hands hold a noose and a fierce staff.
Holding spears and swords, divine, and adorned with crowns and other ornaments;
all of them assuming various forms and decorated with diverse jewels and finery.
Richly endowed with the beauty of every limb, marked by all the auspicious characteristics,
Oḍeśī, the mistress of the wheel, is accompanied by Oḍanātha.
Khphreṃ! To the seat of Oḍiyāna, the sandals!
The worship of the three powers is in the left triangle.
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate upon a pedestal made of vajra, situated in the midst of the ocean of milk.
There, a divine lion-throne was present, possessing a radiance equal to a blazing fire.
There, O Goddess, is an auspicious lotus with eight petals and a pericarp;
there is the orb of the sun, and upon that, five corpses.
The one whose banner is the bull, capable of destroying perverse pleasures, stands together with her;
upon his back is the Mother of the World, whose lotus feet are in the pratyālīḍha posture.
White as a conch shell or cow’s milk, red in color, and possessing three eyes;
she holds her own severed head in her left hand and a blood-stained flaying knife in her right.
She whose earrings, armlets, anklets, bracelets, and other ornaments have dissolved away,
who is adorned with large pearls, whose chest is broad, and who wears a serpent as a sacred thread.
Adorned with ornaments of bone, she wears a variegated girdle of small bells and a garland of skulls around her neck, with a tiger skin draped about her waist.
One should contemplate her adorned with crescent-moon ornaments, radiant with a crown,
and drinking the blood flowing from her own neck.
To the right [is] Varṇinī, red in color, emerging from the armpit of the Goddess;
she is red in hue, with an excellent head, and wears a red serpent as a sacred thread.
One should visualize [the goddess] adorned with all ornaments, clothed in an elephant hide,
being drunk from by the right channel of the Great Goddess;
she has two arms, holds a flaying knife and other implements, possesses three eyes, and is adorned with bones.
And on the left of the Goddess is Ḍākinī, who greedily devours the world.
Having the complexion of a swarm of Karālikas, three-eyed, delighting in the terrible,
clad in human skin, with a tongue lolling out, she is terrifying.
One should visualize the left channel of the Great Goddess as a headless trunk, adorned with necklaces and armlets, with disheveled hair, holding a skull-cup, and being drunk from by Mahādevī.
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Śrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ eṃ vajravairocanīye hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā || Triśakti ||
In the upper corner: meditation.
Profound, intoxicated with passion, possessing a golden luster and uniform radiance,
four-armed, three-eyed, and seated upon a lotus throne.
In her right hands she holds a mallet and a noose, and in her left a tongue and a vajra;
she wears yellow garments and possesses firm, full breasts, and is joined in union [with her consort].
Adorned with golden earrings, yellow in complexion, with the crescent moon and the serpent Śeṣa as her ornaments,
wearing yellow jewelry and garlands, she is seated upon a golden lion-throne.
Having thus meditated upon the Mother of the World, who causes the paralysis of enemies.
Oṃ hlīṃ, O Vagalāmukhī, paralyze the mouths and speech of all the wicked; nail down their tongues;
destroy their intellect! Hlīṃ oṃ svāhā. This is the Brahmāstra.
In the southeast corner: the visualization.
Hrīṃ! [I salute her] who has the color of molten gold, who is adorned with various flowers, who is clothed in divine garments, and who rides upon a buffalo throne.
With crowns and earrings in the shape of rings, with armlets, jeweled anklets,
and variegated garlands of gems, they were adorned with excellent strings of pearls.
She is adorned with eighteen arms, her breasts and chest are full,
she is endowed with all ornaments, and her radiance is equal to ten million flashes of lightning.
She holds a sword, an arrow, a discus, and a vajra-hook;
she is auspicious, with hands granting boons and holding a hand-drum (ḍamaruka), and is beautifully adorned with a trident and a vessel.
And in the right hand, these [implements] are auspicious according to their beauty:
the *pheṭaka*, the bow, the mace, and the beautifully adorned bell.
She holds a noose and makes the threatening gesture with her hand, and possesses a khaṭvāṅga and a mass of hair;
she is marked by the bindu-mudrā, resides in Sindhu, and is seated upon a lion throne.
Having stood beneath him and severed the head of the great asura Mahiṣa,
he emerged from his neck, [slaying] the Daitya of great strength and prowess.
Having pierced her with his trident, he held her by her hair.
Having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess, who bestows the fruits of all desires.
Thus is meditation.
Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hsphreṃ ugracaṇḍe raṇamardini hūṃ phreṃ, always protect you and me, jū saḥ! O Mṛtyuharā, obeisance, svāhā! [This is] the sword-weapon mantra.
The worship of the central field.
Meditative absorption.

One should meditate upon the Lord, the Master of the Field, who is black in color, four-armed, and holds a hand-drum (ḍamaru), a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga), a skull-cup (kapāla), and the gesture of primordial wisdom (jñānamudrā).
Thhsrauṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ! O Kṣetrapāla, fierce with the power to destroy all things, [I worship] the venerable sandals.
O five-faced one!
RJJHRĪṂ Mahācaṇḍa Tejasaṃkarṣaṇi Kāli Manthāne HAḤ. [The syllables.]
Phreṃ āṃ koṃ phiṃ mahāsiddhisamaye khphreṃ bhairavī ghoralakṣmī varaprade svāhā || Varṇa ||
Āṃ phiṃ phāṃ, O Mahāsṛṣṭi Caṇḍalakṣmī Siddheśvarī, phe phaṭ! [The syllables.]
Hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ pheṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. [The syllables.]
KH PHREṂ | Namo bhagavatī siddhilakṣmīśvarī phaṭ svāhā || [The Color] ||
This is the offering (bali) for them. Thus concludes the worship of Pañcavaktra.
Then one should worship the ten weapons.
In the east: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, I worship the venerable sandals of Varadanātha.
In the southeast: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Abhayanātha, Śrī Dukaṃ.
In the south: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Lord of the Kalasa, Śrī Dukaṃ!
Nairṛtya: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable sandals of Khaṭvāṅganātha.
In the west: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable sandals of Muṇḍanātha.
In the northwest: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Lord of the Trident, Śrī Dukaṃ!
O gentle one! Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable sandals of Aṅkuśanātha!
In the northeast: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable sandals of Khaḍganātha.
Above: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable sandals of Kapālanātha.
Below: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, the venerable sandals of Pāśanātha. Thus is the worship of the ten weapons.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, [I offer] the sandals to Ānandaśakti Bhairavānandavīrādhipati Śkṣmlvryīṃ. [Bali.]
Aghora. Meditation.
Five-faced and of great splendor, blazing with fifteen eyes, ten-armed and most formidable, adorned with various garlands and wreaths.
Adorned with various ornaments and decorated with necklaces and anklets,
he bears a divine mass of matted hair, with the crescent moon as his crest-jewel.
O beloved, one should meditate upon the eye in the eastern face as being divine, white as cow’s milk, resembling foam, possessing white luster, and producing great radiance.
One should contemplate the left face as having the form of a pomegranate flower, accompanied by a bandhūka blossom, and resembling the rising sun.
O beautiful one, may he who is golden-hued, resembling gold, with the luster of saffron and yellow orpiment,
divine and bestowing great radiance, grant his protection in the western direction.
The face of the Seer is formidable and fierce, momentarily turning slightly red;
it is dark like a blue lotus, deep black, and possesses a luster equal to blue collyrium.
Meditating upon the one known as Aghora— who is made formidable by a jewel-serpent, who has tawny hair, and who is most terrifying— bestows the accomplishment of all aims.
The face of Īśāna is upward-facing, the form of emanation, both supreme and non-supreme; it resembles snow, the kunda flower, and the moon, and is as pure and stainless as clear crystal.
He was refreshing the entire world with a mass of moonbeams,
raining down a great flood of streams resembling nectar.
Meditating upon Īśāna, one obtains the qualities such as *aṇimā* and others;
[he holds] a trident, a knife, a sword, and a rosary made of the king of serpents.
O lady of excellent hips, she shines with weapons in her right hands;
O beloved, she holds a skull-bowl, a hand-drum, a spear, a noose, and a goad.
In her left [hand], O beautiful one, are those divine weapons, blazing and most splendid;
on her shoulder, O lovely lady, is the king of serpents adorned with a garland of *vaḍa* flowers.
Upon her neck is a necklace of scorpions, and her two ears are adorned with radiant ornaments;
she sits upon a great lotus throne, encircled by a girdle at her waist.
His feet are adorned with small bells, rich in beauty, and decorated with garlands of jewels; they are joined by anklets and well-ornamented with strings of pearls.
Seated upon the Ananta throne, resembling molten gold,
he is established upon the Ananta throne as the locus of seventy million mantras.
Having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess Tārā, who is divine, resembling snow, and radiant like the moon, [one should contemplate her] within the center of the wheel according to one's own will.
Thus concludes the section on meditative absorption.
Aiṃ Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghoreṃ Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phe, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hraiṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ Rudrarūpe Hraḥ, [I offer] the sandals. Bali.
Vajra. Meditation.
And having meditated upon the supreme goddess, who holds a vajra in her hand and possesses great power.
O Dear One, she is endowed with the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and her hand holds a noose.
The Goddess, wearing red garments, resembling the rising sun,
endowed with all auspicious marks, and adorned with every ornament.
Seated upon a vajra-lotus throne, adorned with hanging necklaces of various colors, she possesses three eyes and is endowed with earrings and a variegated crown.
Having thus meditated upon the goddess Mahākubjī, who has the luster of the rising sun and a slightly smiling face, one attains success in the Vajra.
Thus ends the section on meditative absorption.
Aiṃ Aiṃ Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ Trailokyākarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmāṅgadrāvaṇī Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇī Aiṃ Sauṃ Saḥ Pādukāṃ. Bali.
The vow of the ascetic; meditation.
The supreme goddess with six faces, resembling a dark blue cloud,
endowed with twelve arms, and adorned with serpent ornaments.
Adorned with a crown and earrings, wearing a serpent as a sacred thread,
she holds a trident, a knife, a sword, a serpent, a spear, and a mirror.
With her right hands, the goddess holds a khaṭvāṅga, a noose, the gesture of fearlessness (abhayamudrā), a staff, and a water-pot, possessing a radiance like a blazing fire of time.
On the left side, O lady of excellent hips, is the weapon (astra) with the luster of the fire of cosmic destruction;
it stands pervading the universe, with the Goddess situated in the center of the universe.
Having meditated upon her as being filled with garlands of flames, blazing with great splendor,
situated in the center of the city of Śṛṅgāṭapura, and standing within the submarine fire (vaḍavānala).
Thus concludes the section on meditative concentration.

Aiṁ! Salutation to the Blessed One, Hsphreṁ! To Kubjikā, Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṁ Chīṁ Kiṇi Vicce! [Salutation to] the Sandal-powder. [Offering of] the Bali.
Aiṃ! Salutations to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā! Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ! To the one with the face of Aghorā, Ṅa Ña Ṇa! Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi Vicce! [I offer] the sandals. The sacrificial offering (bali).
Aiṃ! O Blessed One, Siddhā, Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ Kubjikā, Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ Khagā, Ai Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhi Kini Vicce, [I offer] the sandals. Bali.
The triple añjali gesture.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, obeisance! To the sandals! Bali!
The Six-Limbed Root Worship of the Mother (Mūlaṣaḍaṅgaṇapūjā). Khphreṃ, homage to the heart. Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head.
Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the topknot (śikhā). Khphreṃ, hūṃ to the armor (kavaca). Khphreṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes (netratraya).
KHPHREṂ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ || GĀYATRĪ || KHPHREṂ SIDDHILAKṢMĪ VIDMAHE NAVATYADHĪKA DHIMahi TANNŌ LAKṢMĪḤ PRA-CODAYĀT ||
Bali: Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers—obeisance!
One should display the *yonimudrā*. [Then follows] the libation (*tarpaṇa*).
Homage to Śrīnātha; homage to Śrīsiddhinātha; homage again and again to Śrīkujeśanātha.
Then follows the offering of the bali-oblation.

Having worshipped each *pratibali* with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), vermilion (*siṃdūra*), and other substances, [one should take] the special *argha* water contained in the vessel with the ring finger and thumb.
Khphreṃ, homage to the Great Rudra-throne!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraiṃ Hrauṃ Hraḥ, salutation to the seat of Mahābhairava.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrāṃ! To the seat of Mahārudra, destroy all my obstacles;
fulfill all my desires! Accept this offering of wine, meat, and rice, along with the bali according to my capacity; Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Then, by Siddheśvarī.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ! To the one seated upon the great corpse-seat: destroy all my obstacles;
accomplish all my desires! Accept this offering of wine, meat, and rice, as well as this *bali* according to my capacity; Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
The nine-syllable [mantra] is to be worshipped in three ways.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
Oṃ, may we know Siddhilakṣmī; may the Great One who possesses ninety [qualities] inspire us toward that Lakṣmī.
Having worshipped him tenfold, the offering of the *bali* for the enclosures (*āvaraṇas*) is performed.
The worship of Krama, Gaṇapati, Nātha, and the others, followed by the offering of the bali in due order.
With the substance placed in the vessel, by joining the left thumb and middle finger.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Vmlvryūṁ! O Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha, destroy all my obstacles;
accomplish all my desires! Accept this *bali* offering with all ritual services! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
[Recite] while joining the ring finger and the thumb.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Gmlvryūṃ! O Lord Gaṇapati of the Krama lineage, together with your beloved consort, bring all people under my influence, destroy all obstacles, and accept this offering along with all ritual services; Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Kṣmlvryūṁ Hūṁ! O Kṣetrapāla of your own abode, Mahābhairava, destroy all my obstacles; accept this offering of all ritual services! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Kṣetrapāla, seated upon the throne of Kṛtānta, possessed of great strength and ferocity, together with your beloved consort, accept this *bali* offering accompanied by all ritual services; fulfill all my desires, grant me success, protect me! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
By means of the union of the ring finger and the thumb.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Smlvryūṁ Saḥ! Accept this offering (bali) from all [beings], svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Hskhphrīṁ! O Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍī, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Aṁ Kaṁ Caṁ Ṭaṁ Taṁ Paṁ Yaṁ Saṁ! O eight Kṣetrapālas beginning with Hetuka, accept this bali offering; svāhā!

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ Amlvryūṃ! O Prayāga-kṣetra, O Asitāṅga-Bhairava, Āṃ Ā Kṣā Ī! O Sarvamaṅgalā of the Kāmarūpa-pīṭha, for the courtesan [and] Goddess Brahmāṇī, destroy all my obstacles and fulfill all my desires!
Accomplish this offering of honey, meat, and rice; accept the bali! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ Kmlvryūṃ! O Rurubhairava of Vārāṇasī, I lā ī Vasakī Sauṇḍinī, Goddess Māheśvarī, destroy all my obstacles;
fulfill all my desires! Accept this offering of wine, meat, and rice as a *bali*—Hūṃ!
Phaṭ svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Caṁ Chaṁ Jaṁ Jhaṁ Ñaṁ Cmlvryūṁ! O Caṇḍabhairava of the Kolāpura sacred field, O Ūhāyeka Vartinī, O Yogapīṭha, O Goddess Kaumārī! Destroy all my obstacles; fulfill all my desires!
Accept this offering of wine, meat, and rice as a *bali*—Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ṭaṃ Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ Ṭmlvryūṃ! O Aṭṭahāsa-kṣetra, Ṛṃ, Ṛkṣa Krodhabhairava, Ṛ Sā Ī Ha Ra! O Siddhā, Khaṭṭakā, Goddess Vaiṣṇavī, destroy all my obstacles and fulfill all my desires!
Accept this offering of honey, meat, and rice; *bali*, *hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Taṃ Thaṃ Daṃ Dhaṃ Naṃ Tmlvryūṃ! O Urjanīkṣatre, Ḷ Unmattabhairava, Ḷ Ṣā Ī Ihāyī Bhaṭṭakī Kaṃdakī Vārāhī Devī! Destroy all my obstacles;
fulfill all my desires! Accept this *bali* offering of wine, meat, and rice; Hūṃ!
Phaṭ svāhā!

Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Paṁ Phaṁ Baṁ Bhaṁ Maṁ Pmlvryūṁ! O Ekapādabhairava of the field of conduct (caritrakṣetra)! Aiṁ Śā Ī! O Indrāṇī Jālandharakilikī Rajakī Indrāṇī Devī! Destroy all my obstacles; fulfill all my desires! Accept this offering of wine, meat, and rice, and this *bali* oblation! Hūṁ!
Phaṭ svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Ymlvryūṃ! O Bhīṣaṇabhairava of Ekāmra, O Kālarātri and Chippiṇī of Oḍiyāna, O Goddess Cāmuṇḍā! Destroy all my obstacles;
fulfill all my desires! Accept this offering of wine, meat, and rice as a bali! Hūṃ!
phaṭ svāhā ||

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Kṣaṃ Śmlvryaṃ. O Devīkoṭa, Aṃ Saṃhārabhairava, Aḥ Ākhyāya, Bhīṣaṇī, Mātaṅgī, Mahālakṣmī, O Goddess, destroy all my obstacles and fulfill all my desires; accept this offering of wine, meat, and rice as a *bali*.
HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Dhāṃ! O Dhāmāmbā, destroy all my obstacles, fulfill all my desires, accept this offering—Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Dhāṃ! O Dhāmavatī, destroy all my obstacles, accomplish all my desires, accept this offering—Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Dhāṃ! By Your splendor, destroy all my obstacles; fulfill all my desires; accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Vāṁ! O Goddess of the Target-Circle, destroy all my obstacles, accomplish all my desires, accept the offering—Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Rāṁ! O Raviprabhā, destroy all my obstacles, accomplish all my desires, accept this offering—Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Vaṁ! O Virājanī, destroy all my obstacles, fulfill all my desires, accept this offering—Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ḍmlvryūṃ! O Ḍākinī, accept this offering; destroy all obstacles, fulfill our heart’s desires, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Rmlvryūṁ! O Rākini, accept this offering; destroy all obstacles;
accomplish my heart's desires! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Lmlvryūṃ! O Lākinī, accept this offering; destroy all obstacles and fulfill our heart's desires! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Kmlvryūṁ! O Kākinī, accept this offering; destroy all obstacles and accomplish our heart's desires! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Smlvryūṃ! O Śākinī, accept this offering; destroy all obstacles, fulfill our heart's desires! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Hmlvryūṁ! O Hākinī, accept this offering; destroy all obstacles and fulfill our heart's desires! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, O Mother Śivādevī, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ! O Mother Bhadrādevī, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Khiṃ! O Goddess Khiṇī Ambā, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, Mother Goddess Viḍālīdevī, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, O Goddess Yamajihvā Ambā, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Goddess Ṛkṣakarṇī, Mother, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Goddess Ghaṭodarī Ambā, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ! O Mother Goddess Ulūkī, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, O Goddess Karaṅkiṇī Ambā, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Mahākamalacaṇḍinī Raudramukhī Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hroṃ Kāṃ Śrīkākamukhī Śrīdevī, accept this bali! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Cāṁ Caṇḍamukhī Śrīdevī, accept this bali offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Ṭūṁ, O Śrī Devī Ṭākālī, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Tṛṁ, O Śrī Devī Śrītāpiṇī, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Pṛṁ, O Śrīpāvakī Śrīdevī, accept this bali offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Goddess Yamaghaṇṭhā, accept this *bali* offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Sauḥ! O Śivādūtī, the illustrious Goddess, accept this bali offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Kṣaḥ! O Goddess Śrījayaṅkarī, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, O Goddess Krodhinī, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Goddess Sakarṣaṇī, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ, O Goddess Lelihānā, accept this offering! Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Goddess Khecarī, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Goddess Bhairavī, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ, O Varṇinī, bestower of all wisdom; O Ḍākinī, Vajravairocanī, bestower of all accomplishments, accept this bali! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ, O Bagalāmukhī, paralyze the faces and speech of all the wicked; accept the offering!
Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hsphreṃ ugracaṇḍe, destroy my enemies! Accept this offering! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ, O Goddess Śaṅkhinī, accept the offering! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, O Goddess Śivādūtī, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ! To the heart-energies beginning with omniscience and to the six limbs, accept this bali offering!
Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ! To Varadanātha, Abhayanātha, Kalaśanātha, Khaṭvāṅganātha, Maṇḍanātha, Triśūlanātha, Aṅkuśanātha, Kapālanātha, and Pāśanātha—svāhā!
To these ten, accept this bali offering! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ, to the preta consisting of the five elements, Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hrāṃ Hmkṣmlvryūṃ! O Siddheśvara, who possesses the form of Ānandabhairava, accept this bali offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
RJJHRĪṂ! O Mahācaṇḍa, O Tejaḥsaṃkarṣaṇī Kālī, O Manthānī, accept this offering! HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hraiṃ Hrauṃ Haḥ! To the one seated upon the great Rudra-throne, destroy my obstacles; fulfill all my desires;
accept this *bali* offering; grant me accomplishment! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!

Aiṁ! To these most secret Yoginīs, who dwell upon the manifest surfaces, who reside in all cremation grounds, who possess all mudrās, who are accompanied by their vehicles and retinues, who are never lacking in food—accept this bali offering!
Fulfill all my desires! Forgive me, forgive me! Kṣāṁ Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā!
BALIVIYA MANTRATHAṆḌILIJAVĀLĪTHUPĀṬABALI HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ KHPHREṂ DEVĪPUTRA VAṬUKANĀTHA KAPILAJAṬĀBHĀRABHĀSURA TRINETRAJVĀLĀMUKHA SARVAVIGHNĀN NĀSAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ ||
O Vaṭukanātha, together with Vallabhāmbā, accept this offering; svāhā!
Thus concludes the offering to Vaṭuka.
On a grass mat, on ashes, on a stone, on a wooden plank, or on the bare ground.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Thhsrauṃ Kṣuṃ! Svāhā to the Lord of this very place, together with his beloved Mother. Thus is the *kṣetrabali* offering.
