On a bare patch of ground, with a heap of ashes and a piece of cloth.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ oṃ gaṃ to Gaṇapati, together with your beloved Mother, accept this bali!
Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Thus is the bali for Gaṇapati.
[The offering] of the *thaṇḍilīya*, *javalāhaṅthu*, *pāṭa*, and *balisa*.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! To all the yogins, to all the pīṭhas, and to all the kṣetrapālas, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! Thus ends the offering to the yoginīs (yoginībali).
The *samayavidyā* for the offering of the *thaṇḍila*, the *liṅga*, the *vane*, the *dhatu*, the *pāṭa*, and the *bali*.

Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Candrayogeśvarī, Candrapīṭhavyomakālī, Mātaṅgī, Bhīmakālī, Kāmarūpiṇī, Siddhikālī, Pūrṇagiricandrakālī, Jālandharicaṇḍakālī, Oḍiyānaraktakālī! Grant the attainment of all samayas! O Susiddha, Suprasara! He Saḥ Kha Hi Li Hrīṃ!
hrūṃ vāhi kāhi khāhi khe hūṃ lāṃ khāṃ lāṃ khāṃ chāṃ hūṃ hāṃ vāṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ sauṃ hreṃ haṃ hūṃ hūṃ hreṃ ||
[Thus ends the Śrīsiddhilakṣmīsamayavidyā.]
Khphreṃ: Śivā Bhagavatī, and likewise Māyābhadrā;
Kiṃkiṇī and Vimalā, as well as Yamajihvā and Ākarṣaṇī.
Ghaṇṭodarī, Cauramātā, Kiṅkiṇī, and likewise Kākinī—
for the destruction of all obstacles and the warding off of all enemies.
May the fortune of accomplishment (siddhilakṣmī) be eternally fulfilled for me in all things. O you who are the thirteen melāpakas, Śrīsiddhilakṣmīs, accept this offering! Svāhā!
The offering of the garland-mantra is the bali.

Oṃ, homage to all the Yoginīs of all accomplishments! Homage to all the Mothers of all accomplishments! Homage to the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī, the Mistress of the entire wheel of families, who is gladdened by eternally arisen bliss! It is as follows: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! Oṃ, O Supreme Haṃsinī, Goddess who bestows the path to Nirvāṇa!

O Goddess, who pacifies calamitous afflictions, who shatters all enemies, misfortunes, and defilements, who is a boat across the ocean of all disasters, and who crushes all foes—come! Laugh! Leap! O devourer of human blood, entrails, and fat!
Crush, crush my own enemies! Eat them! Pierce with the trident! Cut with the sword! Strike!

Cut [through my obstacles] until you fulfill all my desires! O Bhagavatī of supreme compassion, who assumes the form of Mahābhairava; you who are praised by the best of the thirty gods; Mother of all mantras; you who are affectionate toward those who bow before you; Goddess Mahākālī, destroyer of Time! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Be gracious!
Make the daughter of the gods and asuras one who is incomparable in passion! Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Phaṭ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Salutations for the invocation, the installation, and the sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers.
One should display the six mudrās: the lotus, the liṅga, the śakti, the arrow, the great goad, and the yoni.
The libation.
Homage to the venerable Śrīnātha; homage to the venerable Śrīsiddhinātha; homage again and again to the venerable Śrīkujeśanātha.
[Thus ends the venerable Śrī-Śrī-Śrī-Siddhilakṣmī-deguli.]
Now, to the illustrious Śrī-Śrī-Śrī-Guhyakālī of Guliyā.
The sacrificial offering for the *thaṇḍila* of worship; the sacrificial offering for the *thaṇḍila* of the *jāvalāṅthu-pāṭa*.
Having sipped water with the threefold truth (tritatva).
Phreṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva)! Phreṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva)! Phreṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva)!
Nyāsa: Svāhā! To the weapon, Phaṭ!
The purification of the hands.
Oṃ Phreṃ, homage to the two little fingers. Siddhikarālī, homage to the two ring fingers.
Hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers. Strīṃ phreṃ, salutation to the two index fingers.
*Namaḥ* to the two thumbs; *namaḥ*. *Svāhā* to the weapon (*astra*); *namaḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands. This is the ritual placement upon the hands (*karanyāsa*).
Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the heart! Siddhikarālī, svāhā to the head!
Hrāṃ chrīṃ hūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Strīṃ phreṃ, huṃ to the armor (kavaca).
Salutation to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ! Svāhā to the weapon, phaṭ!
Thus is the ritual placement upon the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The worship of the argha vessel.
The sandals for the seat of the argha vessel.
Oṃ phreṃ siddhikarālī hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā.
The six limbs.
Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the heart! Siddhikarālī, svāhā to the head!
Hrīṁ chrīṁ hūṁ, vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair (śikhā). Strīṁ phreṁ, huṃ to the armor (kavaca).
Salutation to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ! Svāhā to the weapon, phaṭ!
Oṃ phreṃ hskṣmlvryūṃ, homage to Siddhikarālīśvarā!
Having invoked [the deity] with the Ākarṣaṇī mudrā, one performs the veiling (avaguṇṭhana).
Salutations for the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers. I shall display the cow-mudrā and the womb-mudrā.
Gāyatrī: Oṃ Phreṃ! We know the Great Mantra; we meditate upon Kāra-Saṃkarṣaṇī; may She impel our power.
Self-worship.
Oṃ phreṃ, the sandalwood sandals. Oṃ phreṃ, the unbroken rice grains sandals.
Oṃ phreṃ, the sandals of Sindūra; Oṃ phreṃ, the sandals of Mohanī.
Oṃ phreṃ, [I offer] flowers and sandals.
Bindutriya || Khphreṁ Oṃ Phreṁ, obeisance to the one consisting of the full moon.
The seat.
Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the one seated upon seven severed heads.
Oṃ phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ, homage to the great seat of Śiva.
Meditative absorption.
The Great Kālī is exceedingly secret, ten-faced, and three-eyed;
she is dark-complexioned, of great splendor, eight-armed, and slender-waisted.
One should meditate on the Goddess, whose faces possess various colors, whose nature is that of the Sun,
who is clothed in a tiger skin, and adorned with ornaments of human bone.
In his right hands, he holds a trident, a goad, a vajra, and a mallet;
in his left, a khaṭvāṅga, a noose, a vessel, a corpse, and a severed head.
Wandering through the king of sequences, which resembles a thousand suns,
she proceeds toward the single accomplishment for the sake of the meaning within the eight directions.
Cit-kālī, situated in the center of the Kula, resides in the Lord whose form is light;
she is supreme liberation, the Vidyā who transcends all states of being, and is beyond the reach of the mind.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Three handfuls of joined palms.
Oṃ phreṃ Siddhikarālī hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā | [This is for] the sandals (pādukā) | The offering (bali) |
Now follows the knowledge of enjoyment.
Oṃ, homage to Mahāmāyā! Hūṃ Phreṃ! O protectress of the three worlds! Śrīṃ Śrīṃ! Siddhi Hrīṃ! Sustain, O son, wealth, grain, jewels, gold, silver, wife, family, and the great treasure;
grant me prosperity, O Great Gaurī! Grant me memory, great intelligence, fame, sovereignty, and good fortune—O illuminator of all!

O Siddhicāmuṇḍā, who performs all actions, fulfill [me], Hrīṃ! Shower down all desires and all prosperity; cause them to rain, let them fall! Grant the great treasure! Grant the eight sovereign powers! Grant sons, wealth, long life, good fortune, wealth in grain, grain, and gold—grant these constantly!

Thus, accomplish all success! O *dhana*, *hrīṃ*! O *strīṃ*, *phreṃ*! Rain down jewels! Command and give orders to all the *yakṣas*! Grant prosperity and sovereignty! Accomplish it without obstacle! Homage!
O Mahāya, King of Yakṣas, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Strīṃ, O giver of great wealth, grant me all riches! Siddhigaurī Hūṃ Namaḥ Svāhā! Thus is the Vidyā for Enjoyment.
The Gāyatrī.
Phreṃ! We know the Kāpālinī; we meditate upon Siddhikarālī; may that Guhyā inspire us. [Bali]
Oṃ phreṃ siddhi hsphreṃ hskhphreṃ khphreṃ karālī khphreṃ hskhphreṃ hsphreṃ phreṃ oṃ svāhā. || [Bali] || [Six-limbed mantra] ||
Oṃ phreṃ, homage to the heart! Siddhikarālī, svāhā to the head!
Hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Strīṃ phreṃ, huṃ to the armor (kavaca).
Salutation to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ! Svāhā to the weapon, phaṭ!
The worship with necklaces; [the offering] in the ocean of blood.
Oṃ hūṃ kṣīṃ klīṃ phreṃ phreṃ phreṃ, the sandals of the ocean of blood! Bali!
Oṃ Phreṃ! The sandals of the ten world-protectors, beginning with Indra.
Oṃ phreṃ! The sandals of Kṣetravatuka, Yoginī, and Gaṇapatinātha.
Oṃ Phreṃ! [I worship] the lineage of gurus beginning with Śrīkaṇṭhanātha and the eight Kalāmbs, the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā).
Oṃ Phreṃ! [I worship] the sandals of the eight cremation grounds, beginning with Jayāvaha.
Oṃ Phreṃ! [I worship] the sandals of Oghādi-Ṣoḍaśakālī.
Oṃ Phreṃ! The sandals of the twelve Kālīs beginning with Sṛṣṭi.
Oṃ Phreṃ! The sandals of the eight Kālīs, beginning with Brahmavatī.
Oṃ Phreṃ! The sandals of the eight Bhairavas, beginning with Asitāṅga.
Oṃ phreṃ, the sandals of the nine Kālīs beginning with Raktā.
Khphreṃ, Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, Sṛṣṭikālikāmbā, the pādukā!
Hskhphreṁ, Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, Mother Stitikālikā, [grant] the pādukā!
ŚKHPHREṂ, Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī Saṃhārakālikāmbā, the sandalwood slipper!
Hrīṁ, Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī, Mother Sthitikālikā, [I worship] the pādukā.
Khphreṃ! To the sandals of Mahācaṇḍayogeśvarī Bhāsākālikāmbā.
This is the bali offering for them.
[Recite] "Oṃ, homage! [This is] the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood, the unbroken rice, and the flower. Then one should display the secret mudrā of the womb.
The three drops: *Namaḥ śrīnāthāya*, *namaḥ śrīsiddhināthāya*, *namaḥ śrīkujeśanāthāya*, *namo namaḥ*. [Thus ends the Śrīguhyakālīdeguli.]
Now, [the ritual] for the goddess Tripurasundarī.

The worship of the sacrificial ground (thaṇḍila). [This includes] the preparation of the sacrificial ground, the drawing of the hand-designs (hṅava), the recitation of the mantra, and the offering of the oblation (bali).
The sipping of water (ācamana) is performed with the threefold truth.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyā-tattva).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva).
The ritual placement (nyāsa): Sauṃḥ, Phaṭ to the weapon (astra).
The purification of the hands.
Aiṃ, salutation to the two thumbs. Klīṃ, salutation to the two index fingers.
Sauṁḥ, salutation to the two middle fingers. Aiṁ, salutation to the two ring fingers.
Klīṃ, salutation to the two little fingers. Sauṃ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.
Thus is the ritual placement of the hands (iti-kara-nyāsa).
Aiṃ, salutation to the heart. Klīṃ, svāhā to the head. Sauṃḥ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Aiṃ, hūṃ, for the armor; klīṃ, vauṣaṭ, for the three eyes; sauṃḥ, phaṭ, for the weapon.
Thus is the ritual placement on the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
The worship of the argha vessel.
Salutation to the seat of the Arghya vessel. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, [I invoke] the sandals.
The Six Limbs: Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, obeisance to the heart; Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, svāhā to the head.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁ, Vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁ, Hūṁ to the armor (kavaca).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, phaṭ to the weapon.
[Recite] "Oṃ, salutations to the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers. Then, one should display the *yonimudrā*.
Self-worship.
Aiṃ, sandalwood, the sandals. Klīṃ, unbroken rice, the sandals. Sauṃ, vermilion, the sandals.
Aiṃ, the sandals of Mohanī; Klīṃ Sauṃ, obeisance to the flower of the Self; Bindunāhāya.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, the Sandals.
Then follows the worship of the Goddess’s seat.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, the sandals for the one seated upon a red lotus.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ: the sandals for the seat of the five pretas.
Meditative absorption.
I worship her who has the luster of the orb of the rising sun, who possesses four arms and three eyes,
and who holds a noose, a goad, arrows, and a bow.
Thus is meditation.
Threefold salutation with joined palms.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ Klhrīṃ Hskhlhrīṃ Sklhrīṃ, the sandals of the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī.
Bali. Gāyatrī.
Aiṃ, may we know Tripurā; Klīṃ, may we meditate upon Kāmeśvarī; Tanno Sauṃ, may she impel us. Bali.
Worship of the retinue.
The libation.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ, the venerable sandals of the Nityās beginning with Kāmeśvarī.
Then the bali offering; the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ, salutation to the heart. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, svāhā to the head.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁ, Vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ, Huṃ to the armor (kavaca).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, Phaṭ to the weapon.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! To Indra and the other ten world-protectors, the sandals! The offering!
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ, [I offer] the sandals to the deity of the weapons, beginning with the thunderbolt.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ: the venerable sandals of the Goddess who bestows the supernatural powers (siddhis) such as atomization (aṇimā) and the rest.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! [I worship] the sandals of Aśitāṅga and the others, and Āṃ Brahmāṇī and the others.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, the venerable sandals of the goddesses of the mudrās, beginning with Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! O Sovereign of the Wheel of Tripura, the Eternal One (Nityā), [I worship] the venerable sandals (Śrīpādukā).
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ, [I worship] the Śrī-pādukā of the Nityā whose form is Kāmākarṣaṇī (the Attractor of Desire).
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ: [I worship] the Śrīpādukā of the Nityā Tripureśī, the Mistress of the Cakra.

Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ Ṭaṃ Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ Taṃ Thaṃ Daṃ Dhaṃ Naṃ Paṃ Phaṃ Baṃ Bhaṃ Maṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Kṣaṃḥ— the venerable sandals of the goddesses beginning with Anaṅgakusumā.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ, the eternal Śrīpādukā of Tripurasundarī, the Mistress of the Cakras.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! O Goddess who bestows all accomplishments, and so forth—[I worship] the venerable sandals of the Goddess.
Hsaiṁ Hsklīṁ Hsauṁḥ: [I worship] the Śrīpādukā of the eternal Tripurā, the Mistress of the Śrīcakra.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ; [worship] the Śrīpādukā of the Goddess, beginning with "on all limbs," and so forth.

Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, [I worship] the Śrī-pādukā of the eternal Goddess Tripurāmālinī, the Mistress of the Cakra. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ rvlūṃ, [I worship] the Śrī-pādukā of the Goddess Vaśinī, the Deity of Speech, and so forth.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! To the eternal Śrīpādukā of Tripurā Siddhā, the Mistress of the Cakra, [I offer salutation].

The libation.
Homage to the illustrious Nātha! Homage to the illustrious Siddhinātha! Homage again and again to the illustrious Kujeśanātha!
[Thus ends the Guhyakālideguli.]
The ritual of the sacrificial offering (bali) at the foot of the *pāṭala* tree on a bed of straw.
I am not capable of performing this offering.
Aiṃ: Ajara, Apakumbha, Iḍācāra, Indramūrti, Ulkāsya, Uṣmāṇḍa, and Ṛpusūdana.
Ṛmukta, Lṛptakāya, Lṝlāpa, Daivadraṃṣṭaka,
Airāvata, Oghāmba, Auṣadhīśa, and others likewise.
Antaka, Arthabāhu, Kamara, Kharānana,
Gomukha, Ghaṇṭāla, Ṅa, Ṇa, Na, and Caṇḍadhāraka.
Chaṭātoṣa, Jaṭālākhyā, Jhaṃkāra, Bhaṭeśvara, Ṭaṅkapāṇi, as well as others— Iṣṭhāṇubandha and Ḍāmara.
Dṛḍhakarṇa, Urṇatīkānta, Taḍidbhās, Sthavira, as well as Dantula, Dhana-da, Nāgakarṇa, and Pracaṇḍavān.
Phetkāra, Vīrasiṃha, Bhṛkuṭī, Meghabhāsura,
Yugānta, Raurava, Lambauṣṭha, and likewise Vatsara.
Śukatuṇḍa, Ṣaḍālāsya, Sunāsa, and likewise Huhuka;
Kṣayantaka is the fiftieth—thus are the fifty Kṣetrapālas proclaimed.
When fifty items are extracted, the Kṣetrapālas remain in their respective places;
however, when the remaining [letters] are devoid of vowels, there are fourteen Kṣetrapālas.
At a solitary linga he is the syllable Hūṃ; in the terrifying cremation ground he is Bhayāvaha;
and in the dreadful forest he always dwells as Mahālakṣmī and Jvālāmukha.
Viḍālavadana shall dwell under a single banyan tree;
Ghaṇṭārāva in a cave-dwelling; and Jalāmbara in a cluster of lotuses.
At Saṅgama is Bhūridhāraugha; likewise at Parvata is Meru;
at Nirjhara is Śravaṇipravāha; and at Nidhāna is Maṇibhadraka.
One should know that he is the Lord of Wealth in the field of mercury, a jackal in sacrificial enclosures,
Śavala in the forest, and is remembered as Madhukara in the garden.
The sixty-four Mahāvīryas remain protecting the world;
one should always offer oblations and worship in that field at all times.
There, four types of beings—the twice-born and others—accept offerings:
the earth, the sky, the trees, and the birds, each desiring the offering from its own respective domain.
Those four who hold eternal authority are the Kravyādas;
the other people are the barbarians, with tawny hair, tawny eyebrows, and tawny eyes.
With fangs formidable and exceedingly fierce, blazing with ornaments of skulls,
[they are adorned] with saffron, camphor, sandalwood, musk, jasmine, fish, and *phalguṣa* flowers.
With flowers, garments, parasols, lamps, and incense of guggulu,
[the rite is performed] by those of purified soul who are devoted to the supreme sequential worship.
Always gratified by the sounding of bells, musical instruments, songs, and so forth, she is the granter of all desires.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ! Descend upon [Name], O Kṣetrapāla with a mass of tawny matted hair, radiant one, three-eyed, flame-faced!
Accept this offering of fragrance, flowers, and the bali-oblation! In the form of Bhairava, *turu muru kha la phreṃ phreṃ phaṭ*! To the Lord of the Great Ḍāmara, svāhā!
By the offering of oblations to all according to the rule with this mantra,
there shall be no famine there, nor any fear from calamities and the like.
A king who is always joyful shall become beloved by all;
he obtains his desired objects and is ever victorious in battle.
Thus concludes the bali offering for the field beginning with Ajarā.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃḥ Oṃ. O Goddess who resides in the city of Kāmarūpa, whose color is like that of a dark cloud, who has attained the vast seat of Jāra, who dwells in the center of the hexagon within Jayantī, and who moves along the three paths as the goddess of the triangle (śṛṅgāṭaka)!

Accompanied by the hosts of Ācāryas and Siddhas, and joined by the groups of sixty Yoginīs who have entered into accordance with them, I— along with the five [letters] beginning with *ḍa*, *ra*, *la*, and *ka*, and Sahajā— bow to the Goddess of the God of Gods.
Whether on earth, in heaven, or in the intermediate space; in the world of the ten directions, at the root of the seven netherworlds (pātālas);

in a sacred field (kṣetra), a seat (pīṭha), a secondary seat (upapīṭha), a formidable crossroads, or a meeting place (melaka); in a cremation ground; by the bank of a river, under a solitary tree, on the auspicious shore of the ocean, or at the descent of Dhūmakāra—[therein one should practice].
In Kolarya, in Pūrṇagiri, and also in the preeminent Oḍḍiyāna at Purabala;
In the city of Kulapati known as Jāla, the foremost of yogic seats; in Kāmarūpa, which is one's own true nature (svarūpa);
in Ujjayinī, Aṭṭahāsa, Paṭupaṭaha, and the region of Velāḍa;
on Śrīśaila, Pālijāṭa, the abode of Paśupati, and the golden Vindhya mountains—
In the illustrious land of Mokāvaḍa, on Mount Marutapatha, [reside] the Ḍākinīs and Sākinīs.
In Kashmir, in the land of Candra, in Draviḍa and Malaya, in Brahmavākya,
in Strīrājya, in Hakvaḍoka, in Urasivirajaka, in the Siddhakṣetra of Uhāra,
in Eruḍyā, at Pārijāta, on the peak of the Himagiri, in the land of Kāñcī, and at Prayāga.
In Saurāṣṭra, in the Middle Country, in the city of Bhṛgukaccha, or in Kośala or Kāmbuka;

In Karṇāṭa or Koṅkaṇa, in the preeminent city of Magadha, in Karṇakubja, Ekaliṅga, Vacho, Haṃsavāha, Himaraja-paṭala, Ḍoṅgara, and the place called Ḍoṅgaraka; in Agni, O Mother, in the Cakra of Mothers, in the abode of the hosts of sages, in Ḍohala, and in Candradeśa.
Or in a mountain cave deep as a pit, known as Puṣparā, which is filled with the roar of lions.
In the place called Vaṅga, in Bhīmanāda, in the city of Śivapura, at Bhadrakūla, in Jayā, on the shore of the preeminent mountain known as Śrīvidyā, at Yakṣakuṃbha, and at Laṅkā;
in Vārāṇasī, at Viśāla, at Tripatha, at Munipatha, and at Śuddhakūlamārga.
Whether at the edge of the Mlecchas, in the Mleccha-mālā, in a cave of the Malaya mountains, in the land of Brahmā, or in a city;

May all those Mothers— praised by various wise ones— who reside in the locations known as Bhadrāṅga, Mūlasthāna, Prakṛtipurālīya, Siṃhakarṇa, Śaśāṅka, Triśotra, Vyomamadhye, Suravaraśayana, and Gahvara, along with the Yoginī Maṇḍajā, be well-pleased.
May the Siddhas and Susiddhas, praised by various wise ones, grant divine accomplishment.

The sword, or the accomplishment of mantra, entry into the supreme city, flight through the sky, the ointment (rocanā), the paralyzing of enemies, victory over the strength and graying hair of foes, the immobilization of all sciences,
long life, poetic genius, the treasure, the elixir, the pill, the sandals, and the accomplishment of desires.
May all these, who delight in wine and meat and are devoted to Bhairava, grant [these things].

May she who is meditated upon— she who utters "Vauṃ Chauṃ Phreṃ" and laughs with "Ha Ha Ha Ha Ha," chewing and drinking [the enemy]— destroy fear in the presence of wicked men, thieves, enemies, death, hosts of malevolent planets, the fall of thunderbolts, in battle, at the king's gate, or amidst a flood of water; she who is Carcika, the one with the skin and the shaven head.
The Mother of Mantra dances, uttering "kili kilita kili" while speaking in the Kaula tongue.
She is withered, possessing a form at will, with the sounds of *la-ra-va-pa*, *hā hā ha hūṃ*;
she is risen, blue-throated, immortal, with a heart-friend, and is praised as the drop (*bindu*) upon the crown of the head.
Phreṃ phreṃ, uttering the sound *phret*, devouring flesh with a roar of blood while full of wrath; licking the tip of her tongue, *la la la la la*, she causes the creeper to melt as she drinks.
Kṛṣṇā, the messenger of Kāmā, praised by the virtues of the immortals, she is merged within the *bindu* and the end of *nāda*.
O you who grant success, you who have attained the supreme state, may you increase my limbs and my inner strength.
The bold guardians of the world, joined with fire and wind, followed by the king (the letter *na*),
with the sixth vowel (*ū*) and the bindu— this one called Kuṇḍalā, who crosses the creeper of the lotus-clan,
renowned as Rudra-śakti, the terrifying Bhadrakālī, may she grant auspiciousness.

May she who is Kām, Kīm, and Kūm, who takes any form at will, who has entered both the Akula and Kula lineages, and who devours those who harbor hatred— may that venerable Kubjikā, known as Cāmuṇḍā, the Kaulinī of the Kula lineage within the Kaula path, bestow upon you the supreme, divine, and unfailing Vāma-knowledge. May she who resides in Koṅkaṇa grant this during the observance of the Kulakrama.
Mālinī, whose abode is revealed in the Left-hand Path (vāmamārga), whose body is the Bindu, and who consists of both Akula and Kula, has entered the circle of yogis within the Oṃkāra-maṇḍala;
she is known as the one seated on the lap of Śrīnātha, praised by the assembly of eminent sages, and possesses a formidable form.
That Goddess, the Mother of the World, whose face is the entirety of Śiva, resides in the circle of the venerable Lord Nātha.

Worshipped by Śrīkaṇṭha, accompanied by the four yugas, known as Ambikā in the central liṅga, established upon the sacred seat (pīṭha), filling [the universe] with her shimmering arts, her splendor arisen from the Kaula path— she who is named the illustrious Kubjikā, possessing the course of the triple-path, consisting of three syllables, and manifesting in three modes.
I bow with devotion to that Goddess, who has manifested her abode and is differentiated by the five [categories] from beginning to end.

May the Mother Kubjikāmbā— Kālī, whose form is a skeleton, who utters the sound from the soles of her feet, the terrifying one who devours the sacrificial offering— reveal the great, divine, and unfailing stream of primordial wisdom.

Hrīṃ glūṃ hrīṃ slūṃ hrīṃ plūṃ hrīṃ mlūṃ hrīṃ nlūṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ! Grant me prosperity (*ṛddhi*), grant me accomplishment (*siddhi*), grant me knowledge (*jñāna*), grant me long life (*āyus*), grant me wealth (*dhana*), grant me grain (*dhānya*), grant me fortune (*lakṣmī*). Accept this great offering (*mahābali*) rich in nectar; *svāhā*. [Thus ends the Mahābali.]
[Completed] ||
Three handfuls of water offered with joined palms.
KH PHREṂ! To the one seated upon the great corpse-throne, the sandals!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, salutation to the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī; I worship the sandals.
The six-limbed [practice].
Khphreṃ, homage to the heart. Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head. Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Khphreṃ, for the armor, hūṃ. Khphreṃ, for the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Khphreṃ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
[Offer] the invocation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers; [say] "Namaḥ"; [then] one should display the yoni-mudrā.
O you who possess the splendor of nirvāṇa, O you of great strength!
Aiṁ kṣāṁ kṣīṁ kṣūṁ kṣaḥ, accept this offering for the Kṣetrapāla; svāhā!
Aiṁ Śrīṁ Hrīṁ! O Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha, accept this offering; svāhā!
Aiṁ gāṁ gīṁ gūṁ gaḥ glauṁ! O Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara, accept this offering; svāhā!
Aiṃ Hūṃ! To the Great Hero, Lord of the cremation ground, accept this offering, svāhā!
Aiṁ Hskhphrīṁ! O Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī, accept this bali offering! Svāhā!
Aiṃ! O you who move through the sky, accept this offering from all the divine hosts; svāhā!
Aiṃ! To all beings, to the Piśācas, and to all beloved deities, accept this offering, Svāhā! Thus ends the great Bali-offering for Tvaṣṭṛ.
[Recite] "Oṃ, obeisance! [I offer] the invocation, the installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and flowers. Then, one should display the *yonimudrā*.
The libation.
Homage to the illustrious Nātha! Homage to the illustrious Siddhinātha! Homage again and again to the illustrious Kujeśanātha!
Now follows the worship of the Hero’s Vessel (vīraghaṭapūjā).
Homage to the Guru.
Salutations to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutation to that illustrious Guru.
Aiṃ, salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the gurus who are the Parameṣṭhin.
Homage to the supreme teachers and gurus.
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Aiṃ Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ, to the throbbing heart, namaḥ.
Svāhā to the head, which has a form more terrible than the terrible.
Caṭa pracaṭa, to the crest (śikhā), vauṣaṭ!
Kaha vama kavacāya hūṃ.
Dama ghāṭaya, vaṣaṭ to the three-eyed one!
Destroy the obstacles! O obstacle-destroyer, hūṃ phaṭ! To the weapon, phaṭ!
Thus ends the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
The seat.
The pādukā to Ādhāraśakti; the pādukā to Anantāsana.
The sandals for the one whose seat is the bulbous root; the sandals for the one whose seat is the stalk.
Sandals for the seat of leaves; sandals for the seat of hair.
The sandals for the one seated upon the pericarp; the sandals for the one seated upon the lotus.
For the lion throne, the sandals.
O Triple-God!
The sandals for the human throne; the sandals for the peacock throne.
I offer the sandals for the sake of the seat of the crucible.
Aiṁ Thhsrauṁ, sandals to the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa of Prastaradvīpa.
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals for Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha.
Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ, the sandals to the venerable Lord of the Kula-gaṇas.
This is the bali offering for them.
Salutations for the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers.
One should display the tarjanī-daṇḍa-gaja mudrā.
The Brahmāṇī and others.
The sandals for the one seated upon a swan; the sandals for the one seated upon a bull.
The sandals for the peacock-throne; the sandals for the eagle-throne.
The sandals for the one seated upon a buffalo; the sandals for the one seated upon an elephant.
The sandals for the seat of the preta; the sandals for the lion throne.
Aiṃ Aṃ, the sandals of the goddess Brahmāṇī; Kaṃ, the sandals of the goddess Māheśvarī.
Caṃ, the sandal of the goddess Kaumārī; ṭaṃ, the sandal of the goddess Vaiṣṇavī;
taṃ, the sandal of the goddess Vārāhī; paṃ, the sandal of the goddess Indrāṇī.
And the sandal of the goddess Amuṇḍā; the auspicious sandal of the goddess Mahālakṣmī.
This is the bali offering for them.
Aśitāṅga and so forth.
Hrāṃ, the pādukā for Aśitāṅgabhairava; hrāṃ, the pādukā for Rurubhairava.
Hrāṃ, sandals to Caṇḍabhairava; Hrāṃ, sandals to Krodhabhairava.
Hrāṃ, the sandals to Unmattabhairava; hrāṃ, the sandals to Kapālīśabhairava.
Hrāṃ, the sandals to Bhīṣaṇabhairava; Hrāṃ, the sandals to Saṃhārabhairava.
This is the bali offering for them.
Now, meditation.
In ancient times, while the ocean— the milk sea— was being churned by the gods and the asuras,
the Great Goddess was born there as a divine maiden of enchanting beauty.
The Goddess resembles the juice of lac, possessing a radiance equal to a ruby;
the Goddess has eighteen arms and is adorned with jewel ornaments.
The goddess, possessing a gentle form, has three eyes and is in the bloom of youth;
she holds a sword, a trident, a thunderbolt, a ḍiṇḍima drum, and likewise a mallet.
In his right hands, he shines with a mace, a lotus, a boon-granting gesture, and a bowl;
and in his [left] hands, a bell, a goad, a severed head, a khaṭvāṅga staff, and two jars.
Holding a blue lotus and the syllable *Bhaya* along with a drop (*bindu*) in her left hand,
she wears a turban fashioned from divine jewels and is adorned with golden ornaments.
Seated upon a white lotus throne, established in the bound lotus posture—
having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess Vāruṇī of divine form.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Aghora: Aiṃ Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hreṃ Jūṃ Saḥ Hroṃ, Rudrarūpe Hraḥ—[I worship] the sandals.
Vajra! Aiṃ aiṃ Vajrakubjinī! Hsphreṃ, you who attract the three worlds! Hrīṃ, you who melt the limbs of desire!
Klīṃ strīṃ, you who cause great agitation! Aiṃ soṃ saḥ, [I worship] the venerable sandals.

The three Vātīśīs: Aiṃ! Salutations to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ! To Kubjikā, Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O She Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi Vicce! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ! O Blessed One, Siddhe, Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ Kubjike, Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ Khage, Aiṃ Ghore Aghorāmukhī Kiṇi Vicce, [I worship] the sandals.
This is the offering for them.
Three handfuls of water.
Aiṁ Hskṣmlvryūṁ Śkṣmlvryīṁ, [I offer] the sandals to the form of Kulakumbha.
It consists of six limbs.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, to the throbbing heart, salutation!
Svāhā to the head, O you of most terrible form and appearance! Caṭa Pracaṭa, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock!
Kaha vama, for the armor: hūṃ! Dama ghāṭaya, for the three eyes: vaṣaṭ!
Vighāṭaya vighni hūṃ phaṭ! Phaṭ to the weapon! Phaṭ!
The Aghora-weapon mantra.
Aiṁ hrāṁ hrīṁ hrūṁ hraḥ! O you of most terrible and quivering form, flash forth! Move! Move violently! Roar! Vomit! Subdue! Strike! Destroy the obstacles! Hūṁ hūṁ hūṁ phaṭ kroṁ!
O Śrī Mahākaumārikā Vicce, [I worship] the sandals.
This is the bali offering for them.
Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers—obeisance!
One should display the Dhenu-yoni-mudrā.
The worship of the great vessel.
The sandals for the one whose seat is the syllable Aiṃ.
Meditative absorption.
Mounted upon a lotus and a corpse, resembling crystal, five-faced and three-eyed, she deludes the three worlds; her body is draped in divine garments and she possesses ten arms,
holding in her left hands a skull-cup, a trident, a jar, the gesture of granting boons, a great noose, and a severed head.
I bow to Siddhilakṣmī, who holds a bell, a skull-topped staff, a sword, and a goad together with the noose of fear.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
Worship with the Aghora-weapon mantra.

Aiṁ hrāṁ hrīṁ hrūṁ hraḥ! O you of most terrible and quivering form, flash forth! Move! Move violently! Roar! Vomit! Subdue! Strike! Destroy the obstacles! Hūṁ phaṭ kroṁ! O Śrī Mahākaumārikā Vicce, [worship] the sandals!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Glūṁ Hrīṁ Slūṁ Hrīṁ Mlūṁ Hrīṁ Nlūṁ Hrīṁ, salutation to the vessel of supreme nectar; [this is] the *pādukā*.
The Root Vidyā. Three handfuls of offerings (triyāñjali).
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to the venerable Śrī Mahāpātra Bhaṭṭāraka; [the sandals].
The six-limbed [practice].
Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Hrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hreṃ, hūṃ, for the armor! Hroṃ, vaṣaṭ, for the three eyes! Hraḥ, phaṭ, for the weapon!
This is the bali offering for them.
Salutations for the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers.
One should display the Yoni Dhenu Mudrā.
Recitation.
Thrauṃ svāhā || Śrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā || Glūṃ svāhā || Yāṃ svāhā ||
Hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ svāhā || Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ svāhā ||
Hymn of Praise.

The tawny-eyed one with red hair, uttering "kiṇi kiṇi," adorned with a multitude of tinkling bells, having fangs in his mouth and a cruel disposition, yet removing all fear; holding a vessel in hand and making a roar— a clearly manifest lion's roar, "ra ra ra ra," sounding, curly-haired, the very essence of the sky.
I bow to Kṣetrapāla, the lord of spirits, ghosts, and the like, together with the host of planetary deities.
Clad in red garments, with a mass of flaming tawny matted hair,
bearing a staff and blazing with a wreath of flames, he is fierce;
fair as the rising sun and the peaks of gold and refined gold.
I bow to Vaṭukanātha, the son of Gaurī.
O destroyer of the suffering of the six realms of existence, who brings an end to all obstacles;
Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaiṃ! O you whose movement reaches the sky, the perfection that grants all aims!
Oṃ Glūṃ! O you known as the Elephant Mudrā, who move with the wind of the breath, O sole vehicle of the rat, O tusked one!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ gāṃ! O Gaṇeśa, the elephant-faced member of the Gaṇas, Lord of Obstacles, homage to you!
She is Icchā, Jñānā, and Kriyā; she is saluted by the best of the Asuras; she is known as Śrī and Maṅgalā;
she is Gaurī and Durgā, O Blessed One, the bestower of auspiciousness; she is the Mātṛkās and Carmamuṇḍā; she is Brahmā and Viṣṇu; she is the entire host of planets, Bhairavī, and Kṣetrapāla.
I bow to you, the Yoginī, who possesses manifold forms and various great mercies.
The Goddess resembles the juice of lac, radiant with the crimson glow of vermilion;
she possesses eighteen arms and is strewn with weapons and adorned with ornaments.
Just as the substance of nectar emerged from the churning of the ocean of milk,
so too did the Goddess arise— she who deludes the world, and who effects both creation and maintenance.
May the Sovereign Lady Kādambarī protect [us], she who was created by the Goddess of the Gods, who shatters the pride of enemies, and who, having severed fear, bestows prosperity.
This mantra, ending with the letter *va*, having *ha* as its moving essence, situated in time (*kāla*), established in the wind (*vāyu*),

accompanied by its own nasalization (*anusvāra*), pervading the three worlds, and well-known as Tumburu— by writing this mantra, even an old man will not suffer from disease; let the city-dwellers proceed to the city free from ailment.
Holding a flawless water-pot in one hand and a battle-axe in the other,
she who is the embodiment of the Kula, the treasure-house of mantras, vibrates according to her own will.
May all this— the offering of perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and the sacred thread, as well as the entire procedure of worship— be completely fulfilled.
Thus ends the worship of the Vīra-Mahāpātra.
One should offer the periodic *pratibali* consisting of flattened *māṣa* beans, fish entrails, and pieces of fish.
Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers—obeisance!
One should display the secret mudrā of Khecarī, which is the source.
The libation.
Homage to Śrīnātha! Homage to Śrīsiddhinātha! Homage again and again to Śrīkujeśanātha!
The Bell Offering.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ hūṃ, O Mother of the Mantra of the World-Sound, svāhā!
The arrangement of incense and lamps.
Then, the incense.
Having sprinkled the incense burner with the mantra "phaṭ," [one should offer] incense such as guggulu mixed with clarified butter, along with perfumes and so forth.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! Produced from the essence of the lord of herbs, rich in fragrance, the most excellent scent, worthy of being smelled by all the gods—may this incense be accepted.
Endowed with divine fragrance, beloved by all the gods,
and worthy of being smelled by all the gods— may this incense be accepted.
O Blessed One, O Maheśvarī of universal form, among those who consume incense,
may the Supreme Goddess, the Mistress of the Gods, be pleased by this incense.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the Blessed Lady, together with her limbs, her retinue, her vehicle, and her weapons—this incense is for the Blessed Lady; obeisance!
Then, the lamp.
Having purified the lamp-vessel with "hūṃ phaṭ," [one should proceed].
Well-illuminated, of great splendor, dispelling darkness everywhere,
this lamp— a light both external and internal— be accepted.
The Ārātrika rite: To the entire circle, *hrīṃ śrīṃ*, obeisance to this lamp for the Blessed Lady together with her limbs (*sāṅgā*).
To the left of the Goddess, on her own right side, for the purpose of the practice of Mohanī.
Having abandoned all with its bindu.
Having drawn a triangle with five dots within a circle on a deluding vessel.
Hsraiṁ śklhrīṁ hsauṁ—one should place [the lamp] upon the lamp-stand.
Khphreṃ. We know Siddhilakṣmī; we meditate upon Kālikā; may that Śaṃkarṣaṇī inspire us.
[This is] the worship with sandalwood and other offerings.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, salutation to Tripurā, whose seat is all mantras.
Aiṁ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ. The sandal of the venerable Oṣadhīkramabhaṭṭārikā. [Bali.]
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to the sandals! Bali!
The six-limbed [practice].
Khphreṃ, homage to the heart. Khphreṃ, svāhā to the head. Khphreṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
KHPHREṂ kavacāya hūṃ || KHPHREṂ netratrayāya vaṣaṭ || KHPHREṂ astrāya phaṭ ||
[Recite] "Oṃ, salutations! [This is for] the invocation, the installation, the sandalwood paste, the unbroken rice grains, and the flowers. Then, one should display the yoni-mudrā.
Then the food offering (naivedya).
Just as there are sweet substances such as milk-rice (pāyasa) and other cooked foods prepared from various ingredients. HŪṂ PHAṬ!
Sprinkling with water from the *argha* vessel: *vauṣaṭ*. Looking [at it]: *hūṃ*. Concealing [it] with the *avaguṇṭhana* mudrā: *hūṃ*.
One should worship with "namas."
yāṃ yāṃ yāṃ yāṃ rāṃ rāṃ rāṃ rāṃ lāṃ lāṃ lāṃ lāṃ vāṃ vāṃ vāṃ vāṃ ||
Having purified the food offering with these four seed-syllables, having rendered it nectar-like by means of the *dhenu-mudrā*,
and having consecrated it three times with the nine-syllable mantra, one should illuminate the sacrificial materials.
This fourfold food, endowed with the six flavors, has been offered by me to you; please accept it, O Supreme Goddess.
O Supreme Goddess, please accept this divine food of great flavor, endowed with the six tastes, which has been offered by me with devotion.
O Goddess, please accept this food offering; make my devotion unwavering.
O Goddess, it removes untimely death and grants the supreme goal in the hereafter.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, to the Blessed Lady together with her limbs and attendants, and so forth: this food offering, salutation!
At the conclusion of the food offering, [present] water for sipping again to the Blessed Lady together with her limbs: "Obeisance to the Blessed Lady together with her limbs."
In that regard, [there is] the fruit and so forth.
O Supreme Goddess, please accept this plantain, pomegranate, orange, and other fruits offered by me to you.
Then, the betel.
May this betel leaf, consisting of areca nut, betel leaf, camphor and other ingredients,
combined with cardamom and cloves, be accepted.
O Destroyer of the Cities, this betel leaf— resembling a spotless golden plate, filled with pearls and lime,
and provided with all the ingredients of jasmine petals, cloves, areca nut, and an abundance of camphor—
is offered by me to you; please accept it.
O Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, bestower of boons, who brings delight to the mouth, accept [this offering]; homage to you!
Japa: To the three deities of Lāhātana.
Thrauṃ svāhā || Śrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā || Glūṃ svāhā ||
Garland Worship.
Then, having again placed guggulu and other substances into the incense burner, [one should proceed].
Khphreṃ: having fumigated the prayer beads with incense, Hūṃ Phaṭ purifies them.
Khphreṃ, having thoroughly fumigated.
Having worshipped with sandalwood paste, vermilion, flowers, and unbroken rice grains.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ! O Māra, O Mahāmāyā, be gracious; grant me success! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
aiṃ aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ ||
kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaḥ ||
kṣaṃ haṃ saṃ ṣaṃ śaṃ vaṃ laṃ raṃ yaṃ maṃ bhaṃ baṃ phaṃ paṃ naṃ dhaṃ daṃ thaṃ taṃ ṇaṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭaṃ ñaṃ jhaṃ jaṃ chaṃ caṃ ṅaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ khaṃ kaṃ ||
Aḥ aṃ auṃ oṃ aiṃ eṃ ḷiṃ ḷṃ ṝṃ ṛṃ ūṃ uṃ īṃ iṃ āṃ aṃ. One should recollect [them] with the *lomavimoma* [mantra].
The garland has three dots; it goes to Candanādi.
Aiṁ Ḍmlvryūṁ Hrīṁ: the sandals upon the rosary.
Oṃ, O garland, O garland, O great garland, whose nature is all powers!
The fourfold aims of life have been entrusted to you; therefore, be the bestower of spiritual accomplishments.
Thus concludes the worship of the garland.
With the western [mudrā]: HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ SVĀHĀ.
Tumbeśvarīyā || HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ SVĀHĀ ||
At the crest-lock.
Hsphrāṃ hsphrīṃ hsphrūṃ, svāhā to the self-willed Great Bhairava of the crest-lock!
To Mahākāla: Oṃ hūṃ maṃ mahākālāya svāhā.
To Ugracaṇḍā: Hsphreṃ Svāhā! To Ugracaṇḍī: Hskhphreṃ Svāhā!
Siddhilakṣmīyā: Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ svāhā. Kāliyā: Oṃ phreṃ siddhikarāli hrīṃ chrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ phreṃ namaḥ svāhā.
By Tripurā: Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ Svāhā. By Nirvāṇā: Phakva.
O you who are the secret beyond secrets, the protectress, accept this recitation performed by us;
may accomplishment be mine through your grace, which resides within you.
Having recited this, one should offer unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) together with flowers into the right hand of the Goddess while reciting her mantra:
"Accept this recitation, svāhā!"
For the purpose of praise; in the giver of the mandala.
What is the fivefold salutation? It is the ringing of the bell: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃḥ.
Salutations to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded.
To Śrī Mahābhairava. The Illustrious Goddess said:
Within the mandala of Śrī Saṃvarta, the power (śakti) that bestows bliss through the sequential steps is most formidable;
it consists of the fourfold logic of emanation, the fivefold [group] residing in both Akula and Kula,
another sixfold [group], four, another fivefold, and again four— the sixteen-fold initiation of command (ājñā).
Among the eight forms of the Goddess, the one consisting of *ha-sa-kha-pha* with the *kalā* and *bindu* is the mudrā known as Puṣpa.
The supreme Śiva-kalā, Vakradevī, who is another sequence [of power], [presides over] the aged, the youthful, and the child;
she is the essence within the division of the Couple (yugmabheda) in Cakrapurī, where Śrīnātha is ever-newly manifested.
Having established his authority in Koṅkaṇa during the first Kali age, he is the descent of the Siddhas who has brought about the state of perfection.
Among their sons and disciples, within nine generations, eight [attained] the state of immortality.

Having worshipped the lineage, the collection of the *gotra*, the entire ancestral succession ending with the sixteen, the sequence ending with the sixteenth, the pure assembly of true existences, beginning with the upper mandala and so forth, by means of the surrounding offerings;

The state of Ādhāra, however, is peaceful; it is the entirety of the Kula lineage, preceded by the location of the mandala, the purification, the three stars, the single eye, the drop that causes fear in the ignorant, and the attainment of perfection in the fire of Śiva.
In the center is the ground of rest; to that excellent Guru Bhairava, the venerable Kujeśa—who possesses power, majesty, and conviction, and by whom his own office is integrated—I bow.

Aiṁ: That power known as Bhaga, possessing the course of the triple path, the letter *da*, the night, and the letter *ka*—Aiṁ! In her [abode], Śrī Oḍiyāna, situated in the center, conjoined with Parakalā and brilliantly radiant;
Hrīṁ Taśrīṁ! In the southern corner, in the manifest abode called Jālandhara.
On the left is Śrī Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha, which causes fear to the fettered beings; by whom the entire universe is worshipped.
Hsphreṁ: in front of that is Kāmarūpa, joined with Madanakalī and the abode of all siddhas; hsauṁ: at the end of the triangle is the entire Yogabindu, adorned with the digit of Paramaśiva.

In the center of that [ground] is the divine liṅga, a portion of Paramaśiva, in the form of the Bindu, in the form of the letter Kha, Klīm, whose nature is eternal bliss; above that is the churning, divided into six modes.
Glūṃ: Beyond the enjoyment of worldly knowledge, the mantra is stainless in both aspects; at the forehead on the Tisra-pīṭha is Aiṃ.
Thus, the entire universe is pervaded by the energy of Rudra, the mother of maintenance and dissolution, who exists in three divisions.

Aiṃ! Residing there is the Goddess of gods, the sustainer of bliss consisting of both Akula and Kula; she is the essence of the Guru’s command and the Bindu, the remover of fear for bound souls, the goddess of accomplishments, and the embodiment of the lineage of goddesses.

I bow to the one named Śrī Kubjikā, whose body is beautiful, who is eternally moist and deeply red, who bestows the bliss of the state of joy in the bhaga, and who is renowned as she who fulfills all desires upon the earth.
Aiṃ: the *santāna* lineage by way of the Meru path; therein the deity is the exit (*nirgama*). Oṃ: the *pīṭha*; the *siddhānvaya* is proclaimed.
One who has become silent, a dweller in a cave, and a *kadambaka* tree—these are said to be frequented by Śaṅkhinī; and Ambā is the dweller in the cave.
The house is said to be the city, and their distinction is Manthānabhairava.
One should visualize the goddess Gotrāmarikā on the left-hand path.
The lineage, the causal condition, the movement, and the authority reside in Trikoṇaka; birth is in the place of Brahmaśilā, and stability is in Śrīkāmarūpaka.
Fame is found in the Kiñcinki tree, and indeed accomplishment is found in the ocean;
O Goddess of Gods, I am pleased with him who knows the Kula lineage.

O auspicious lady, one should perform the placement (nyāsa) according to the division of the sixteen supports (ādhāras), as well as the ritual of the kuśa grass and the sequence; when thus worshipped, it bestows accomplishment, and one should present it to a worthy disciple.
Oṃ, salutations to you, O Mahāmāyā, whose body is subtle, both supreme and non-supreme;
who are solitary, the abode of the universe, known as Nāda, and garlanded with Bindus.
O Mahākuṇḍalī, who has arisen from the essence of the body, who is immovable and the sustainer of the universe, you are eternally established in the midst of the Haṃsa.
She who dwells in the midst of the moon, sun, and fire; she who pervades the void, both supreme and non-supreme;
she who abides in the form of the syllable Om; she who holds the half of the half of the letter Ha.
Within that which is subtler than a hundredth part of a hair-tip, infinite, inexhaustible, and imperishable;
resting upon the filament of the lotus, which is the support of the energy (kalā) of the half-moon of the letter *Ha*.
O Great Māyā named Sakalā, granter of boons, worshipped by the world;
you who abide within each individual channel and pierce each individual vital point.
The goddess of thirty-eight digits resides in the parting of the hair at the aperture of Brahma;
she resembles a flash of lightning and has the coiled form of a serpent.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
these five great pretas are stationed at the soles of his feet.
O Goddess, mother of the three worlds, salutations to you who are the embodiment of Śakti;
you reside between the Iḍā and Piṅgalā nerves, having the form of a lotus fiber.
The Goddess, who resides in the center of the Bindu, is Kuṭilā and Ardhacaṇḍikā;
she has the luster of a drop of frost and hangs from the End of the Twelve.
Gaurī resides in the heart called Umā, possessing the splendor of twelve suns;
she dwells within the void in the void, known as Haṃsā, the sustainer of the vital breath.
In the one called Lamba, the supreme goddess moves from south to north;
having emerged at the tip of the nose, she flows along the central channel.
O Hṛllekhā, supreme bliss, established upon the crown of the head,
rubbed by the bell of the Nāda, and endowed with the eight qualities.
In the gross and the subtle, when not agitated, within the two-fold sheaths of dharma and adharma,
in the state of cause, effect, and agency, [resides] the threefold void whose form is Nāda.
In that consciousness which is supreme among the supreme, pure, eternal, and firm,
resides the Goddess who bears all colors and is renowned as the Secret Reality (Guhyatattva).
In the great array rooted in power, endowed with the bindu and the seed-syllable,
bodiless and highly fortunate, you are the one who carries one across the ocean of saṃsāra.
O Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, and Parājitā;
O Tumburu, you who abide in the midst of the seed-syllable, homage to you, the liberator from sin!
The Goddess, who effects bondage and liberation, is established at the end of the sixteen;
she is the one who causes wandering by means of the spear of power, endowed with the great array.
Brahmāṇī, Bhrāmaṇī, Gaurī, Māyā, Yantrapravāhiṇī,
the goddess Svacchandabhairavī, Krodhabhairavī, and Unmattabhairavī.
O Rudrā, you who abide in the form of fifty phonemes have been proclaimed by you;
O Amṛtā, Ruru, Caṇḍā, salutations to you, Jñānabhairavī!
O you with fierce fangs, lightning-tongue, starry eyes, and terrifying face; I bow to you, O Goddess of the lords of gods, Aghorā of terrible prowess,
Jvālāmukhī, Vegavatī, Umādevī, and Sarasvatī.
And the Yoginī Śrīyādevī, Gaurī, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī; the goddess Haṃsā, Svarordhvagā, Gomukhī, and Śaktimālinī;
Kroṣṭukī, Subhagādevī, Durgā, and likewise Kātyāyanī.
The one known as Nityaklinnā, Raktā, Ekākṣarā, and the supreme Parā;
likewise Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, and Vaiṣṇavī.
You are Vārāhī, Māhendrī, and Cāmuṇḍā with a terrifying countenance;
you are indeed Yogeśī, O Goddess of gods, adorned by the eight families (kulāṣṭaka).
The Goddess who upholds the eight groups of eight is Lakṣmī, the illustrious one of manifold forms;
she is indeed Aindrī, Āgneyī, Yāmyā, Nairṛtyā, and Vāruṇī.
In the northwest, the north, and the northeast, they are likewise proclaimed;
[the tīrthas] Prayāga, Varuṇā, Kolā, Aṭṭahāsā, and Jayantikā.
To Caritrā, Kāmrakā, and Devīkoṭāṣṭakā;
likewise to Kālī, Umādevī, and Devadūtī—salutations to you!
O Bhadrakālī, Great Goddess, bearer of hide and skull, terrifying one!
O you who are both vast and subtle, O Great Peaceful One; salutations to you, whose form is Śakti.
"O Great Illusion, at the end of the *svāhā* following *bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, grant me [the vision of] Dayānātha; I, seeking knowledge, desire to know this."
The person who recites this hymn at the three junctions of the day attains their desired wishes and becomes beloved by women.
[Thus ends the hymn to Mahāmāyā on the state of the essential identity of Śiva and Śakti.]

The tawny-eyed one with red hair, uttering "kiṇi kiṇi," adorned with a multitude of tinkling bells, having fangs in his mouth and a cruel disposition, yet removing all fear; holding a vessel in his hand and making a roar— a clearly manifest lion's roar, "ra ra ra ra," sounding like a wild beast, the very essence of the sky.
I bow to Kṣetrapāla, the lord of spirits, ghosts, and the like, together with the host of planetary deities.
Clad in red garments, with a mass of flaming tawny matted hair,
bearing a staff and blazing with garlands of fire, he is fierce;
as white as the rising sun and like the peak of a golden mountain.
I bow to Vaṭukanātha, the son of Gaurī.

O destroyer of the suffering of the enemy’s lineage, who has stilled the fear of existence, whose body is the end of all obstacles, Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaiṃ! O you who move through the sky with the six limbs, O Siddhi, giver of all aims!
Oṃ Glūṃ! O Mudrā, known as the Elephant, O you who move with the wind of the breath, O sole seer of the mouse-vehicle!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ gāṃ! O Gaṇeśa, the lord of obstacles with the face of an elephant, salutations to you!
The Brahmāṇīya [is recited].

One should conquer Brahmāṇī at the base of the petal in the direction of Indra (the East); she is mounted upon a swan, resembles molten gold, has four faces and three eyes, and holds in the tips of her hands a *brahmakūrca* vessel, a water-pot with a shining staff, and a lotus-seed rosary; she is beautifully attired.
I bow to her whose body is variegated with perfumes and other unguents, who bears a heavy mass of excellent matted locks.
Belonging to Maheśvara.
She is Māheśī, holding a skull, a hand-drum, the gesture of fearlessness, a trident,
and a staff topped with a skull in her long, powerful arms; she resembles a dense mass of snow,
sits at the base of the southeast petal, shines with three eyes, and bears a crescent moon upon the tip of her tawny matted locks.
One should worship with perfumes and other offerings until the bull has ascended; having mounted it, he goes forth daily.
Of Kaumāri.

One should worship Kaumārī with perfumes and flowers— she who is rich in youth, possesses a most beautiful face, and has the luster of saffron; she who bears in her right hands the spear, the noose, and the goad, as well as the gesture of fearlessness, and who is intoxicated by wine, large-bodied, and radiant with a pair of wide eyes.
Adorned with all ornaments, she sat at the base of the leaf of the Śikhinī tree, restrained by her vow.
Belonging to Viṣṇu.
In the southwest direction, at the base of the leaf, one should meditate upon Vaiṣṇavī, who has limbs as dark as a water-laden cloud and beautiful hair;
she holds a bell, a conch, a skull, and a discus in her staff-like arms, sits upon the bird Garuḍa,
and is resplendent with a crown made of jewels.
She who, ever intoxicated by the passion of honeyed wine, constantly seeks satisfaction through perfumes and other such pleasures; |||
Of Vārāhī.
I bow to Vārāhī, who holds a shield, a mace, a club, and a plough, whose face is fierce in battle, whose cheeks are rubbed by jeweled earrings shining at the base of her ear-lobes,
who is eternally worshipped by the universe, and who sits upon a formidable boar as fierce as a mountain peak.
One should worship her, whose teeth are most beautiful and whose bodily luster is smoky-grey with smoke, with perfumes and other offerings.
Indrāṇī’s [hymn].

At the base of the petal in the direction of Vāyu, one should visualize Indrāṇī, whose face is adorned with jewels resembling the orb of the moon, whose complexion has the luster of sapphire, and whose eyes reach as far as her ears;
she wears a crown made of gems and holds in her four lotus-hands a bow, a conch, a trident, and an arrow.
One should daily worship her, who is intoxicated, who is seated upon her own elephants, and who is praised by the best of the gods.
To Cāmuṇḍā.
And Cāmuṇḍā, whose face is split by fierce, gaping fangs from her violent laughter, who has three eyes, and who holds a sword, a trident, a skull-cup, and a shield in her lotus-like hands;
she is fleshless, with blood-red eyes, and brings fear to the three worlds at the base of the leaf of the gentle direction.
One should worship Kālī, who is adorned with skeletons, whose hair stands upright, and who dwells in the cremation ground.
Of Mahālakṣmī.

Afterwards, one should worship her who is of wondrous form, with a most beautiful face, possessing the luster of pure gold, holding in her lotus-hands a rosary, the gesture of fearlessness, a lotus, and shining *mātuluṅga* fruits—
she who is rich in auspicious marks and worshipped by the guardians of the three worlds, beginning with Varuṇa.
O Lord, [I see] Lakṣmī at the base of each petal of the directions, her form constrained by the weight of her lofty and full breasts.
All these [are] Brahmāṇī and the others.
Aśitāṅga and so forth.
Homage to Sitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodhīśa, Unmattakapālabhairava,
and the one named Bhīṣaṇa in the midst of Palāśa.
I bow to the Bhairavas, who are known as the Withdrawal.
[The section] beginning with "hetukā" (the causal).
He who is the causal one, the destroyer of the three cities, he whose tongues are fire, vetālas, and the sacrificial flame; he who holds Time and the skull, likewise the one-footed one,
who indeed possesses a terrifying form and a fearsome appearance.
To Ugracaṇḍā.
O Goddess who slew Mahiṣa, O you of great illusion, destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, remover of Raktabīja— I bow down to Ugracaṇḍī.
He was struck with fear.

The king Vaiśvānara makes the disputant mute and acts like a deer; he quiets the mass of the illustrious and makes the angry man equanimous; he turns the wicked into the virtuous and makes the traveler lame with speed.
He causes the proud to shrink and paralyzes all the wicked through the mechanism of your power.
O Śrī Nityā Bagalāmukhī, O auspicious one, salutations to you every day!
By means of the three powers.
Red, dry, and exceedingly black, possessing the course of the triple-path, the three goddesses are endowed with the three measures;
having praised her own self, those who have attained even the state of slaughter are established in the three classes—
youth, childhood, and old age— and she becomes the savior from existence, awakened in the three times.
May the mother of Veta, the auspicious one who bestows victory, whose womb is full of sweetness, and who is the eternal worship and the limb of Śiva, be victorious.
By Hanubhairava.
I bow to the Supreme Lord Rudra, who has the form of Bhairava;
the God who protects the three worlds, the Master and Sovereign of the Ḍāmaras.
By Nāṭeśvarī.
Repeatedly squeezing and pressing the entire universe between his two hands, as if it were a ripe,
glistening fruit, Trijaṭa drank it in mouthfuls again and again like one intoxicated by its essence.
May Mahābhairava protect us by means of his ritual dance, the grand display of the tāṇḍava.
The fifth [belongs] to Vārāhī.
Homage to you, O Great Illusion, who bears the name Vārāhī;
you who are Kolāsyā, the most fierce one, and the bearer of the adamantine snout.
By Siddheśvarī.
O Maheśānī, she has one face and three eyes, with the crescent moon as her crest-ornament;
she has four arms, two of which are joined in the añjali gesture.
May the goddesses, seated upon corpses, red in color and most brilliantly radiant,
possessing the luster of ten million full moons, blaze forth with their own intense splendor.
Of Chinnamastā.
At the navel is a white lotus, and above it, the stainless orb of the fierce-rayed sun;
for the sake of the arising of Dharma-karma, [one should meditate upon] Chinnamastā, who is praised as the sole essence of saṃsāra and the mother of the three worlds,
possessing a triple body within that center at the junction of the three paths.
I bow to that Yoginī, whose form is wisdom, who removes the fear of death, and who is the mudrā of yoga.
The letter *ū* is the dancing feet; *ha*, *kṣa*, *ma*, *ra*, *va*, *ju*, and *o* are the belly; the fire-linga (*agniliṅga*) is in the northwest;
the nose (*ghrā*), the skin (*añjinā*), the moon (*ākāśaśasī*), and the whole (*sakala*) are the head, joined with the bindu, nāda, and the half-moon;
the water-stream from the Ganges (*nirjiṅgaṅgāmbudhārā*) is the straight supreme digit (*ṛjuparamakalā*); Bhairava is the embodiment of the mantra.
Pāyoddeva, Navātmā, Sakalaguruvare, Bhairava, and Śrīkujeśa.
Brahmāṇī has a face as gentle as a lotus or the moon; Māheśvarī is playful; Kaumārī destroys the pride of enemies; Vaiṣṇavī holds the discus as her weapon;
Vārāhī has a mouth with a deep, terrible gurgling sound; and Aindrī wields the thunderbolt as her weapon.
May Cāmuṇḍā, Gaṇanātha, and the hosts of Bhairavas protect me, O Mother.
In the center, seated upon three thrones, with faces joyful with intoxication, Vajrapadmā is brilliantly radiant;

on the eight petals of the Brahmāṇī and other goddesses, in the directions and intermediate points within the field of the syllable *praṇava*, are the Śrī-prayā and others; joined in the twenty corners, they flash forth at the tips of the vajras with the syllables *va, sa, ṣa, śa, ha, ṣa, kṣa*.
May she who consists of thirty-two syllables—divided into twenty-eight parts, possessing three divisions, and endowed with the sequential steps—protect us.
The sword, the accomplishment of mantras, the ruin of the foremost cities, flight through the sky, or the eye;
the paralyzing of enemies, the subduing of the victory of foes, all branches of knowledge;
long life, poetic talent, the treasure, the elixir, the pill, the sandals, and the accomplishment of desires.
All those who give rise to inconceivable [thoughts], together with the offering of wine (alibali), are joined by Bhairava.

Dark-red in hue, with three eyes, her breasts heavy with weight, she walks with the gait of an elephant in rut; her lips are like the *bimba* fruit, her eyes are beautiful, and her broad hips are adorned with a girdle resplendent with jewels.
Her divine body is beautified by garments, and her mass of hair is curly, dark, and fragrant with flowers.
May she, known as the illustrious Kubjikā, bestow the unfailing, divine flood of the command of aesthetic relish (rasa).
She who resembles the luster of the bandhūka flower, who possesses three eyes, sits upon a lion-throne, and is most beautiful;
she who destroys all enemies here for everyone, is adorned with white garments,
and has eighteen lotus-like hands that are stainless and grant the fruits of one's desires.
I bow to that Ambika, the Mistress of Tumba, the destroyer of the demon Mahishasura.

Where is space, where is the wind, where is fire, where are the waters, where is the earth, where is Brahmā, where is Janārdana, where is the serpent, where is Indra, and where are the gods and asuras?
Delighted by the destruction of the world at the end of the aeon, the illustrious Siddhiyogeśvara alone remains.
Victorious is the Lord Mahābhairava, the hero of the drama of play;
the Lord who has the luster of great black collyrium, [who assumes] the form of Mahākāla and Mahārudra,
possessing a massive body and a large frame, and bearing a curved knife and a skull-cup.
Homage to you, Mahākāla, the three-eyed deity who bears a sword and a flaying-knife, blazing with the splendor of fire, the destroyer and annihilator of enemies.
Mārkaṇḍeya took an incarnation to bestow grace upon those afflicted by calamity; he whose hand was shattered against Brahmā, who was like Brahmā himself,
and whose power was manifested within the hymns of praise from the heads of Daityas rejoicing at their own decapitation.
May this belong to the goddess Caṇḍikā, whose glory is yours.

That Goddess who is the destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, who is the devourer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, who is the primordial one who brought about the destruction of the demon Mahiṣāsura, who takes refuge in the blood-seeded [demon],
she who is the crusher of the Daityas Śumbha and Niśumbha, and she who is the glory of the God of gods.
May that goddess protect me with her right arms, and may Jayā, O Caṇḍī, protect me.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus is Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, the supreme Lakṣmī,
white as camphor, crystal, the moon, and the *kunda* flower; she is the remover of all bonds and the unshakable boat for those drowning in the mire of suffering within the ocean of saṃsāra.
May she who possesses glorious five lotus-faces, ten arms, and stands upon a corpse protect you!
O fulfiller of hopes, remover of sins, destroyer of the flood of the world's suffering, deliverer from afflictions, slayer of enemies, ender of the delusion of worldly existence;
O cause of ultimate welfare, O Primordial Cause, [salutations] to the one who moves through the pain of living beings among the best of gods.
I bow to you, O Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who instantly grants boons and protection from calamities to the gods.
That which abides as a radiant form within the cavity of the fire of destruction, situated in the midst of the three paths of the moon, sun, and fire;
it is consciousness, the mind, the objects of thought, the senses, and the state of the void.
She whose essential nature is the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
Consisting of gnosis, differentiated by the divisions of all phenomena, ever delighted by bliss and absorbed in the ultimate reality—
O you whose body is formed by the digits of the channels, you who are the very form of mantra!
Indeed, the syllable *chidra* consists of seventeen syllables.
O hundred-syllable Vidyā, you who have gone beyond the activities of the Kula; O fierce one, supreme mistress of the three worlds, perfected through union with the Kula;
you who possess both singular and manifold movements, the excellent wheel worthy of highest worship.
O you who are perfected through association with the virtuous and worshipped by Bhairava!
Kālī, whose waves of time are fashioned by her own digit (kalā),
who dwells within the wheels of the Śrīcakra, divided into nine divisions,
she is the Fullness, joined with the Moon, and has the form of the Sun of the Kula.
The excellent accomplishment of consciousness is well-established in the Fire family.
Having attained the state of the sky-farer (khecarī), she is supremely fierce;
the great ocean of ultimate meaning has been declared through the sequence of the wheels (cakras).
Devoted to yoga through the company of the virtuous, she bestows the accomplishment of the Kula.
I bow down to the supreme Kālī, who exists as the very nature of all things.
Bearing the splendor of Indra’s very bow upon her forehead, and spreading the radiance of the syllables *sauṃ* and *klīṃ* everywhere, this Gaurī— who subdues all—
stands ever present like the heat of the sun, possessing the brilliance that destroys the three cities.
Or she, consisting of light and consisting of speech, might suddenly destroy the three cities by her power.
Māyā, Kuṇḍalinī, Kriyā, Madhumatī, Kālī, Kalāmālinī, Mātaṅgī, Vijayā, Jayā, Bhagavatī, Devī, Śivā, Sāmbhavī, Śakti,
the beloved of Śaṃkara, Trinayanī, Vāgvādinī, and Bhairavī.
Hrīṃ! You are Kālī, Tripurā, the Mother whose face is both supreme and non-supreme, and you are Kumārī.
Salutations to you, O Goddess of the lords of gods, Siddhilakṣmī of great splendor;
salutations to you, O Great Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, Rājyalakṣmī.
You are the supreme Kālī; you alone are Siddhilakṣmī.
You are the supreme Caṇḍī; you alone are Ugracaṇḍī.
You are the supreme Rājñī; you are the Queen of the Queens of Kings.
May he, who has utterly destroyed all enemies, grant all spiritual accomplishments.
I speak of nothing else, nor do I hear, nor do I contemplate;
I remember nothing else, nor do I worship, nor do I take refuge in anything other than your lotus feet, which I have now attained with devotion.
Protect me, O Bhūti; out of compassion, grant me spiritual accomplishment.
Just as armor serves as a defense against the strikes of arrows,
even so may peace serve as a defense against all obstacles.

May the guardians of the local fields (kṣetrapālas) of their respective abodes, together with Brahmāṇī and the others, along with the Great Bhairava Aśitāṅga, the Gaṇas, Vaṭukas, Yoginīs, and Kṣetrapālas, together with their limbs, retinues, and attendants,
and the world-protectors such as Indra in the cardinal and intermediate directions, be well-pleased and grant boons.

The consecration of a stone temple and the hoisting of the golden pinnacle and banner upon it, along with the *koṭyāhuti* sacrifice and the establishment of the perfected fire (*siddhāgni*), performed by the patron, Śrī-Śrī-Jayabhūpatīndramalladeva-varman of the Mānava-gotra, for the sake of pleasing his chosen deity (*sveṣṭadevatā*).
In this rite of acceptance (*adhivāsana-karman*), for the purpose of worshipping the sacrificial ground (*thaṇḍila*),

may there be for the patron (*yajamāna*) together with his hosts and retinue— longevity, health, sovereignty, progeny, wealth, prosperity, and the increase of lineage; and may [the deities] become bestowers of fruits as described in the scriptures.
There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge.
Therefore, O Supreme Goddess, protect me, protect me with your compassionate nature.
May all this— the offering of fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, the sacred thread, and worship— be entirely complete according to the prescribed ritual.
The satiating [offering].
Bhairava, who dwells upon the seat of the gratified departed spirits, the remover of the fear of worldly existence, whose form is the mantra;
Caṇḍī, seated upon the fierce throne; the Gaṇas, Gurus, Vaṭukas, and the guardians of the world; the lords of serpents;
the protectors, Yakṣas, excellent holy sites, all the hosts of ancestors, the Mothers, and the Kṣetrapālas.
May the yoginīs, joined in yoga, whether moving in water or moving in the air, drink this beverage.
May all the deities, together with the Rudras and the lords of their hosts, as well as the Yoginīs and the Kṣetrapālas who are established within my body, drink [this]. [The mantras:]
Homage to Śrīnātha! Homage to Śrīsiddhinātha! Homage again and again to Śrīkujeśanātha!
[Thus ends the venerable ritual procedure for the worship of the sacrificial ground.]
For the worship of acceptance.
For the purpose of fasting. [This concludes the ritual procedure for the preliminary consecration.]
